who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older for Discovery Station and Astronomy volunteering. Commit to at least 8 hours a month for one year.
how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' on the volunteer page, create an account in the museum's volunteer system, complete the orientation and online training, and sign a Program Volunteer Agreement.
notes: The Astronomy Education volunteer role (also 16+, at least 4 hours a month for one year) was marked 'not recruiting at the moment'. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: At least 8 hours per month for one year
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 can apply to volunteer. The Teen Advisory Group is for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application online. Go to a Teen Volunteer Orientation. The dates are on the library events page. Use an email that is not from your school. You can write to volunteer@alexlibraryva.org.
notes: The page was last updated in March 2025. Confirm the age range and orientation dates by email. Volunteers cannot lead story times.
duration: No required hours listed
pay_detail: Unpaid. Service hours can be earned.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, in middle or high school, who live in the City of Alexandria. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. Your household must get SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or free or reduced lunch. Or its income must be at or below 130% of the poverty line. Students with an IEP can also qualify.
how_to_apply: Send the Smartsheet youth application one time, with all your papers. You need proof of an Alexandria address, proof you can work, proof of income or benefits, and a photo ID. Some students with benefits need only three papers.
notes: Forms that are not complete, or sent more than once, can slow or hurt your application. Questions: DCHSSummerYouth@alexandriava.gov or 703-746-5940 (4850 Mark Center Drive, Floor 6). The page does not mention work permits.
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to July 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Paid; rate and weekly hours not stated on the program page (a city video page says 20 to 30 hours per week)

who_can_apply: Rising 11th graders, 12th graders and post-secondary students. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Apply during the window; the process includes an interview. The page encourages students to attend a performance and check back next year. Contact: collision.project@alliancetheatre.org or 404-733-4700.
notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.
duration: 3 weeks, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily (June 29 to July 17 in 2026, with performances July 17 and 18)
pay_detail: Free to all participants. No stipend mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 living in Cherokee, Clayton, Douglas, Fayette, Gwinnett, Henry or Rockdale County. In-school or out-of-school youth who face a barrier such as offender history, homelessness, foster care, parenting, disability or being a basic-skills-deficient or English learner diploma holder.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Contact the provider for your county. Clayton: 770-997-4511 (640 Hwy 138 SW, Riverdale). Gwinnett: 404-913-0769 (3805 Crestwood Pkwy NW, Suite 300, Duluth). Cherokee: 770-345-5483. Henry: 404-913-0769. Douglas: 770-997-4511. Fayette: 770-910-7733. Rockdale: 770-991-7608.
notes: This is the only Gwinnett and Clayton county youth workforce program found. The City of Atlanta, Fulton, DeKalb and Cobb are not on this page's county list; see their own entries. Providers named on the page: Cherokee Youth Works and Hearts to Nourish Hope. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either. The page does not mention wages, stipends or work experience pay.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page states no age or residency rule for the teen services.
how_to_apply: Write your resume with the template, then apply for jobs on the Teen Job Board (hosted on Indeed). Book 1-on-1 resume or mock interview sessions through the Microsoft Forms link on the page.
notes: In Virginia, 14 and 15 year olds must have a work permit (Youth Employment Certificate) to work; under 14 cannot get one. The page links the state Department of Labor and Industry portal. The separate Youth Employment Program on the same site is for ages 18 to 24, not teens.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Pay depends on the employer. Services are free.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 entering grades 10 to 12. Must be an Arlington resident.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open in early March. To find the form, search for the name Arlingteens Leaders on the arlingtonva.us site. Look for the one that says teens.
notes: Dates above are from the 2026 flyer; check the page in March for 2027. Contact: 703-228-3329.
duration: Two weeks (July 20 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Lunch is provided on the first and last day.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 by May 1 and at least two years older than the oldest camper at the site. Works at county run camps only.
how_to_apply: Sign up in the county system with a household account. It is a free volunteer activity. Finish the ePACT paperwork. Pick your sessions and camp sites. If you are new, sign up for an interview. Email campvol@arlingtonva.us.
notes: Registration opened Feb 18, 2026 and closed when full. The page gives no 2027 dates yet.
duration: At least 2 consecutive weeks per assignment, no more than 8 hours a day
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to register.

who_can_apply: Arlington County youth ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: The page has no application steps. Email Linh Nghe, Prevention Director, at lnghe@arlingtonva.us to ask about joining.
notes: Ask about service hours or a stipend; the page does not say.
duration: Meets the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month in the school year, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade who live in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link for the institute on the 21st Century Leaders site. Spots are limited and some students go on a waitlist. Acceptance comes by email, so check spam.
notes: Expect applications to open around January again, as they did last year. The same group runs Leadership Connect all year. It is online and self-paced. Seniors who finish 3 levels can get a paid summer internship and a scholarship.
duration: About one week, residential (overnight)
pay_detail: Applying is free. The page says some institutes, including SYLI, may cost to attend, and that financial aid is available. The price is not listed.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). The page gives no 2027 dates yet.
duration: 50 hours between June 2 and July 24 (2026), including a required 6-hour training day. Shifts Tuesday to Sunday in 2-hour blocks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.
duration: 7 weeks (June 2 to July 16 in 2026), 18 hours a week, Tuesday through Thursday
pay_detail: $12 per hour, paid every two weeks.

who_can_apply: Students 15 to 17 in 10th or 11th grade who are doing well in school. Selection uses nominations from schools, ABL members and community partners. A parent must approve the application.
how_to_apply: The student fills out the application linked on the program page. A parent or guardian approves it. Call 404-584-8126 to ask about dates and nominations.
notes: Pay, dates, cost and site locations are not listed, so call to confirm first. Atlanta Business League is at 931 Martin Luther King Jr. Dr. NW. The summer season is from the program name on search results, not the page; confirm.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Summit Trail Apartments are for young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list ages for the drop-in center.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Need Housing Support form on the CHRIS 180 page, or call 404-486-9034 or 1-800-896-4106. The team says it will reach out privately. Main office: 1030 Fayetteville Road, Atlanta.
notes: Support and housing, not a job. Call to ask about ages for the drop-in center, hours and where it is. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. For dual enrollment, you must be on track to graduate and have a 2.0 GPA. Early College Essentials and Cybersecurity need a 2.6 HOPE GPA and grade 11 or 12.
how_to_apply: Take the YouScience career quiz (recommended). Talk to your school counselor. Then submit the online application. Students with an IEP or 504 plan also need a team review.
notes: Career paths include HVAC, Culinary Arts, Dental Science and Patient Care. Atlanta Technical College runs the dual enrollment paths. They include Carpentry and Cybersecurity. The page lists more. You can be denied if there is no room or you miss the minimums.
duration: Part of the school day: morning group 9:15 to 11:30 am, afternoon group 12:30 to 2:45 pm
pay_detail: School program. The page does not mention pay. Dual enrollment is through Atlanta Technical College.

who_can_apply: Volunteers 8 and up at most ongoing projects. Anyone under 18 must come with an adult chaperone who stays the whole shift. Groups need 1 adult for every 4 youth ages 8 to 11 and 1 adult for every 8 youth ages 12 to 17. Adults register for shifts themselves.
how_to_apply: An adult signs up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. Then email volunteers@acfb.org or call 404-419-1727 to add the youth to the registration. Groups of 8 or more fill out a group request form.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Stay for the whole shift. Come on time because late volunteers more than 30 minutes cannot serve. Special events may have other age rules.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 registration cutoff is for. Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.
duration: The 2026 Teen Leaders Summer Academy ran June 8 to July 24, Monday to Friday.
pay_detail: Teen Leader activities are free. Pay for the summer employment program is not stated in the catalog.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at an APS high school that offers the Mentorship and Internship classes. You do not have to be labeled gifted. Your school picks the students.
how_to_apply: There is no separate form on the page. Ask your guidance counselor whether your school offers the class, or call the gifted office at 404-802-7585. The coordinator matches you using a career survey from early fall.
notes: The coordinator matches students to internships after a career survey in early fall. Students and families arrange their own rides. You must finish the fall Mentorship course first.
duration: Fall mentorship class, then a 60-hour one-on-one spring internship that begins in January and concludes with the Capstone Celebration in April. Hours per week and days are not stated.
pay_detail: The page does not say whether you get pay or school credit. It calls Mentorship and Internship classes.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. The district page does not list grade, age or GPA rules, so ask your school counselor or the CTAE office.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Call or email the Work-Based Learning contact, or ask your school counselor.
notes: The phone on the page is (404) 802-5878. The page also lists CTAE career paths. They include Engineering Drafting, Allied Health, Cybersecurity and Culinary Arts. Students in other districts use their own district.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated on the district page. You earn high school credit.

who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.
duration: June 8 to July 16 in 2026 (about 6 weeks). Some positions may extend.
pay_detail: Paid. The page says competitive wages and does not state a rate.

who_can_apply: Young business owners ages 11 to 17. You have a product or service, you have paying customers and you want to grow.
how_to_apply: Click Apply now on the YMB Fuel page. Applications are reviewed, then there is a shortlist and interviews. You must commit to attend.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Your business needs paying customers already. For newer ideas the site lists YMB Spark (early-stage help) but its page was not read. YMB also holds an annual Summit (two days, ages 11 to 17 can register); dates and cost were not on the page. The page says the program takes place live in Atlanta, Georgia, and may have virtual parts.
duration: One week summer intensive
pay_detail: Free to join. Grants are given at Pitch Day; the amounts are not listed.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Libraries prefer a commitment of at least six months for regular volunteers.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch you want. Volunteers are recruited, interviewed and trained at the local branch.
notes: Not every branch recruits teens, so call first. Volunteer jobs can involve lifting boxes of books and standing for a while.
duration: Regular volunteers: at least 6 months preferred. Volunteens: summer program.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25. The city page lists seats by council district. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Contact the liaison, Tyron Rice, trice@baltimorecity.gov, 443-827-8421, to ask about open seats and the application.
notes: Members are appointed by the Mayor. Seats are limited, so ask before applying. Check the commission website for the current application.
duration: Term lasts until December 2028 for current members
pay_detail: Not stated on the city page.

who_can_apply: High school students from Baltimore City. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Complete the Baltimore City YouthWorks application, then the BCLC application linked on the Civic Works page.
notes: The Civic Works page looks out of date (it mentions 2025). Check the page in spring, or use its Contact Us page, before relying on dates.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: Not stated on the Civic Works page. Teens apply through the YouthWorks summer jobs application.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page's teen event filter lists ages 14 to 17. Be Involved is open to any teen at any branch. Teen Advisory Boards and Buddies use applications.
how_to_apply: For Be Involved, check the events calendar and drop in. For Teen Advisory Boards or Buddies, contact your local branch. Questions: yfe@bcpl.net.
notes: Older BCPL announcement pages were not available, so past application windows are not confirmed here.
duration: Be Involved is drop-in. Teen Advisory Board and Buddies dates are not posted on this page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service-learning hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 who work well with kids and teens and are comfortable talking with the public.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application and send it to the Volunteer Coordinator (volunteers@mdsci.org). Expect a placement interview.
notes: The page links two different youth application PDFs, so ask which one is current. Schedule and hours are not posted. Contact: 410-545-5940.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 17. Apply with a portfolio of art or design work.
how_to_apply: Online application (a fee applies), submit work samples, then deposit if accepted. Email precollege@mica.edu with questions.
notes: Prices are the 2026 amounts from MICA's 2026 payment page. The main page does not list tuition amounts. Prices for 2027 are not posted. The main page says to submit 6 pieces of work.
duration: 2 or 4 weeks (2026: about July 12 to Aug 8)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $3,850 for 2 weeks or $7,700 for 4 weeks. Commuter $2,725 for 2 weeks or $5,450 for 4 weeks. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Students about to enter 11th or 12th grade. Recent graduates must plan to study actuarial science at Morgan in the fall. The application is competitive. Students who are considered get a phone interview.
how_to_apply: Apply through the SAAMS program. Some students get a phone interview. Email msusaams@morgan.edu for application updates.
notes: The FAQ says there are no additional costs or fees beyond travel to and from campus for the last week, and it does not say who pays that travel. Phone (443) 885-3964. Check the page for the application window.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: No cost to attend. Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Local high school students who finished 9th grade, are interested in marine biology or environmental science, and can do the full program including the training week and the shifts.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in December. Selected students come to an in-person interview with Aquarium volunteer staff.
notes: Training week is required (2026: June 22 to 26). The page lists both 12 shifts over six weeks and at least 10 shifts across five weeks, so ask which applies. Closing date for 2027 not posted. Students do not work directly with animals except at the Living Seashore exhibit.
duration: About 6 weeks of volunteering after a training week (2026: June 29 to Aug 9)
pay_detail: Unpaid. $40 fee for registration and materials if accepted (need-based scholarships are available).

who_can_apply: Baltimore City high-schoolers, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Branches Fall 2026 application on the Parks & People page. Contact Sophie Poirier, sophie.poirier@parksandpeople.org, 410-448-5663 x108.
notes: Held at 2100 Liberty Heights Avenue, Baltimore. The page also mentions a summer job part. Ask about the summer and spring sessions. The Branches page says applicants must be able to apply for a work permit, must attend all in-person sessions, and that a family orientation is required. The foundation phone is (410) 448-5663 and the email is info@parksandpeople.org.
duration: A fall session, Monday to Thursday 4:30 to 6:30 pm (the 2025 session ran Sep 30 to Dec 18)
pay_detail: Paid. The rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens who live in Baltimore City and are in grades 9 to 12, and can attend the meetings.
how_to_apply: Application on the Pratt Library page when it opens in spring. Not open now.
notes: Meets 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 6:00 to 7:30 pm at the Central Library.
duration: 8 months (November to June)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours. Dinner is provided at meetings.

who_can_apply: Baltimore City teens in grades 6 to 12. Space in each group is limited.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Pratt Library page when a new series opens. Not open now.
notes: Each series has a new theme. The page does not announce the next series.
duration: 4 weekly sessions per group
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in teaching. Applicants are selected.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Towson College of Education page when registration opens, likely in February. Contact Assistant Dean Omari Jackson, 410-704-3877.
notes: The 2026 Towson news notice says the program is free, with free daily lunch. The one-credit course is Exploring Careers in Education.
duration: 4 days, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. (2026: July 13 to 16)
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided each day.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Baltimore City with a strong interest in biology, chemistry, medicine or related fields.
how_to_apply: See the RAMP page for the application process when it reopens. Teens also need a YouthWorks application for pay.
notes: Held on the UMB campus in downtown Baltimore. Scholars earn Stop the Bleed and CPR/AED certifications in summer one.
duration: 2 years: 5 weeks in July and August, about 10 school-year sessions, then a second 5-week summer
pay_detail: Summer parts can be paid through YouthWorks. Up to $500 for the school-year research rotations.

who_can_apply: Middle school and high school students. The page gives no age or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Register online on the UMBC SEA page when 2027 registration opens.
notes: The page lists extendedlearning@umbc.edu as the contact. The original link now redirects to youthprograms.umbc.edu.
duration: 1 week per course
pay_detail: Standard prices range from $374 to $499 depending on the course.

who_can_apply: High school students. Priority goes to Baltimore City residents and Baltimore City Schools students. Some spots are held for Baltimore County students. Others are considered if space is left.
how_to_apply: Register through Wide Angle (registration is required for all students). Email the programs team or sign up for their newsletter for the next registration.
notes: Wide Angle follows the Baltimore City Schools calendar.
duration: Fall 2026 high school classes: Sep 28 to Dec 11 (no classes Thanksgiving week)
pay_detail: High school students who attend at least 50% of classes can get a pro-rated stipend (a W-9 form is needed).

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21. The page does not give a residency rule for this program.
how_to_apply: Contact Wide Angle through their programs page. The details are not listed on the page.
notes: Wide Angle has also been a worksite for Baltimore YouthWorks (a lead, not confirmed here). Ask them how MediaWorks is funded and how to apply.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Described as a paid summer intensive. The rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Baltimore City residents ages 14 to 21 (age counted as of mid-March of the program year). Needs identity and work authorization papers.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the YouthWorks portal and upload ID, work authorization and tax forms. Under 18 also needs a Maryland work permit signed by a parent. Applying early does not guarantee a job.
notes: Pay of $15 and the work permit rule come from the 2026 pages. The 2027 pay is not posted yet. Help desk (410) 545-1820. Credit recovery classes can also be a paid worksite.
duration: About 5 weeks (June 29 to July 30, 2027)
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2026 (up to 5 hours a day, 5 days a week, 25 hours)

who_can_apply: Students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade who may want a future career in healthcare. Download the camp form for the full qualifications and paperwork.
how_to_apply: Download the camp application form from the Carilion news page, then follow its instructions. Contact the camp directors at lmfreeman@carilionclinic.org or krproctor@carilionclinic.org.
notes: The camp is in Roanoke, not Blacksburg. 2027 dates are not posted; check the Carilion camps news page in early 2027.
duration: 4 days (June 16 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page seeks volunteers and student volunteers. It lists no minimum age or youth rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Contact form on the volunteer page. You can also email info@historicsmithfield.org. Or call 540-231-3947.
notes: No age rule is posted, so ask whether teens under 16 or 18 need a parent. Shifts are Wednesday to Saturday daytime for tours and the store.
duration: Museum season April to December; July camp; some roles year-round
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. You need a parent signature and your shot record. You also need a note of support from a teacher, school counselor or an adult who is not family.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application. Send the other forms. They are a disclosure and release form, a signed parent consent form, your shot record and a note of support.
notes: The page also lists a signed disclosure and release form and parental consent form. You must keep your scheduled shifts. Hospital address: 3700 South Main Street, Blacksburg.
duration: 3 to 9 hours a week in the school year. More shifts allowed in summer and school breaks with parent permission.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A free meal in the cafeteria for a 3-hour shift.

who_can_apply: Community and project clubs are for ages 9 through 18. The home school Senior club is ages 14 to 19. Clubs have size limits and fill first come, first served, and they depend on volunteer leaders.
how_to_apply: Email one of the Extension 4-H staff on the page. They are Kendra Young kkyoung@vt.edu, Lesa Miller lvmiller@vt.edu and Margarita Palomino mrpalomi@vt.edu. Or call the Montgomery County Extension office at 540-382-5790. Staff pass your request to the club leaders.
notes: The clubs page does not give an age rule or meeting time for the Teens for a Better Tomorrow club, so ask staff. This is a youth club, not a paid job.
duration: Clubs meet 9 to 12 months a year. Home school clubs meet Oct to early May.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the clubs page. Ask the Extension office.

who_can_apply: Selected students from nine public high schools in the partner divisions: Radford City, Giles, Floyd, Pulaski and Montgomery County public schools.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor or gifted resource teacher, tell your parents, line up two teacher recommenders, get your transcript, then fill out the NRVGSAH Application Packet.
notes: School districts arrange transportation to Radford. Choose from visual arts, dance, theatre, music, design, history, politics and philosophy. The program is new.
duration: Three hours each weekday morning during the school year
pay_detail: Page says students earn nearly two years of college credit at no cost to the family.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors from Virginia or other states. It is not just for girls. Any student who is interested can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a typed essay of 400 words about why you like science, math or IT. Get one letter from a counselor, teacher or adult leader. Contact David Horton, rhorton@radford.edu, or 540-831-5958.
notes: Radford is about 15 miles from Blacksburg. Families get students to and from campus. You share a room with one other student.
duration: One week, residential (dates not shown on the page)
pay_detail: $1,600 covers tuition, room and board. Competitive scholarships can cover the full cost, and earlier applicants are more likely to get one.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age range is given.
how_to_apply: Online application form linked on the camp website. Email info@same-vatech-stemcamp.org to check the 2027 dates.
notes: Site says the camp is a day camp at Virginia Tech and was postponed to Summer 2027. The old July 1 deadline and July dates on the site may be out of date, so confirm with the organizers.
duration: 3 days (July 22 to 24 listed for the postponed 2026 camp)
pay_detail: Cost not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA. The page lists no location rule.
how_to_apply: Register online during the winter window. The page gave no apply link when read, so use the contact on the page: Louann Morrow, lomorrow@vcom.edu.
notes: Next-cycle dates are not posted; expect a similar early-year window. Camp has a strict dress code (closed-toe shoes, no shorts or hats) and no phones in the anatomy lab.
duration: One week (two sessions in 2026: weeks of June 21 and July 5)
pay_detail: Free. Meals, lodging and activities are included. No pay.

who_can_apply: Enrolled senior 4-H members in Virginia. The page says the event is for 4-H youth ages 14 to 18. You must be signed up as a member through 4-H Online.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H first. Your county 4-H office can help. Then register through your family profile in 4-H Online. Your county 4-H agent handles unit delegations.
notes: You must already be a 4-H member. Part of the page still shows last year's details, so check the newest page. Statewide event that happens to be in Blacksburg, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card.
duration: 4 days (2026: June 16 to 19)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $310 for full time registration, $70 for the one-day competition. Each unit gets one first-time delegate scholarship for half the cost ($155).

who_can_apply: Anyone who lives in Montgomery County can join. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must come to every activity. They must also fill out a sign up form. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer sign up form linked on the FAQ page. Call 540-382-5775 or email hayesaw@montgomerycountyva.gov. Hours are Mon to Fri, 8:30 to 5.
notes: Teens need an adult with them, so it works best for families or a parent who volunteers too. A volunteer inactive for more than 12 months may be removed from the roll.
duration: No required hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Current 8th or 9th grade students at a Virginia middle, high, home-school or private school. You must be a Virginia resident and a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident, with at least a C+/B- average (2.7 GPA) and a desire to explore STEM. The program is meant for students without STEM experience.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the BLAST page. Pick one session. A recommender and a school counselor must also submit forms online before the deadline.
notes: This is a state program with sessions at five universities, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card. The page says applicants must be a current 8th or 9th grader in one place. It describes rising 9th and 10th graders in another place. That means the same thing, since you apply in the school year before. The page lists the window as December 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027.
duration: 3 days, in college dorms
pay_detail: Free for all participants. Meals are provided during the session.

who_can_apply: Rising 8th and 9th grade students. Any student who might like cybersecurity is welcome. You do not need any previous experience.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the CyberSpark page. Phone: 540-231-4312.
notes: Mostly for younger teens (rising 8th and 9th graders). Cost and whether it is a day camp or overnight are not stated, so ask the program. Camp, not a job.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Everyone in grades 9 to 12. No prior design courses needed.
how_to_apply: Use the registration links on the page for the Blacksburg or virtual session. No refunds after the May 15 close. Questions: Chris Pritchett, cpritche@vt.edu.
notes: Page shows 2026 information. Expect registration to open around Dec 1 again, but this is a past pattern and not confirmed. Overnight campers stay in suite-style dorms with an RA.
duration: One week (2026 Blacksburg session June 21 to 27)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: Blacksburg session $1,250 (materials not included, about $100 estimated); virtual session $250. Needs-based scholarships are offered through the registration form.

who_can_apply: Campers ages 15 to 18. The page lists no school or residency rules. Limit of 16 campers.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the link on the STEM Summer Camp page. For a scholarship, email the contact on the page. That is kdivitto@vt.edu or the Fralin education director.
notes: The same page lists camps for younger ages; only the Geosciences camp for ages 15 to 18 is for teens. The page shows 2026 details, so confirm before planning for 2027.
duration: One week, 9am to 4pm (2026: June 1 to 5), day camp, no overnight
pay_detail: $120 for the week (2026). Two scholarships are available each week for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Rising 7th or 8th graders. First-time applicants get preference.
how_to_apply: Three parts: a student application with a one paragraph essay on what interests you about engineering, a parent form (consent, and financial statement if you want a scholarship), and a recommendation from a math, science or technology teacher.
notes: For younger teens. The drone week is residential only. Phone 540-231-7337.
duration: Three sessions, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm: June 14 to 20 (drone camp, residential), June 22 to 26, and June 29 to July 3 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: day camp $350 per week, residential $1,000 per week. Needs-based scholarships available through the parent form.

who_can_apply: High school students who start their senior year in 2026-27. You need a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 or the same in another scale. You need to have done or be doing pre-calculus. You also write a short note about why you are interested.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the PIP page and submit a statement of interest. Questions: PCOBrecruiting@vt.edu.
notes: Only for rising seniors, so a teen has one chance to apply. Travel to Blacksburg is on the family.
duration: 10 days, residential (page dates: Thursday July 9 to Saturday July 18)
pay_detail: Free. The page says cost of attendance is covered except travel to and from Blacksburg. No pay.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents entering grade 10, 11 or 12. You must be a first generation college student. That means neither parent graduated from a four year college in the U.S. or abroad.
how_to_apply: Send in the Pathways application linked on the page. Contact Perry Martin at pathways@vt.edu with questions.
notes: Only for Virginia residents who would be first generation college students. The pages do not say whether the summer program is free. The eligibility text on the page mentions students entering grades in the fall of 2025, so it may be out of date. Check the application link before you plan.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask pathways@vt.edu.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders with at least two years of lessons on violin, viola, cello or double bass.
how_to_apply: Registration information is not posted yet (the 2026 page said it was coming soon). Questions: stringproject@vt.edu.
notes: Dates are last year's. The page said registration information was coming soon.
duration: 3 days, residential (June 12-14 in 2026)
pay_detail: $450 covers meals, dorm housing, T-shirt, music and supplies

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12 at listed schools. They include Blacksburg High, Auburn High, Christiansburg High and Eastern Montgomery High. It mostly serves students who are first in their family to go to college and have lower family income. Any student who needs college prep help may join.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Talent Search page if you attend a listed school. A Spanish application PDF is also posted.
notes: Not a job. It is a free college access program. Out-of-school and adult learners are not covered by this card.
duration: Ongoing through school years
pay_detail: Free. No pay.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students, per the Virginia Tech engineering pre-college list. The camp pages do not give more rules.
how_to_apply: There are two parts. One is a student application. It has activities, short essays of 120 words or less each, and a transcript. The transcript does not need to be official. The other is a parent form. It has consent and a financial statement used for scholarships. The application is shared with the C-Tech2 camp. You can choose either camp or both.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The pages are partly out of date (they mention the 2025 application), so check the newest page and confirm dates with the program. The Virginia Tech C-Tech2 camp has its own card in this guide.
duration: 2 weeks, residential
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks. It covers room, board and program costs. You pay your own travel and personal items. Scholarships are available based on financial need. Cancel 30 or more days before camp for a 50% refund.

who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 6 to 18 may apply at each location. Each Club has its own enrollment.
how_to_apply: Use 'Register for Membership Here' on the join page, which goes to the BGCMA parent portal (bgcma.org/local-clubs/parent-portal). Use the Find a Club page to pick a Club. Headquarters phone: 404-527-7100.
notes: This is a general club membership, not a job or internship. The pages do not describe teen specific programs or teen jobs, so call your nearest Club and ask what is offered for teens. Checked 2026-10-10: the join page says summer enrollment is now open but names no year, so we cannot tell which summer. Left unconfirmed.
duration: Membership year. The join page says summer enrollment is now open.
pay_detail: Annual membership fee. The join page lists no dollar amount. It says the fee is lower than other youth groups, is waived for youth with Amerigroup insurance, and that no child is turned away for inability to pay.

who_can_apply: Residents of Brookhaven or nearby areas, ages 14 to 18 or 19. The page says both, so confirm. You need passing grades and a clean background check. You cannot have criminal convictions or Juvenile Court referrals.
how_to_apply: Download the Cadet Application Packet and the Cadet Agreement Waiver (both PDFs) from the page. The page does not describe the steps after you turn them in.
notes: Meets at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Road. The page lists ages 14 to 18 in one place and 14 to 19 in another. There is a community service requirement. Contact Officer Hawkins through the page or call 404-637-0600. Not a paid job.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursdays 7 to 9 pm
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Cost is not listed.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 who live in or around Brookhaven. No grade is listed. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Reserve a spot with the online form on the page, or contact the department. The page says early sign-up is encouraged.
notes: Held at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Rd, Brookhaven, GA 30329. Call Officer Angela Hawkins at 678-296-1904. You can also call the Community Engagement Unit. The number is 404-637-0600, Option 8. This is unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: 5 days, 9 am to 3 pm (July 20 to 24 on the page, year not printed)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 (the Virginia Wing page says to be at least 12 and not yet 19, and a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). The squadron has both teen and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email va-130info@vawg.cap.gov or call (703) 239-4530 to ask about a meeting. The Virginia Wing steps are to visit with your parents. Then go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the cadet application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Meetings are at Irving Middle School, 8100 Old Keene Mill, Springfield, VA 22152, but the location can change for school events, and in August they meet elsewhere. Meetings are cancelled on the same days Fairfax County Schools cancels. The squadron page says it won a 2021 Virginia Wing Squadron of Merit award.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursday nights 6:30 to 9:00
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 in Wake and Johnston counties per the Capital Area youth page. The interest form for Wake County asks whether you are 16 to 24. The NextGen site says the program serves young adults facing barriers such as legal issues, home problems or missed education, and lists Wake, Johnston, Chatham, Lee and Orange counties. Exact eligibility rules and income limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form for your county at capitalareanextgen.org, or use the Request More Information form on the Capital Area youth page.
notes: This is the federal workforce (WIOA) style youth program for Wake County. Durham is covered by a different workforce board and is not listed. The pages do not say whether 14 to 17 year olds qualify in every case; ask the career center.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Apprenticeships and work experience are listed as services. Whether work experience is paid is not stated.

who_can_apply: Open to teens in high school now, and to teens about to start high school. You must live in the Chapel Hill-Carrboro area.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Council application. It is a PDF on the town website. For questions, email the supervisor, Galen Poythress, at jpoythress@carrboronc.gov.
notes: The group wants committed leaders, not students who only need volunteer hours. The page lists jpoythress@carrboronc.gov as the contact, but its link goes to a townofcarrboro.org address, so confirm which one works. The next new member information meeting is not set yet.
duration: General meetings on the third Wednesday of each month at 7pm, Drakeford Library Complex
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join.

who_can_apply: High school students in the summer before junior or senior year, at least 16 on the first day of camp (no exceptions). A government photo ID is needed for CDC security. Non-Atlanta residents may apply but must arrange housing and travel. Non-U.S. citizens may apply with the documents asked for.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe the application steps. The camp page says the application is found through the FAQ page when it opens, and to check back in January 2027.
notes: Very competitive in past years, but numbers were not on the pages. Sessions are fixed, campers cannot arrive late, leave early or miss days.
duration: Five days, 8:45 AM to 4:00 PM. The 2026 sessions were June 22 to 26 and July 20 to 24.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to attend. Campers cover their own housing and daily transportation.

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer interest form offers the age choices 14-17 and 18 and older. The page does not state a separate minimum age.
how_to_apply: Read the position descriptions, then fill out the volunteer interest form on the library's Volunteer with us page and pick Youth Event Support Volunteer.
notes: The 14 to 17 range comes from the age options on the interest form, not from a written rule. Call 919-968-2777 or email library@chapelhillnc.gov to confirm the minimum age and hours. The library also has a Teen Room for ages 13 to 18; no teen advisory board was listed on the pages.
duration: Ongoing; most needed in summer and on afternoons and weekends in the school year

who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 5 to 18. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out a member form in the online member portal. It is linked from the Membership page. Phone 434-971-9400 or email admin@bgclubcva.org.
notes: There are six clubs: Albemarle Campus, Cherry Avenue, James River, Madison, Orange and Southwood. UpNext is named only on the home page. Ask the Southwood Club how to join and what it pays.
duration: Ongoing; open after school and all day in summer
pay_detail: Low membership dues, amount not stated. UpNext pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Children ages 12 to 17 may volunteer if a parent or guardian is with them for each shift. In the Food Recovery Area, ages 12 to 16 need a parent or guardian at each shift. Volunteers ages 17 and older may work there without an adult after an initial shift with an adult. Youth groups ages 12 to 15 need one adult chaperone for every 3 children. Youth groups ages 16 and 17 need one adult for every 6 youth. Volunteers must be 18 or older at the Winchester warehouse.
how_to_apply: Create your own account on the online volunteer calendar. It is required for safety and communication. Then register for a shift. If you do not get a confirmation email, the registration did not go through. Contact the volunteer team at volunteer@brafb.org. Group sizes are 4 to 8 people at most locations. They are up to 10 at the Verona warehouse. Everyone needs their own account.
notes: A parent or guardian must be at every shift for ages 12 to 17, so this works best for families. The page lists the front desk as (540) 268-3663. The footer lists 540-248-3663. Confirm which number is right. The page names the Charlottesville warehouse and offsite locations under the 12 to 17 rule with a parent or guardian at each shift, and names the Winchester warehouse as 18 and older.
duration: One shift at a time. Shift length is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts

who_can_apply: High school students in the Charlottesville area. Grade levels are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form on the C3 youth page.
notes: The same page says C3 takes high school and college interns each term. Work includes grants, policy, marketing and energy checks. Pay and ages are not stated. See the careers page of C3.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The page says paid interns lead the group but does not say if teen members are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. The page welcomes volunteers ages 14 and up. Groups with people under 18 need at least one adult chaperone for every 10 children.
how_to_apply: Use the Schedule Orientation or Volunteer Application link on the SPCA volunteer page to choose an orientation date and fill out the volunteer application. Orientation comes before you take on tasks. Contact: volunteer@caspca.org or 434-973-5959 ext. 314.
notes: The pages do not say if 14 to 17 year olds need a parent signature. They do not say if there are limits on which animals teens can work with. Ask at orientation. The apply link goes to the SPCA's event calendar on a third party site.
duration: Ongoing. Hours and length are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The volunteer pays a $25 volunteer fee plus a separate $9 background check. The page does not say if either is refundable.

who_can_apply: Classes are free for Charlottesville City Schools and Albemarle County Public Schools students. The pages do not list grade levels. They do not list the steps to enroll.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe an enrollment process. Ask your school counselor. Contact CATEC at 434-245-2419 or catecinfo@charlottesvilleschools.org. The 2026 to 2027 Program of Studies PDF is linked from the CATEC high school program of studies page.
notes: Confirm first. Grade levels and enrollment steps are not on the pages. For 2026 to 2027, CATEC does not offer some academic courses. They are Biology II, English 12, USA Government, and Economics and Personal Finance. EMT and Fire Science are no longer dual enrollment through CVCC. Students still earn CTE credits. Address: 1000 East Rio Road, Charlottesville.
duration: School year classes. Program lengths and schedules are not stated on the program pages.
pay_detail: Free for Charlottesville City and Albemarle County students. Students earn high school elective credits, can earn industry certifications, and some programs offer dual enrollment college credit. Transportation to and from your base school is provided.

who_can_apply: Charlottesville-area youth 14 to 21 (14 by the start of the CAYIP Academy). City of Charlottesville residents get priority. Parent or guardian must also complete paperwork for youth under 18.
how_to_apply: Submit the CAYIP application (questionnaire, inventory and agreement to participate) during the session window, then a one-on-one interview. Accepted youth attend the mandatory paid CAYIP Academy. Contact: cayipinquiries@charlottesville.gov, 434-987-0018.
notes: Applications are only accepted during a session window. Transportation is not provided. Interns may miss at most 5 days per session. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers must get an Employment Certificate before any work; the page does not mention it, so ask CAYIP staff how it is handled.
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Virginia Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18. The national Civil Air Patrol page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Send the squadron a message on Facebook or email 091.pa@vawg.cap.gov and they will be in touch. The Virginia Wing headquarters number on the page is 804-454-7356.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron page gives no street address, so ask for the exact meeting location before you go. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets each Tuesday from 7 to 9 p.m. at Lakeside Middle School.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says the program is for up to twelve city students. A related summer internship for four Charlottesville High School youth is supported in part by the city youth internship program (CAYIP).
how_to_apply: This is not listed. Email grow@cultivatecharlottesville.org or call 434-365-4529. Ask how to join.
notes: Pay, ages and how to apply are not posted, so ask first. The nonprofit lists "Food Justice Interns" under its City Schoolyard Garden program. Apprentice jobs on the page are for young adults, not teens.
duration: 8 weeks, 20 hours per week
pay_detail: Not stated. The City Schoolyard Garden page, checked on 2026-10-10, calls other roles paid but gives no pay for these interns. Ask first.

who_can_apply: Habitat Store: age 12 and up (ages 12 and 13 must come with a parent, guardian or older sibling). Construction site: at least 16. Power tools: at least 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a Habitat Store orientation or a building shift. Use the VolunteerHub links on the volunteer page. For Youth Build Days, email volunteer@cvillehabitat.org.
notes: Teens under 16 cannot work on the construction site. Habitat clubs at local high schools have regular volunteer chances; ask your school.
duration: Ongoing; shifts vary
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Open to all. The high school track is for rising 9th graders through college freshmen. Tuition help is offered. The site also runs free workshops for under-resourced youth (KEEP it Reel).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a workshop in the online store (first-time users make an Amilia account). Ask for tuition assistance with the online form. Email programs@lighthousestudio.org or call 434-293-6992.
notes: Light House also lists a Careers page, an Adrenaline Film Project (Nov 5 to 8, 2026) and a Youth Film Festival. Those were not read in detail.
duration: 1 to 2 weeks, 9am to 3pm (2026 listed dates June 1 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the program page. Tuition assistance is available, reviewed case by case and first come first served.

who_can_apply: High school students. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Contact Education Director Daniel Kunkel. Use the contact link on the Live Arts education page.
notes: The page gives no dates, cost, or application. Confirm the program still runs. Live Arts also lists Teen Studio (ages 14 to 18) as a class, not a job.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The Live Arts education page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask the Education Director.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. The page prefers 14 and up but will consider mature, motivated 13 year olds. Attending an Earth Roots or other teen camp session is preferred. The teen, not a parent, fills out the application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application on the page when it reopens. Waitlist or questions: connect@livingearthva.org or 434-260-0086.
notes: A leadership program, not a job. The school also runs a Teen Apprentice Program (about $3,315 tuition) that was not carded.
duration: 1 or more weeks (2026 day CIT weeks June 22 to July 24; overnight weeks June 14 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Teens pay: day CIT $365 per week, overnight CIT $515 per week (2026). No pay or stipend is mentioned. A scholarship fund exists.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in the Charlottesville area who are Music Resource Center members. Members must be in 6th to 12th grade and go to school each day.
how_to_apply: Become an MRC member (drop in at 105 Ridge St, Mon to Fri 2:30 to 7pm, no appointment), then fill out the wait list form on the MRC Certified page. Phone 434-979-5478, musicresourcecenter@gmail.com.
notes: Sophomores and younger can ask to join the wait list, but exceptions are not likely. Work permit rules for Virginia were not checked.
duration: Studio track: 32 hours of lessons plus 10 to 20 paid hours. Live sound track: 28 hours of lessons plus 10 to 20 paid hours.
pay_detail: Paid a competitive wage above the state minimum for 10 to 20 internship hours. The training is free for members. Membership fees are a sliding scale from $1 to $250 a year based on family income.

who_can_apply: Listed for ages 15 and up. Everyone must pass the in-water pretest or be removed from the class.
how_to_apply: Register through the city's Registration & Tickets system. Within 72 hours of registering, email swimprograms@charlottesville.gov with the subject Lifeguard Pretest to book the pretest at least 8 days ahead.
notes: The page does not say the class leads to a job. The city lists seasonal and variable-hour jobs on governmentjobs.com; none were open on 2026-10-09. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before any work.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 15 (must be 13 by June 1). The page lists no grade or school rule.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through the Y account system (Daxko) and pay the fee. Weekly sign up closes two weeks before each week. Money help is on the scholarship page. Contact youth@piedmontymca.org or 434-270-7534.
notes: A paid program for teens, not a job. It is a leadership step toward working as a camp counselor later. A Greene County CIT program is also listed on the Y site but was not read.
duration: Up to 9 weeks (2026: June 8 to Aug 7), 7:30am to 5:30pm, plus free training June 1 to 5
pay_detail: Teens pay. $50 registration, then $175 per week for YMCA members or $200 per week for non-members. The June 1 to 5 training week is free. No wages or stipend are listed.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at a school that takes part. You must meet the rules to join, and your school and a parent or guardian must say yes. Homeschooled juniors and seniors can take Dual Credit classes. Freshmen and sophomores are looked at one by one.
how_to_apply: For dual enrollment, sign up with your high school counselor. For Dual Credit, apply through PVCC admissions at admissions@pvcc.edu.
notes: More than 1,200 high school students join each term. Early College has rules to qualify. It may have district scholarships.
duration: Each semester
pay_detail: Dual enrollment classes taught in your high school are no cost to the student. Dual Credit classes taken on your own outside the school day require tuition.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers ages 15 to 18 for the summer months.
how_to_apply: The page has a general volunteer link (Apply here). It does not say it is for junior volunteers. Call the volunteer office to ask.
notes: Only the age range and summer timing are posted. GPA, grade, hours, and deadlines are not stated. Confirm everything before applying.
duration: Summer months; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth who live in Charlottesville City or Albemarle County. You can be in grade 7 up to high school graduation.
how_to_apply: Send one form for each student on the program Application and Wait List page. Contact partnerships@virginia.edu or 434-924-2414.
notes: Pay and internship details are not posted. Ask the office. There is a wait list.
duration: Ongoing; summer camps for younger students and internships for high schoolers
pay_detail: Paid internship placements for high schoolers. Pay rate and hours are not stated on the page. The program itself is free, with transport and meals provided.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who are 15 to 18 years old by the program start date. Design-curious students are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form by the deadline. Include a note for the scholarship review. Free Zoom info sessions ran Dec to March. Questions: program director Kyle Sturgeon, sturgeon@virginia.edu.
notes: Summer 2026 was fully enrolled. Each session has 20 students and at most 10 can stay overnight in UVA dorms. Day students commute.
duration: 6 days, 9am to 4pm (2026 sessions June 8 to 13 and June 22 to 27)
pay_detail: Tuition by household income. Under $100k: tuition waived. $100k to $160k: $1,350 (day) or $1,600 (overnight). $160k and up: $1,650 (day) or $1,900 (overnight). Overnight adds $250 in the listed prices.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with strong academic records. The page gives no GPA cutoff. Housing is not provided and high school students cannot use UVA housing unless they are in UVA Advance.
how_to_apply: Send the Online Non-Degree Student form and choose Summer Session. Send a Medical Consent Form for Minors signed by a parent. Ask your counselor or principal for a Secondary School Report and your transcript. Contact summer@virginia.edu or 434-924-3371.
notes: Families set up their own housing. For a live in option, see the separate UVA Advance card.
duration: One course per session; session dates not read
pay_detail: 2026 tuition listed per credit hour: $484 for Virginia residents or $1,787 for non-residents, plus a one-time comprehensive fee ($493 or $553) for on-Grounds courses. The page does not say which rate high schoolers pay, so ask the office.

who_can_apply: Students at Charlottesville schools (middle schools, Charlottesville High zones and Lugo-McGinness Academy). Also students who live in the city but go to a private school, are homeschooled, or go to school out of the district. The council picks its 15 members. Ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Youth Opportunity Coordination page. Call Juanika Howard at 434-529-7978. She helps youth find ways to take part.
notes: Seats are set by school and grade, so only some seats may be open at a time. Ask the coordinator when applications open.
duration: School year, monthly meetings
pay_detail: Not stated. Treat as unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 10 to 12. You send an application and two references who are not relatives. You also do a 15-minute interview.
how_to_apply: New LITs fill out the online application and have two references send the reference form. Returning LITs use a separate form. Then a 15-minute interview.
notes: This costs money and is not a paid job. You must attend at least 85% of your session. Dates shown are from summer 2026.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, Monday to Friday about 8:30 am to 3:45 pm, plus a one-day training
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs $500 per session for new LITs, $450 for returning LITs. You earn about 140 volunteer service hours per session.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page lists no ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Water Warriors page. You can also sign up there for emails about Water Warriors news and events.
notes: In summer, high school students can test water samples, check CASSI units and clean trash traps with staff. Contact: Jillian Griffin, jgriffin@chattahoochee.org, or 404-352-9828.
duration: School-year program Oct 2026 to April 2027; summer shadowing for high schoolers (dates not stated)
pay_detail: Not stated. The page describes service hours and does not mention pay or a cost.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth at least 12 and not yet 19. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Visit a squadron and attend at least three weekly meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron with the Georgia Wing locator. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application, or ask if you can apply online. Wing office: 770-428-9031, publicaffairs@gawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Georgia Wing page says cadets are not obligated to join the military. The national page lists military obligation for cadets as none. Dues vary by location and the national page says $25 to $50 per year, so ask your squadron for the exact amount. The Georgia Wing home page lists squadrons including Atlanta (GA109), Marietta, Roswell, Chamblee, Lawrenceville, Cumming and others.
duration: Ongoing. A weekly squadron meeting of about 2 hours, one Saturday event monthly, and one week-long encampment in summer (national page).
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, per the national page. A very active cadet might spend about $300 to $600 in the first year before aid, with some help for uniforms and overnight fees.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application packet by the deadline. Chosen applicants get an email and an interview. Call Volunteer Services at 931-502-1055 with questions.
notes: Clarksville is northwest of Nashville. The source is a hospital news post from March 2026. Confirm the 2027 dates with Volunteer Services. The Nashville Vanderbilt University Hospital page says volunteers must be 18 or older. It says its summer high school program is on hold.
duration: Two one-week sessions (8 a.m. to 4 p.m., all five days), or a senior track of at least 40 hours in June and July
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is stated.

who_can_apply: High school juniors. About 60 students are chosen for each class by the steering committee. The page lists no county or school rule.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps or link a form. Contact the Cobb Chamber: Katie Guice, 770-859-2334, kguice@cobbchamber.org.
notes: Costs money and is not a job. Ask about financial help. No application deadline is stated, so call early. The page says six evening programs but lists seven evening dates; the duration follows the dates.
duration: Aug to April: orientation, fall retreat and 7 sessions (2026-27 class)
pay_detail: $850 tuition for selected students. The page says financial help is accepted for those who cannot pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must be 14 and in high school to join. Need a 2.0 GPA or higher, a clean background check, physical fitness and good character. Gang or organized crime ties disqualify you.
how_to_apply: Go to three meetings in a row. Then pick up an application packet and turn in a detailed application. Last step is an oral interview with a panel of cadet officers and advisors.
notes: Meets at the Cobb County Police Training Academy, 2435 East-West Connector, Austell, GA 30106. Contact Officer Andy Higgins, (770) 528-8388. New members have a 6-month trial and get a uniform after 6 meetings in a row. Not a paid job.
duration: Weekly meetings: Thursdays 6 to 8 pm in the school year, 6 to 9 pm in summer
pay_detail: Volunteer program. No fees are listed. The Post raises money to attend national contests.

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older. People 18 and older must pass a background check first. The page does not say which roles teens can take.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Cobb County Public Library Volunteer Application. You can also contact the branch where you want to help to ask what openings it has.
notes: Library phone (770) 528-2326, contactus@cobbcat.org. Branches: East Cobb, Gritters, Kemp Memorial, Lewis A. Ray, Mountain View, North Cobb, Powder Springs, Sewell Mill, Sibley, South Cobb, Stratton, Sweetwater Valley, Switzer, Vinings, West Cobb.
duration: Ongoing. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Cobb County School District juniors and seniors who are 16 or older. Your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator can tell you the rules at your school.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. All applications must be completed in full before they are considered. The district page lists a coordinator for each high school.
notes: District CTAE and WBL coordinator on the page: Sapph Espinoza. The job should relate to your career goals and CTAE coursework. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: A school year; students can be in WBL both junior and senior year. A 90-minute block needs at least 7.5 work hours a week.
pay_detail: Placements may be paid or non-paid, according to the district page.

who_can_apply: Cobb County residents ages 16 to 24 who meet income qualifications (decided at eligibility) and are in one of the program's target groups.
how_to_apply: Fill out the B.O.S.S. application inquiry form online (it asks if you live in Cobb County, are 16 to 24, and are in school), or call 770-528-4300 or email bossinfo@cobbworks.org.
notes: Funded through WIOA, so participants must meet eligibility rules. The same site lists a PowerUp! plumbing pre-apprenticeship and a Cobb County Fire P.R.E.P. Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.
pay_detail: Participants can earn up to $8,500 across the program's activities, according to the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. This is a composite squadron, which means it has both cadets and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email the squadron commander to ask about visiting a meeting with a parent. CAP's usual steps are listed on the Virginia and North Carolina wing pages. They are to go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Squadron location: 6709 Corporal Frank Scott Drive, College Park, MD 20740. Commander listed on the page: Capt. Estelle Roche, estelle.roche@mdwg.cap.gov. The meeting time is from the squadron page; confirm before you go.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6:45 to 9:00
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $55 for Maryland in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Seven teen seats for young people no older than 18 when appointed. The page does not say where you must live, but it is a city committee.
how_to_apply: Email the Recreation staff liaison through the city page to ask how to join.
notes: No meeting in March. Summer recess is June to August. Meeting places vary by month.
duration: Meets the second Monday of the month, 6:30 pm, with a summer break June to August
pay_detail: Not stated (no pay mentioned)

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the orientation date. No grade rule listed. Needs proof of immunizations (MMR, varicella, hepatitis B, Tdap, current flu shot, TB screen).
how_to_apply: Fill out the student form linked on the page. Go to the required orientation. Send shot records. The Lanham contact is Valerie Nicholas, Volunteer Coordinator. Her address is vnic100@luminishealth.org.
notes: Ask the Lanham coordinator for the semester due date, since the page does not list one for Lanham.
duration: One semester, at least 3 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Enrolled in grade 10, 11 or 12 in good standing, 16 by the application deadline, U.S. citizen, 3.0 unweighted GPA, and permanent residence within 50 miles of NASA Goddard (Greenbelt, MD) or NASA Wallops (Wallops Island, VA).
how_to_apply: Apply in NASA STEM Gateway, pick one or more projects, and upload a transcript plus resume details. Projects are added until the end of February.
notes: The page lists up to 55 high school students. General questions: info@spaceclub.org.
duration: Six weeks each summer, from late June until early August.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Send an email to Jessica Peters. Her address is jessica.peters@pgparks.com.
notes: Ask for the next session dates.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and older. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application link. Email megan.merchant@pgparks.com to ask how to apply before the March 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Confirm first. The county page has no application link. It does not describe audition steps. Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after a job offer.
duration: May to July 2027
pay_detail: Paid apprenticeship. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Prince George's County residents ages 13 to 18. No grade is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is free. It has a short essay and a piece of original artwork in your preferred genre, such as music, dance or visual arts. Contact: Shaiday Dancy, Teen Arts Specialist, 301-446-3252, shaiday.dancy@pgparks.com.
notes: Applicants could also be invited to be a Teen Arts Council ambassador. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Eight months, October 2026 to June 2027, with meetings every two weeks
pay_detail: $300 stipend after you finish the eight month term

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 who pass the audition.
how_to_apply: Attend the audition on February 7, 2027 at 3 p.m. Questions go to megan.merchant@pgparks.com. The audition event page was not available when checked, so ask for audition details (what to prepare) by email.
notes: Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after the minor is offered a job. Confirm first. The page lists the audition but not what to prepare.
duration: Weekly rehearsals starting April 2027 and a summer performance schedule from June 28 to August 6, 2027.
pay_detail: Paid, part time. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Email jessica.peters@pgparks.com.
notes: Ask for the next session dates.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: Dual enrollment is for PG County Public Schools juniors and seniors. You need an unweighted GPA of at least 2.6 and must meet placement rules. Concurrent enrollment is for Maryland residents in grades 11 and 12 who are in private school, homeschooled or not in PG County. The same rules apply. Talented and Gifted is for grades 8 to 10. You must have been named gifted in the last year and have a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
how_to_apply: New students: use Apply Now on the PGCC application portal. Returning students: finish the counselor and high school certification form. Talk to your school counselor first. Phone 301-546-7469.
notes: Also look at Early Admission and Early/Middle College on the PGCC high school programs page. Early Admission is for seniors, so ask your counselor. Early/Middle College is for first-generation students. This is not a job.
duration: One college term at a time
pay_detail: PG County Public Schools pays tuition, fees and textbooks for dually enrolled students in qualifying courses. Eligible Maryland concurrent students get a 50% tuition discount.

who_can_apply: Students 16 or older. You need to clear immunization checks and a background check. You also do online training. Bring an ID to the orientation interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Send back the onboarding form by fax or by email. Go to an orientation. You will have an interview with the volunteer coordinator. Then finish training and the background check. The email is UMCapitalRegionVolunteer@umm.edu.
notes: Hospital is at 901 Harry S. Truman Drive North, Largo, MD 20774. You will get a confirmation email within two business days after sending the application and health form.
duration: 100 hours within 12 months, 4 hours per shift
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. It is hard to get in. You need to know advanced math well. UMD's camp list says rising grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Camp Registration form linked on the camp site. Contact: mathcamp@umd.edu.
notes: Check the FAQ page for cost and dates before applying.
duration: Two weeks (June 22 to July 2 in 2026). Page says 'See You Next Summer in 2027'.
pay_detail: UMD's 2026 camp list showed $25; the camp site does not state a cost.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade in the fall. The page does not list a GPA or location rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with a one page personal statement. Email a recommendation from a STEM teacher and your official transcript to summerengr@umd.edu. Contact: Sandra Crespin Melgar, summerengr@umd.edu.
notes: Costs money. Price, dates and deadline above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.
duration: One week, residential. In 2026: Session One July 26 to 31 and Session Two August 2 to 7 (you attend one).
pay_detail: $1,400 per student (project materials, activities, and room and board; transportation is not included). Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students from Montgomery and Prince George's Counties. 18 to 24 students are accepted. No grade level listed (UMD's camp list says grades 9 to 12).
how_to_apply: Register through the link on the event page (it was full in 2026). Questions: Abba Gumel, agumel@umd.edu.
notes: Held at 6116 Executive Blvd, North Bethesda, MD 20852. Not on the College Park campus.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily (July 27 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the camp page (the 2026 link was go.umd.edu/whatsyourstory2026). Questions: whatsyourstorycamp@umd.edu.
notes: Ask about scholarships by email.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily (Aug 3 to 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 registration fee, includes a light breakfast and lunch. Scholarships available (no details given).

who_can_apply: Students who go to high school in Maryland or Washington, D.C., or live there. You need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5. You must show interest and skill in math, science or engineering.
how_to_apply: Online application with a one page personal statement (12 point, double spaced), an official high school transcript, and official PSAT or SAT scores if you have them. You must attend all sessions, orientation, and the pre and post tests. Contact: Ms. Aishah Briscoe, FutureEngineer@umd.edu.
notes: The page does not say whether the program is residential. Costs money but is low compared with most pre-college programs. Dates and the $400 price are from the 2026 page.
duration: Three weeks, in person on the UMD campus. The 2026 session ran Monday July 6 to Friday July 24.
pay_detail: The whole program costs $400 per student. Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: Current 10th, 11th and 12th graders. You should be strong in school, like robotics and show initiative. You need a high school transcript and a resume to apply.
how_to_apply: Use the online application linked from the SPARC page (Apply Now). Include your high school transcript and resume. A parent or other authorized adult must sign you in and out each day. Contact: robotics-sparc@umd.edu.
notes: Very expensive and commuter only. Participation does not guarantee admission to UMD. The page banner says Apply Now with an application deadline of December 1, 2026. Confirm the 2027 price with the program.
duration: Three weeks, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Summer 2027: Session 1 July 6 to 23, Session 2 July 26 to August 13. You enroll in one session.
pay_detail: The Summer 2026 price was $5,000 for one 3 week session (project materials and activities; lunch and transportation are not included). The 2027 price is not posted. A limited number of need based scholarships are available, and payments are not refundable.

who_can_apply: High school students from Prince George's County. No grade levels listed (UMD's camp list says grades 10 to 12).
