how_to_apply: Fill out the high school student interest form linked on the camp page. Contact: Megan Newcombe, newcombe@umd.edu.
notes: Check the page in spring for 2027.
duration: One week (June 22 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free to attend

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are thinking about majoring in engineering. The page says the programs are open to all students. Gender does not matter.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps beyond saying the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Contact Jen Kuntz of the WIE Program at jakuntz@umd.edu or 301-405-0315. Scholarship and payment details are sent after admission decisions.
notes: Costs money. The program does not guarantee admission to UMD. Other UMD engineering pre-college programs are listed at https://eng.umd.edu/pre-college-programs/summer.
duration: One week, residential. The 2026 session ran Sunday July 12 to Friday July 17.
pay_detail: $1,500 per student for Summer 2026 (covers materials, activities, and room and board; transportation is not included). Scholarships are available for admitted students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students who are sophomores or higher by September 2026, and newly graduated seniors. The page says UFCC 2026 in this section but lists 2027 dates, so confirm the year.
how_to_apply: Be free all week. Then fill out the online application. Have two adults who are not family send letters of support. They can be a teacher, counselor or club adviser. A committee will let you know. Accepted students pay the fee to hold a spot.
notes: Students arrive Sunday 2 to 3 p.m. and leave Saturday at 1 p.m.
duration: One week, arrive Sunday and leave Saturday (July 11 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $150 activity fee after acceptance ($153.50 if paid by PayPal). Tuition is covered by a Maryland Department of Natural Resources grant.

who_can_apply: 15 or older by the start of the program, and a current high school student who returns to high school in the fall. The page does not set a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Online application with one professional reference (name and email).
notes: Located in Washington, DC, so it is a commute for Maryland teens. Check back in February 2027 for the application.
duration: 6 weeks, 2 shifts a week (Tue/Wed or Wed/Thu), 10am to 3pm
pay_detail: Unpaid. At least 50 service hours.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County youth ages 14 to 18 who are in school. You keep at least a C average and have good attendance and behavior.
how_to_apply: Get the DCFR Explorer application packet from the page. Send it in with 3 job references and your latest report card.
notes: Contact frexplorers@dekalbcountyga.gov. Not a paid job, so no work permit.
duration: Year-round, with a 2-week summer Cadet Training
pay_detail: $50 yearly fee, due after you are fully admitted. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings for the school year; at least one meeting must be in person
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours for attending meetings.

who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 16 and older. Adult volunteers also need a background check. The page does not list any other rule for teens.
how_to_apply: There are four steps. Fill out the Volunteer Application. Sign the Volunteer Waiver. Go to a short orientation, online or in person. Then start.
notes: Call 404-294-2838 or write to Monique Larkin at mllarkin@dekalbcountyga.gov. The page gives no direct link to the application. Other park volunteering lists no minimum age. Examples are clean-up days and nature programs.
duration: Ongoing. Weekday afternoons and Saturdays.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: DeKalb County School District students, mostly juniors and seniors. The program page links to a PDF of the rules on grades, behavior and attendance. Ask your school's WBL coordinator for the current rules.
how_to_apply: Apply to your school's WBL coordinator. Ask what the current rules are.
notes: Only for DeKalb schools students. You must leave campus at the start of your first WBL class, even on days you are not scheduled to work. The district CTAE office is at 1701 Mountain Industrial Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083.
duration: A school class block (1, 2 or 3 periods in a row)
pay_detail: Paid or unpaid work experience. Pay amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: 2025 rules: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 21 who pass a drug screening and background check. Interns were picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: In 2025, online registration at dekalbcountyga.gov/dsyep. That address now leads to a registration form marked no longer active. For help the 2025 county release listed the Workforce Development Manager at (470) 572-8229.
notes: Confirm that a new cycle exists before planning around it. All dates, pay and rules here are from the 2025 county release. WorkSource DeKalb also lists youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers as a service group. It sends people to ATLworks.org to check eligibility. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 2 to July 3 in 2025)
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2025. A 2026 rate is not posted yet, so confirm it.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors in 2026-27 who are at least 15 by June 1, 2027 and from the Research Triangle area. Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN to receive the stipend. Students must provide their own transportation.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a recommendation letter (links on the CeBA page). Applicants hear back in mid-April.
notes: The 2026 deadline is stated two ways. It is March 20 on the flyer and March 27 in the FAQ. The page says there is no housing or transportation help, so only local students are considered. The $2,400 is a completion award. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 31), about 9 am to 5 pm on site
pay_detail: $2,400 awarded on completion of the program

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or 17 (16 by June 24 in 2026). Students must attend both days at one site. Space is limited to 25 slots at each site.
how_to_apply: Student completes the online application and a parent or guardian completes the Participation Agreement (both on Qualtrics links on the page). No late or incomplete submissions.
notes: Both Duke pages are titled Junior Volunteer Program but describe this event for 2026. The application window was only 3 days, so watch the page in early April. Questions: DRHVolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Durham) or DRAH_VolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Raleigh). Duke University Hospital says it no longer offers a junior volunteer program for high school students.
duration: 2 days (2026: June 23-24 at Duke Regional in Durham; June 24-25 at Duke Raleigh Hospital)

who_can_apply: Durham City or Durham County residents between 14 and 24 as of June 30, 2026, per the Duke page. The Duke article describes participants as Durham-area high school students.
how_to_apply: Submit the Durham YouthWorks application and select the healthcare category (link on the Duke Community Affairs page). Contact: Kimberly Monroe, kimberly.monroe@duke.edu.
notes: Applications go through Durham YouthWorks (City of Durham), whose own page could not be read (blocked). The article says about 50 students were planned for the latest class. North Carolina requires a Youth Employment Certificate for anyone under 18 who works; the employer starts that process.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 6-24, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students in current grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 to attend. (The page also lists middle school programs for grades 6-8.)
how_to_apply: Join the information request list on the Duke Pre-College page to be told when 2027 dates and courses open.
notes: Courses, session dates and fees for Summer 2027 were not posted on 2026-10-09. Check back after the October 2026 announcement.
duration: Three sessions; dates to be announced in October 2026
pay_detail: 2027 residential fee not yet posted (Duke lists it as to be determined). Enrollment deposit: $500 before April 2, 2027, or $1,500 after April 1. Airport shuttle $45 each way; extra nights $120 each.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up at Dunwoody Nature Center (15 and up at Island Ford). Be mature, reliable, flexible and energetic. You must attend a pre-camp orientation, in person the first time.
how_to_apply: Write to the Junior Counselor Coordinator. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org.
notes: Phone 770-394-3322, info@dunwoodynature.org. The first email link on the page goes to a different address, so use the one in the FAQ (juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org). Camp dates are not listed on the page. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Asked to commit to a 5-day camp week, but you can work any days you are free. Full day 9:00 am to 4:00 pm or half day 9:00 am to 1:30 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer position, no cost. You can ask for a letter documenting your hours.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 13, or have a guardian's permission to fill out the form. The form lets you pick the age group you want to work with, including teens 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer form (skills, preferred age group, days and times, hours per week, emergency contact). Questions: Maker_STEAM@dconc.gov.
notes: Days offered are Monday to Saturday. Time options are morning, afternoon or evening. The page does not describe a teen-only volunteer track.
duration: You choose hours per week on the form

who_can_apply: The For Teens page says the program is for all tweens and teens in grades 6 to 12. The general volunteer page says all volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Contact the teen librarian at your preferred branch. The general volunteer page also says to fill out the volunteer application form (PDF) and bring it to your nearest library.
notes: The two Durham County Library pages disagree on age: the teen page says grades 6 to 12, the general volunteer page says 14 or older. Ask the teen librarian which applies. The library says it cannot currently host court-mandated community service hours.
duration: Ongoing, set with the branch

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old (bring proof of age to the pre-course swim test). The page also says candidates must be at least 15 on or before the last class session, so ask which rule applies. You must pass the pre-course swim test: a 150 yard swim-tread-swim, then a timed event with a 10 pound object retrieved from 7 to 10 feet deep.
how_to_apply: Sign up online at dprplaymore.org (Register Online). Or sign up in person at any Durham Parks and Recreation site. Then pass the swim test before the course. Apply for lifeguard jobs on the City of Durham career page.
notes: Search ActiveNet for DAS for current dates. Space is limited and filled by order of pre-course test registration. Questions: DPRAquatics@durhamnc.gov, 919-560-4444. Whether teens under 18 need NC working papers was not checked.
duration: About 6 hours of online work, then in-person sessions (Spring 2026 courses ran March 30 to April 2)
pay_detail: Training is free. City of Durham pool lifeguard jobs started at $18.90 an hour on the outdoor pools page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. No experience is required.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer page and sign up for an open shift. Or email DPRVolunteers@DurhamNC.gov about the role you want. Then fill out the online volunteer application.
notes: Phone 919-560-4355. DPR also lists tutor and mentor roles with youth at recreation centers (after school and summer camp assistants); the page does not give an age for those, so ask.
duration: Shifts as listed on the volunteer opportunities page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. DPR can give you a record of service hours for school or scholarships.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. High school graduate, equivalency holder, or currently in a program leading to a diploma. GPA of 2.00 or above.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student interest form on the Durham Tech page. Or contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator, Dr. Norman Collins, at 919-536-7200 ext. 1402.
notes: Open to students 16 and up, including current high school students. Which fields are offered is not listed on this page.
duration: Varies by field
pay_detail: Pre-apprenticeship may or may not be paid. Apprenticeship pays a wage scale that increases with experience. Tuition waiver while in the apprenticeship.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. Need a 2.8 or higher unweighted GPA, or test scores showing college readiness. The career path also accepts a written recommendation from your principal. To stay in, you must keep at least a 2.0 college GPA after two college courses.
how_to_apply: Go to an interest meeting. Talk to your school counselor and the Durham Tech liaison. Then send the CCP application and papers. These are the waiver and pathway forms, test scores and transcript.
notes: Students at Middle College High School, City of Medicine Academy and Durham School of Technology use a different path and deadline. The pages state no North Carolina residency rule. Check with the college. The eligibility page confirms the 2.8 GPA or test score rule. It also confirms the principal waiver for the career path.
duration: One semester at a time
pay_detail: Tuition-free

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 as of June 1 of the program year (June 1, 2026 on the current page).
how_to_apply: Create a MyImpact account and complete the application, with student and parent signatures on four forms. Get a recommendation from a teacher or school counselor by the deadline and rank up to three hospital locations. Interview, health screening and orientation follow.
notes: The window was only 10 days in 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting in early 2027. Space is limited and waitlists happen. Health screening includes a TB test and proof of chickenpox and measles immunity. No shadowing, internships or clinical hours.
duration: 8 weeks (June 1 to July 24 in 2026), one shift per week, Monday to Thursday, at least 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. No program fee stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students; the page says it serves current sophomores and juniors. Application needs transcript and recommendations.
how_to_apply: Choose a program and course, review costs, then start the online application (transcript, recommendations, $70 fee). After acceptance, complete the pre-arrival checklist and pay the $350 enrollment deposit.
notes: Expensive. The nearest deadline is the Pre-Med Institute on Feb 1, 2027 (deadline_iso shows the main May 3 date). Financial aid deadline was May 1 in 2026. Information sessions are in November and December 2026.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks (2027 noncredit sessions June 13 to 26, June 27 to July 10, July 11 to 24)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: 2-week noncredit course $5,510 residential or $3,925 commuter; 3-week institute $8,264 residential; 4 weeks $11,020. $70 application fee. 2027 prices not posted.

who_can_apply: At least 16 by the start date (June 8 in 2026) and a rising or graduating senior. In-person spots need U.S. citizenship or permanent residency; others may apply to a virtual-only option. You can live anywhere in the U.S., but there is no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply in the Summer Scholars application portal. Two teacher recommendation letters are required, and one must be from a STEM teacher. You cannot submit until both are in. You cannot edit after you submit. An unofficial transcript is fine.
notes: Competitive. Parents or guardians handle off-campus housing and care for students under 18. Dates shown are from the 2026 page. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16; this program starts at 16.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm (June 8 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,400 stipend if you finish the program. No program fee.

who_can_apply: High school students in Fairfax County.
how_to_apply: Email DITHR@fairfaxcounty.gov to ask how to apply.
notes: The county page has only a short note. Ask about pay, age and how to apply by email in March or April.
duration: Mid-June until a week before school starts
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 15 at the start of the course. Must pass the lifeguard course and its swim prerequisites (swim 100 yards, retrieve a 10-pound brick, tread water without hands for one minute) and a criminal background check. No prior certification needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Park Authority Aquatic Certification page, then interview. Questions: FCPAJOBS@Fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Employment is contingent on passing the course. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Part-time; hours vary by Rec Center
pay_detail: Weekday opening and midday shifts start at $15.00 per hour; weekday evenings and weekends range from $12.41 to $15.00 per hour. Training is free (listed as a $250 value).

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer guide is for adults, youth ages 12 and over, corporate groups, and people who need to fulfill a service requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator for your branch (the guide lists names and phone numbers) or use the Volunteer Login link in the library's volunteering guide.
notes: The guide does not spell out the sign-up steps for teens, so call your branch coordinator first. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: You must be a junior now in a Fairfax County public school. You should be doing well in class. You should care about local government. You cannot also do the Governor School Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send one letter of support. It can come from a teacher, scout leader, boss or someone like that.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 4 to 6 pm starting in February. You get yourself to meetings and the internship. Questions: DMBYLP@fairfaxcounty.gov or 703-324-4062. Page does not give the internship year; it is July 2027 for this class.
duration: Monthly meetings from Feb 2027 plus a 3-week internship in July (40 hours per week)
pay_detail: $1,000 for completing the 3-week internship

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. You must be legally allowed to work in the U.S. You must be getting services from a referring group or the WIOA Youth Program. You must want to find work. You must be able to work at least 20 hours a week and go to the workshops.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply alone. A sponsoring group or the WIOA Youth Program picks you. Email DFSEYE@fairfaxcounty.gov or see vcwnorthern.com/eye-programs/ to find a referring organization.
notes: Referral only. The county page also lists a WIOA Youth program for ages 17 to 24 who are out of school or close to graduating. In summer 2026, 133 youth worked with 100 local employers. Virginia work permit rules were not checked.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students in the Commonwealth of Virginia.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the ACCESS Academy page when it opens again. If you have questions, write to Dr. Roberto Pamas. He is the ACCESS Academy Director. His email is rpamas@gmu.edu.
notes: Held at Fuse at Mason Square, 3401 Fairfax Dr, Arlington, VA. It filled up in 2026, so apply early next year.
duration: One week, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily (2026 sessions: July 13-17, July 20-24, July 27-31)
pay_detail: No cost to students. Lunch provided daily. You provide your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students. No coding, health care or technology experience is required.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Fill out the Future Programs Interest Form on the camp page to get updates. Contact: Maria Uriyo, muriyo@gmu.edu.
notes: This is a day camp at George Mason University's Fairfax campus, 4400 University Drive, Fairfax, VA 22030. Not a job.
duration: 5 days, 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. each day
pay_detail: The camps list at Mason says it is a free, five day program. The camp page itself does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who like leadership, making peace, community work or social sciences. Students come from all over the country.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. If you are admitted, you get steps to sign up and pay a deposit. For a scholarship, check the box. Then send a personal statement and your parents' most recent 1040 tax form.
notes: Contact: Averi Jordan, ajorda22@gmu.edu. In 2026, 63 students went to the summit.
duration: Four days, overnight (page lists July 25 to 29 for Summer 2027)
pay_detail: $1,390 without college credit, or $1,500 with 1 college credit. Scholarship review is possible.

who_can_apply: High school students (GMU's camps list says ages 13 to 17). Virginia applicants must go to certain schools. Students whose family income is under 400% of the federal poverty level get priority. The researcher track is for students with no research experience. It is also for students with few health chances at school.
how_to_apply: Send the online application form. Allow about 14 days for email replies. Some applicants are interviewed. Send questions to the program director, Jonathan Sanchez. His email is jsanche@gmu.edu.
notes: The page also mentions that acceptances begin July 1, 2026. That does not fit with the December deadline. Check the timeline with the director.
duration: Spring 2027 cohort starting Jan 20, 2027 (details to be decided); year-long track for fellows and interns
pay_detail: Free. 100% virtual.

who_can_apply: Fall 2026 classes by age: 9 to 17 for 2D art, 11 to 17 for Unity, 13 to 17 for advanced Python (needs prior programming). Younger-only classes run in Manassas. Typing and basic computer skills expected.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the MGTA page when registration opens for a class.
notes: Not a job or internship. Listed because it is a real university program for teens in tech and game design. Check the page for the next session.
duration: Fall 2026: six Saturdays 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at Fairfax; summer classes are five days, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: $595 per fall class. Scholarships page exists but gives no details.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The page itself says rising juniors, so use the page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.
duration: 3 days, 2 nights
pay_detail: Free for selected students. Overnight students get two nights of dorm housing, meals and a daily snack. A limited number of day-only slots exist. You arrange your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page (wjmc.gmu.edu/register). Scholarship details are at wjmc.gmu.edu/scholarships/. A Nominate link is also on the site.
notes: Check the cost and deadlines with the program before you apply.
duration: One week (July 11 to 16 or July 18 to 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the program pages. A scholarship is offered.

who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page on the WYSE site, or have someone submit a nomination (wsp.gmu.edu/nominate). Call 703-993-5010 for cost and deadlines.
notes: The site shows a Register button for the June 27 to July 2, 2027 session, but the page does not say whether registration is open. Confirm the status and cost with the program before applying.
duration: One week (June 27 to July 2, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Ask the program: 703-993-5010.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. You must finish a county volunteer orientation and a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Make a profile at volunteer.fairfaxcounty.gov and search the word NCS. Apply to openings. Go to an NCS Volunteer Orientation and pass the background check. Email ncs-volunteers@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: The page has no teen-only section or list of teen roles, so ask the volunteer office what is open for 13 to 17 year olds. The phone number printed on the page has a non-Virginia area code; use the email.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are 16 by the first day of class and meet dual enrollment readiness (for example a 3.0 GPA, or set test scores). Needs a current high school transcript and parent e-consent. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply to NOVA for the summer term. Then fill out the Dual Enrollment Portal form in myNOVA. You pick courses, upload papers and get a parent to say yes online. Contact DualEnrollment@nvcc.edu or 703-503-6291.
notes: Selection is by lottery. The page shows 2026 dates; check in March for 2027.
duration: Six weeks, Mon and Wed 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (June 22 to July 29 in 2026)
pay_detail: No tuition or pay listed. Textbooks are free, lunch is provided, parking pass for drivers. You arrange your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Any teen aged 14 to 17. Rec-PAC school sites have no interview; camp sites at Rec Centers and parks need an interview.
how_to_apply: Rec-PAC school sites: fill out the application and return it to the Rec-PAC office. Rec Center and park camp sites: contact the site for an interview. All CITs attend a 3-hour training and pass a knowledge test.
notes: This FAQ page looks old. It links to 2019 Rec-PAC sites. Check the fee, dates and deadline with the Park Authority at 703-324-8700 before you apply.
duration: At least one week encouraged, up to the full summer; school sites run 8:15 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts as volunteer hours. The FAQ lists a $160 fee for the whole summer at school-based Rec-PAC sites.

who_can_apply: High school age girls in Northern Virginia (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: For girls only. Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to go to all classes. Not a job.
duration: Summer weekdays
pay_detail: Free of charge. Transportation help is offered case by case.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 20 who like the idea of a career in law enforcement. There are four units. They are the Criminal Justice Academy (Chantilly), West Potomac High School, Annandale High School and South Lakes High School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Public Safety Cadets interest form on the page. The page also links an application. It links a waiver. It links a recommendation form. Email fcpdpsc@fairfaxcounty.gov with questions.
notes: An older Fairfax County police page called these units Explorer posts. They had the same unit numbers. That page no longer loads. Ask the cadet email about the current rules, such as citizenship, grades and costs. The page links an application, a waiver and a recommendation form.
duration: Ongoing unit membership
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs for uniforms or gear are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Fairfax County high school age students (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Police Academy application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to attend all classes. Not a job.
duration: Summer weekdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Transportation help is offered case by case.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.
duration: One year, June 1 to May 31, at least 45 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time $50 fee after acceptance, which can be waived for those who qualify.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 16 (age counted on September 1 of the 4-H year). You do not have to be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It names the camp and the weeks you want. Upload a resume. List two adults as references. They do not have to be from 4-H.
notes: Apply to Camp Cloverleaf, Camp Timpoochee or both. Weekly themes and prices are on each camp's page. Teens pay the camp fee, so this is not a paying job.
duration: At least 1 camp week, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Junior counselors pay the full early bird camp fee for each week they attend. They can apply for state camp scholarships.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Your age is counted on September 1. You can also stay until you finish high school.
how_to_apply: Call your county Extension office. Then join online in 4-H Online. Paper forms are also available.
notes: State events include iLEAD and 4-H University Legislature Day at the Capitol. Florida has three 4-H camps: Cherry Lake, Cloverleaf and Timpoochee. You do not have to be a member to go to their summer camps.
duration: 4-H year runs Sept 1 to Aug 31
pay_detail: $20 per year for community club members ages 8 to 18. Some counties charge a different amount.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. At least four hours a week. Some sites are full; check the list on the page.
how_to_apply: Step 1: online volunteer orientation. Step 2: online application. Step 3: contact them to set up an interview. Call 407-543-4047.
notes: Pick a location that is accepting applications. The internships on the same page are for college students getting credit, not high school.
duration: At least 4 hours a week, flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. Competitive. Two full 8 hour days a week for the summer term (June 1 to July 31 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Send in a form with a video. Also send in a recommendation form. A Level 2 background check is required.
notes: Parents are asked to let the teen be the main contact. Fingerprint fees are reimbursed for those who finish. Max 3 excused absences.
duration: Summer term, 2 days a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Broward County students ages 16 to 18. You must be able to work in the US and have a valid ID. Your family must meet the income rule (economically disadvantaged). Picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window is open. Income and a random lottery decide who gets in. Chosen youth get a packet by mail and go to training.
notes: Funded mainly by the Children's Services Council of Broward County. Remote work is not offered. Next year dates are not posted, so check the page in winter.
duration: About 8 weeks, June to early August
pay_detail: $14 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 (13 by the first June class). Must apply, interview, attend multi day training and pass a final exam.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form when it opens in February. Attach 3 papers. Then interview.
notes: Teens are expected to handle their own email and schedule. Volunteer Office: 407-323-4450 ext. 127.
duration: Training in June; volunteering on weekends and school breaks
pay_detail: Unpaid; $30 fee for training materials and uniform

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and up. Must attend at least 5 of 6 sessions and volunteer 6 hours a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen form with a letter of commitment. Contact Simone Crawley, 727-623-4731.
notes: Hours may count toward service requirements; ask the museum.
duration: 6 weeks (June 7 to July 23 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free; unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students on a team from a school, homeschool group, 4-H group or nature center group. A full team has 5 competing members. The team registration fee covers up to 2 advisors. Each county sends one team.
how_to_apply: Join your regional contest first. Regional leaders sign up the winning teams. Then advisors finish signing up and pay.
notes: The key dates page is titled 2026 but lists an April 2027 contest, so confirm the year with organizers. Teams of 4 or fewer can take part but not compete for places.
duration: 1 day state contest
pay_detail: $300 per team, flat rate.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16. You like botany, plant biology, ecology or gardening. It is run through the Miami-Dade County Public Schools Summer Youth Internship Program. Only Miami-Dade public school students get school credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add 1 letter of recommendation from a science teacher.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Look for a similar spring deadline. Recent undergraduate and graduate internships on the same page are not for high schoolers.
duration: 5 weeks (July 1 to Aug 2 in 2026)
pay_detail: Stipend at the end of the program (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in an agriculture course at their school. Joining a chapter in a nearby school district is a state and local decision.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher to enroll you in an agriculture course. Use the Chapter Locator on the site.
notes: For overnight events, an advisor or an adult your school approves must come with students. You also need a permission form and a medical form. Event fees pay for lodging and meals at most events.
duration: School year
pay_detail: National dues $7 per year plus state dues $10 per year. Local chapters may add dues.

who_can_apply: Miami-Dade County Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 16 years old. Upward Bound Math and Science (UBMS) students apply first; other students can be accepted if they agree to join UBMS. Applicants must be willing to get a scuba certification.
how_to_apply: Use the Join the Program link on the Your Shores page to start the application. The page lists no deadline.
notes: The page shows Saturdays from September 23 to May 25 with no year, so confirm dates with the museum. A medical checklist form and swim requirements apply. The page says participants earn a stipend but gives no amount.
duration: Saturdays, September to May
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Camp Registration Portal linked from the camp page, or call the camp at 561-624-6929.
notes: Paid camp staff jobs at this center need you to be at least 19, so this camp is the teen route. Address: 12100 Seminole Pratt Whitney Road, West Palm Beach, FL.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: The camp lists programs from $400 to $515 per week. The Leadership Camp price is not listed separately on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and 17 who apply and are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the leadership camp application on the camp page. Then follow the steps to contact the camp. You only sign up online if you are accepted.
notes: The camp address is 7325 NE 170th Ave, Silver Springs, FL. Phone 352-625-2804. The page does not name the year of the listed weeks, so confirm 2027 dates.
duration: 1 week or more
pay_detail: $200 per week. 40 Service Learning Credits are awarded for each week.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 for the Hooked on Conservation and Paddle Adventure weeks. Age is counted on the first day of the camp week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Camp Registration Portal. No payment is due until you get a spot. Payment is due 14 days after you are told you have a spot.
notes: Capacity is 20 per teen week, so spots go fast. Address: 6650 Dickman Rd, Apollo Beach, FL. Phone 813-922-7961.
duration: 1 week day camp
pay_detail: Camp price is not stated on the program page. Limited scholarships: email Suncoast@MyFWC.com. A $25 non-refundable deposit applies.

who_can_apply: High school seniors at schools that partner with Genesys Works. The page says the Jacksonville program works with Duval County Public Schools to recruit students. The first Jacksonville class launched in 2025. The page does not state a pay rate.
how_to_apply: Start on the Genesys Works application page. Choose Jacksonville. Interview. Then confirm your spot for summer training.
notes: The page says the Jacksonville program works with Duval County Public Schools to recruit students. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The first Jacksonville class launched in 2025.
duration: 8 weeks training (summer) then a year long internship
pay_detail: Paid internship (rate not stated on the program pages)

who_can_apply: At least 16, or part of a pre approved group such as scouts or 4-H. You provide your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Pick the volunteer form that fits the park or role and send it in. To coach, contact the rec center directly.
notes: Scouts can use the Scout Project Application. Camp host applications for fall and winter 2026-27 will only be considered for spring and summer 2027.
duration: Flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Duval County residents ages 16 to 21 who are in school (22 for youth with special needs). Or ages 16 to 24 who are out of school and not working or at risk of being cut off from school and work.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the MYAWP page to open the candidate portal. The page says the student application closed August 19 at 11:59 pm, and it does not list session dates.
notes: The page says demand is expected to be higher than the slots. Business interest form deadline was September 11.
duration: Sessions through the year (fall 2026 session listed)
pay_detail: Paid internship (rate and hours not stated on the page)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18. Everyone must pass the City background screening, which may include fingerprints. The page says there are more applicants than openings.
how_to_apply: Look at the openings on the volunteer page. Apply online. Staff will email you the next steps.
notes: Not everyone who applies is picked. Group volunteering: JPLVolunteers@coj.net. Teen specific openings are listed on a teen page that was not read.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens currently in high school, ages 14 to 18 when they enter the program. Apply, interview and be picked. Not all applicants are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form in the November window. Interview. Go to the required training.
notes: The page gives the Nov 1 to Nov 25 window as the pattern each year. It does not say the exact 2026 dates are for that year.
duration: Year round: 30 hours fall, 30 spring, 80 summer
pay_detail: Unpaid; $100 annual fee for badge, shirt and materials (financial help available, nobody turned away)

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. Ages 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian signature. Photo ID is required.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch you want. Meet the Volunteer Coordinator or Branch Manager. Then send in the Volunteer Application/Agreement. A free fingerprint background check follows.
notes: The page says students can earn community service hours for graduation. The branch manager must approve your spot.
duration: Flexible, set with your branch
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders ages 15 to 18 enrolled in a Miami-Dade County Public School. Apply through your school champion. Students must complete the online pre-internship course.
how_to_apply: Finish the first steps, including the online class before the internship. Talk to your teacher champion at school. Hotline: 305-693-3005.
notes: Students may earn school credit if they pass the review and finish their work. The page says to check back for 2027 sign up details.
duration: 5 weeks (July 1 to Aug 2 in 2026), at least 30 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid by stipend (amount not stated on the program pages); students open an EdFed Credit Union account for direct deposit

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at any Jacksonville high school. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application when it opens. Required: two Family Day volunteer shifts. Meetings are the first and third Wednesday of each month from 5 to 6:30 pm.
notes: Past members earned upwards of 40 service hours. Members must volunteer at two Family Day events, with dates to be announced.
duration: September to April, first and third Wednesday, 5 to 6:30 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer hours (past members earned 40 or more)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. You must be able to work on your own. Supervisors cannot always be there.
how_to_apply: It is not open now. To ask when 2027 forms open, call Volunteer Coordinator Amy Hester at 352-273-2055. Or send an email to volunteers@floridamuseum.ufl.edu.
notes: Return for Summer 2027 is hoped for, not promised. Confirm before planning around it.
duration: Summer; selected teens may also serve in the school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth must be at least 14 and have completed 8th grade. Adult weekday session volunteers must be 18; teens use individual postings and one time events.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the volunteer page. No application is needed for the one time events.
notes: The museum only signs volunteer hours for students who are 14 (going into high school) or older.
duration: One time events (a few hours) and posted openings
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: North Miami residents ages 15 to 18 at the time of appointment, in grades 10 to 12, with at least a 2.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume, school transcript, a minor participation form, a photo and video form, and 2 short answers (200 words each).
notes: The next cycle is not posted. Contact Library Director Paul Bazile, 305-891-5535.
duration: School year term (length not stated)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students in Orange County. Age and grade rules vary by event. Check with your branch.
how_to_apply: Register for an event at a participating branch. Questions: AskOCLS@ocls.org or 407-835-7323.
notes: Advisory boards give 1 hour of service for each monthly online meeting. For the literary magazine you must send in work to get hours.
duration: Events and monthly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours (up to 2 hours per event)

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You need a reliable ride and must pass background and drug screens. You must be free to work the whole summer. You must pass a swim test (200 yards, tread water 2 minutes, get a 10 pound brick).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a certification class, take the swim test on day one, finish all days, then fill out the summer job application at the end of class. HR then sets up a background check and drug screening (can take up to 3 weeks).
notes: Bring a government ID and Social Security card to class, per the page. Call 407-246-4090. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Certification classes over several days (January to May); then the summer season
pay_detail: $15 to $17 an hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17, per the center. The page says applications for the 2026-2027 school year have closed.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it opens (it opens about twice a year, for Summer and School Year). Questions: volunteer@osc.org.
notes: The center says volunteering here meets most middle school and high school community service rules. Questions: volunteer@osc.org.

who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who face barriers to education, training or employment. Both in-school and out-of-school youth are served. The page does not list the exact barriers or income rules.
how_to_apply: The state pages give no application steps. They give no list of local offices. Use the contact page at tcsg.edu or the WorkSource Georgia portal (worksourcegaportal.com). Find your local office there.
notes: The pages do not say how to enroll. A call to your local WorkSource office is the real next step. The services page says the Occupational Skills part is for ages 18 to 24. So 14 to 17 year olds would use the other services. Atlanta area teens may also see the city and county programs listed separately in this guide.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free to join. The services page lists paid and unpaid work experiences, but the program pages give no pay rate.

who_can_apply: High school and undergraduate students. Minimum age 15 by Jun 18, 2026 for remote or computer-lab internships and 16 for in-person wet-lab internships. No minimum GPA; transcripts are not requested.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement; interested mentors interview strong candidates and offers go out in early April. Request a fee waiver code from cosassip@gmu.edu if needed.
notes: Labs are at the Fairfax campus, the Science and Technology Campus in Manassas, or Woodbridge; students arrange their own transportation and campus housing cannot be arranged for minors. This is a paid-by-the-student internship, not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 8 weeks, full time (Jun 18 to Aug 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: Exceptionally talented high school juniors and seniors. You need a non-degree application and fee. You need your official high school transcript. You need permission from your high school counselor or administrator. Non-native English speakers must meet the English proficiency rule.
how_to_apply: Complete the Non-Degree application. Send your high school transcript. Send your counselor or administrator's permission. Fairfax County Public Schools and Loudoun County Public Schools students can use the school partnership pages. These are for math and science dual enrollment.
notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.
duration: One semester at a time, up to 11 lower-level credits
pay_detail: An application fee and college course costs apply. The amounts are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. The program is built for young people who face barriers to work, such as low income, foster care, homelessness, disability, teen parenting or a record. The page lists no formal rules.
how_to_apply: Email youth@ging.org. The page lists 404-420-9900 as the general Goodwill number, not a program line.
notes: Address on the page: 2201 Lawrenceville Hwy, Suite 300, Decatur, GA 30033. Career centers listed: Athens, Cornelia, Decatur, Duluth, Oakwood, Smyrna and Woodstock. The page does not say which counties are served, so ask when you email. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16. This program starts at 16.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The page does not give a wage.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents in a public, private, charter or home school in Georgia, in the class of 2027, 2028 or 2029, who are 16 by April 4, 2027 (no exceptions). Proof of U.S. citizenship or U.S. person status is required for most positions. You need your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online pre-application. It has a resume (PDF), a personal statement and a letter of recommendation. It must be 100% complete before it closes. You can join the 2027 contact registry for updates. Email support.hsi.stem@gtri.gatech.edu with questions.
notes: No weekend, after hours or remote work. Housing is not provided. Do not send unsolicited emails or calls to GTRI employees about internships. The page asks this. Finishing the pre-application does not guarantee a job. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This internship requires age 16 by April 4, 2027.
duration: Five weeks, about June 14 to July 23, 2027; up to 24 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not on the page.

who_can_apply: Gwinnett County residents or students who go to school in Gwinnett County, ages 15 to 21. You must be 15 by the first workshop. You must be free for the whole paid internship program. You need a reliable ride. You cannot be a past Empower Gwinnett County Government intern. No grades or work experience are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the posted window. A form link is on the program page. Human Resources picks applicants based on interests, career goals and department needs. No interview is required. Selected applicants get a conditional job offer. Some jobs may need a background check.
notes: The main page says the 2026 application is closed. It says the 2027 dates will be posted there. Questions: HREmployeeEngagement@GwinnettCounty.com.
duration: 2 Saturday workshops plus 4 weeks (June)
pay_detail: $15 per hour for the two workshops and the four-week internship

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who live in Gwinnett County and will be in 7th through 12th grade as of August. Everyone must pass an application process.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the page to reach the youth academy application. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page names no season or week for the sessions and gives no age range. The only date given is the May 29, 2026 application deadline, so confirm the week before planning. Season is set to summer only because the deadline is in May. Unpaid program, so no work permit. Only the general county number 770.822.8000 is listed.
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm
pay_detail: Free. The page says the academy is free.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 to 18 years old and go to a Gwinnett County public school. Case by case, the program may approve school outside Gwinnett County. You must be in good standing in your school and community.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. The parent and the student both sign it online. Go to orientation. Turn in a recommendation from a teacher, a school leader or a community leader.
notes: The page does not say whether it pays, how long it lasts or what the exact opening date is. No essay is mentioned. County phone: 770.822.8000.
duration: Length not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page says participants can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. The page says the minimum age is 13 with parental permission required. Homework help covers students in grades K to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form from the Apply Online button on the volunteer page. List the branches you want. If you are a GCPS student, use a personal or parent email, not a school email.
notes: The background check on the page applies only to volunteers 18 and older. Open spots vary by branch.
duration: 40 hours over 6 to 12 months, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to be a certified lifeguard. You can start the prerequisites (an in-water skills test) at 15. Lifeguard I or II jobs need a current lifeguard training certificate by hire date.
how_to_apply: 1. Contact a year-round aquatic center and schedule the In-Water Skills Test. 2. Get certified in lifeguard, first aid and CPR/AED through the American Red Cross course. 3. Apply for the position online at GwinnettCountyJobs.com.
notes: Course costs are not listed, so ask. Email Lifeguard@GwinnettCounty.com or call 770.822.8000. The page does not mention work permits. The season is listed as part-time seasonal, with no months given.
duration: Part-time seasonal jobs at the county's year-round aquatic centers and seasonal pools. Dates are not listed.
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: The page and form do not list an age. The form asks for your school, grade and a parent or guardian signature, and asks about teen leadership training. Accepted aides must pass a background check and fingerprinting.
how_to_apply: Download the Summer Camp Aide Volunteer Application from the Day Camps page. Fill it out with a parent or guardian. Email it to CommunityServices@GwinnettCounty.com or Parks@GwinnettCounty.com, or drop it off at the camp site you want. Use a separate form for each camp site.
notes: Day camps are for children ages 5 to 13. The minimum age for aides is not stated, so call 770.822.8000 to check. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Minimum of two weeks, picked from camp weeks between late May and July 31
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. $21 for two required camp t-shirts, paid after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who have finished 8th grade and have a clean record. Open to youth interested in law enforcement.
how_to_apply: Pay the sign-up fee and do an interview. Contact the Community Affairs Section to start.
notes: Sponsored by Learning for Life. Contact Cpl. Juan Reyes at 678.442.6520 or PDCommunityAffairs@GwinnettCounty.com. Community Affairs Section: 3125 Satellite Boulevard, Duluth, GA 30096. The page has no Explorer page of its own. Details come from the outreach programs page.
duration: Three Mondays a month, 6:30 to 9:00 pm, at the Police Training Center in Lawrenceville
pay_detail: One-time registration fee of $61. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students who will attend a Gwinnett high school the next school year. No ages or grades are listed. You must get yourself to the Gwinnett Justice and Administration Center in Lawrenceville and other program sites.
how_to_apply: There is an Application link on the page. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not list exact dates, ages or the application steps. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Friday afternoons over the summer
pay_detail: Free to students

who_can_apply: The county page and flyer say the program is open to high school, undergraduate and graduate students. No ages or grade rules are listed in what was read.
how_to_apply: Find the listings and apply at VolunteerGwinnett.net. You can also call 770.822.7955. Or write to VolunteerGwinnett@GwinnettCounty.com.
notes: The VolunteerGwinnett.net listings page would not open because of a certificate error. So the open jobs, ages and hours were not read. Ask about the minimum age before you apply. The county page names Muriam Nafees as the contact for volunteer internships.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer internship. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who can work on their own and keep a weekly schedule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeen application (a PDF on the page). Go to the orientation meeting, which is required. Ask your local library for details.
notes: The plan differs by library branch.
duration: Weekly schedule; varies by library
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Not stated on the main page
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 by the start of the session, interested in a healthcare career, and able to attend every session date. Needs a 250-word written response, background check, TB screening, MMR, varicella and Tdap proof, an interview with a parent, an in-person orientation and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Register during the window through the 'High school students register here' link on Inova's student page. Spots are assigned by lottery, one entry per applicant, and the student handles all email.
notes: Mandatory student-and-parent info meetings are in mid-November 2026 and orientations in late December 2026 (dates differ by hospital; one of each is required). Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 4 to Jun 20, 2027; 1 shift per week, 3 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 18 (students in 6th grade or older). Boards meet at Central (1st Monday, 5 pm), Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial and Northside; Crozet is full and Gordon Avenue is not currently running.
how_to_apply: Use the Join a Teen Advisory Board page or contact your branch. The page does not say how to apply beyond that.
notes: Meeting times: Greene 1st Tuesday 4-5 pm; Louisa 3rd Thursday 3:45 pm; Nelson 2nd Thursday 4-5 pm; Northside 2nd Monday 7-8 pm. Gordon Avenue's entry on the teen volunteers page says its board is accepting applications while the TAB page says it is not currently running; call the branch.
duration: One meeting a month

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. Teen volunteers should be able to work independently. Branches include Central, Crozet, Gordon Avenue, Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial, Northside and Scottsville.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch (Send a Message link) or email the Young Adult Services Manager through the JMRL contact form. The page does not list formal application steps.
notes: Volunteering can count toward school or club service requirements. At the time of reading, Gordon Avenue said all weekly positions were filled. JMRL's volunteer coordinator is listed as Acacia Rodgers, volunteer@jmrl.org, 434-979-7151 ext 6695.
duration: Varies by branch

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. The national site says you must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated to succeed. The program pages do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Brunswick center: 4401 Glynco Pkwy, Brunswick, GA 31525. Turner center: 2000 Schilling Ave, Albany, GA 31705. Neither center page showed a closure notice on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. That is normal for this federal program, but only enter it on the official jobcorps.gov site with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds. The Atlanta center is not listed here because its page could not be confirmed.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says it covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16 by June 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in spring 2027 for the application.
notes: Spots are limited. Other high school chances are on the hospital's For High School Students page.
duration: Summer only. No year-round roles for high schoolers.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who live in Missouri or Kansas. You go to a public or charter school. You do not need research experience. Shots must be up to date. First choice goes to students from poorer neighborhoods.
how_to_apply: Fill out the STAR 2.0 student form on the program page in the winter window.
notes: Held at 2401 Gillham Road, Kansas City, MO. You must attend the whole 6 weeks.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (2026: June 15 to July 23)
pay_detail: $2,600 stipend

who_can_apply: Any high school student in the Kansas City metro area, any art form. If picked for an interview you must be free in August.
how_to_apply: Use the form on the KemperTeens site when it opens again. Then interview in August.
notes: Meets at 4420 Warwick Boulevard, Kansas City, MO. You must get yourself to meetings and events. Page does not say which month applications open.
duration: Alternate Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., Sept to Nov and Jan to May (2026-27)
pay_detail: $100 per month stipend. Free to join.

who_can_apply: High school age students. Exact ages not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: See the volunteer page for the form when a session opens. Questions: volunteer@theworldwar.org or 816-888-8115.
notes: Adults must be 19 or older for the regular program, so this is a separate youth track. Ask about the age rule.
duration: Three sessions a year: spring, summer and fall
pay_detail: Unpaid. Museum store discounts.

who_can_apply: Students from schools across Kansas City. Age or grade not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Council application form linked on the museum's teen programs page. Questions: teens@nelson-atkins.org.
notes: Teens also get $5 tickets to special exhibitions. The same page lists Teen Open Mic Nights (free, bi-monthly) and Teen Drop-In Art Making.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer experience.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 12th graders ages 14 to 19. You live and go to high school in Jackson, Clay, Platte or Cass counties in Missouri, or Johnson or Wyandotte counties in Kansas. You must meet employer hiring and work rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form. Finish the paperwork. Go to a prep workshop. Then interview at the spring hiring fair.
notes: The 2027 close date and hiring fair date are not posted yet.
duration: 5 weeks (2026: June 1 to July 2)
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Talk to the teen volunteer coordinator at your branch to ask if they have openings.
notes: Openings depend on the branch.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Current sophomores and juniors with at least a 3.0 GPA. You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. You must like a health job (nursing does not count). You must also have money or school disadvantage. Family income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty line.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STAHR form. Send a transcript with unweighted GPA. Send 1 professional recommendation through the online reference form (letters are not accepted). Questions: stahr@umkc.edu, 816-235-6169.
notes: Questions: stahr@umkc.edu or 816-235-6169.
duration: 2026: June 8 to July 17, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus August to April
pay_detail: Free. Students who meet expectations get a stipend, a scholarship, or both. Amounts not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in 8th to 12th grade at the time of application. Seniors can join for the summer season only. Mature, responsible teens who like working with the public and care about animals.
how_to_apply: Apply online for a pathway when applications open. See the zoo's VolunTEEN page.
notes: The zoo page says applications open November 2026. Exact dates are not posted.
duration: May through April. Three seasons: summer, fall, spring.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Trailblazers need 60 hours in summer and 18 hours each in fall and spring.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 and enrolled in high school or an equivalent program. Parent or guardian written permission is in the application. No drugs, underage drinking or gang ties, and you must pass a background check (a waiver may be allowed for past minor offenses). Cadets who join before 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Go to a weekly meeting. You learn about the program and meet the officer mentors. You can pick up an application there.
notes: Contact Officer David Buchanan, dbuchanan@kennesaw-ga.gov, 770-424-8274. Kennesaw Police, 2529 J O Stephenson Ave, Kennesaw, GA 30144. The page does not give a meeting day or time, so call first. Not a paid job.
duration: Weekly meetings. Day and time are not listed.
pay_detail: Volunteer program. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Kentucky 4-H teens in 8th grade and up (2026 listing). Sign up through your county Extension office.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Conference Registration Form. Turn it in to your county Extension office by the deadline. You must be in Kentucky 4-H through 4-H Online.
notes: Details come from the Meade County Extension listing for the state event. The Kentucky 4-H leadership page names the Teen Conference but gives no details. Scholarships are not mentioned there; ask your county office.
duration: 4 days (June 2 to 5, 2026)
pay_detail: $300 per person (2026)

who_can_apply: Kentucky youth ages 9 to 18.
how_to_apply: Join through 4-H Online. Call your local Extension office. You must be signed up to join programs.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. Fees are not listed on the page. The four 4-H camps are Feltner, Lake Cumberland, West Kentucky and North Central.
duration: Program year Sept 1 to Aug 31
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in at least one agriculture course. The page says members are 12 to 21.
how_to_apply: Use the Chapter Locator on kyffa.org or ask your ag teacher. Phone 502-564-3472.
notes: 25,178 members in 186 chapters (per the page). Dues are not stated.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current Kentucky residents in 11th grade who plan to return to a Kentucky school. You must have taken the ACT, PSAT or SAT in grades 9 to 11. Public, private, parochial and homeschool students can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school or district with the online student form. Home school students should contact the GSP office. Applications are read without names. Each school or district can send a set number based on its junior class size.
notes: The deadline_iso shown is the earlier of the two deadlines. Ask your school counselor which one applies to you. Scholars agree to stay all five weeks and may leave campus for one Family Day. Leaving early means no certificate.
duration: 5 weeks (June 19 to July 23, June 20 to July 24, or June 27 to July 31, 2027)
pay_detail: Free for selected students. The state and donors cover tuition, room, board and most supplies. Families pay for travel to the program and spending money. A refundable residence deposit is required.

who_can_apply: Current high school or home school sophomores and juniors. You live in Kentucky, go to school in Kentucky, or have a parent or guardian who works in Kentucky.
how_to_apply: Create an Acceptd account and open an application for your art form. Part 1 collects your two recommenders and Part 2 has your materials and answers. Finalists do a final round audition or review.
notes: Dates may change, says the timeline page. Final auditions are held in person at Northern Kentucky University. Some are online. Email gsainfo@kentuckyperformingarts.org with questions. Or call 502-566-5192. The $35 or $50 application fee and the free or reduced lunch fee waiver are not on the GSA pages checked; confirm the fee with the GSA team before paying.
duration: 3 weeks, June 6 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to the student. Application fee is $35 for one art form or $50 for two. The fee can be waived for students who get free or reduced lunch.

who_can_apply: Any middle or high school student interested in science.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the yearly meeting of the Kentucky Academy of Science. K-12 Junior Academy students pay $0. Send in a short summary of your research. Each participant needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. High school oral presenters also upload a consent form that their school signs.
notes: High school oral presenters may be picked to go to the American Junior Academy of Science (AJAS 2027, Feb 17 to 21 in Chicago). The page says the academy will pay for sign up, travel and rooms for at least 6 students in 2027. The sign up page does not print the year. Confirm the October dates with the Academy.
duration: Two days, Nov 6 and 7, 2026 at Murray State University
pay_detail: Registration is free for K-12 Junior Academy students. Junior Academy student membership costs 5 dollars.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low-income and have at least one listed barrier. A barrier can be being behind in basic skills or having a disability. Out-of-school youth are ages 16 to 24 and need at least one listed barrier, such as having dropped out of school.
how_to_apply: Contact the youth career planner for your area. A map on the program page shows them. You can also contact any Kentucky Career Center office.
notes: This is a state overview. Kentucky has 10 local workforce areas. In-school youth must be low-income and meet a listed barrier. Out-of-school youth must meet a listed barrier. Ask the youth career planner for your area about your case.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Volunteers under 18 need a parent's approval. You must have a library card in good standing.
how_to_apply: Print the General Volunteer Application. Hand it in at the library where you want to work.
notes: The policy page says exceptions to the age 14 rule may be made for short projects such as Scout requirements. Volunteers of any age may not work at public service desks or use staff computers. In-library tasks like shelving are listed for adults only.
duration: At least 3 hours of service a month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities in the Knoxville area. They can be in high school or past it.
how_to_apply: Email Eva at eva@themuseknoxville.org to apply. A staff member makes a skills plan for each person.
notes: The same page lists the Muse Apprenticeship Program (MAP) with Business, Education and STEAM paths. It says the museum is no longer recruiting for 2026-27. It does not list ages, hours or pay.
duration: Groups come to the museum weekly. The length is not stated.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Age 14 and up for Family Fun Day. Age 16 and up for Summer Art Academy. Other volunteer roles at the museum are 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the KMA Volunteer Application PDF and email it to the Volunteer Coordinator at dmann@knoxart.org. Call 865-525-6101 with questions.
notes: The volunteer page does not describe its internships. Ask before you plan around one. The museum also runs Summer Art Academy afternoon workshops for teens 13 and up. In 2026 tuition was $170 for members and $200 for non-members, with a scholarship form.
duration: Dates are not listed
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by April 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Upload an essay of no more than 2 pages. Give at least 2 references who are not family. Incomplete forms are not considered.
notes: Volunteer meetings are a must. They are recorded and online for now. Parents and teens should read the weekly email updates. An early review does not promise an interview or a spot.
duration: At least 50 hours per calendar year
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time program fee of $50, plus you must keep a Zoo Knoxville membership (discounted, bought when you start volunteering).

who_can_apply: High school students of all levels. No ages or grades are listed.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration is open. In 2026 registration was closed and a waitlist form was on the page.
notes: Costs money, not a job. Contact doarch@kennesaw.edu. Kennesaw campus: 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144.
duration: 10 weekdays (July 6 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $1,050 for 2026. Materials for modeling and drawing are included. Scholarships are not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders for camps at the KSU Center. The Aerospace Engineering camp at the Marietta campus takes rising 6th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: The 2026 sessions are over, though the page still shows Registration Open labels. For Summer 2027 updates, fill out the contact form on the page. No 2027 dates or registration are posted.
notes: Places: KSU Center, 3333 Busbee Dr NW, Kennesaw. The Marietta campus hosts Aerospace. Contact discoveru@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6765. It costs money and is not a job. Confirm sign-up status with the team before you pay.
duration: One week per camp
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $499 for baking, AutoCAD, Chef's Master Class and Medical Skills; $399 for Adulting 101; $350 for Aerospace Engineering. Scholarships are not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade through college freshmen. The Dance Intensive is for intermediate to advanced dancers.
how_to_apply: Register on the pages for each program. They are linked from the main page. Sign-up starts November 1. Questions: arts@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6742.
notes: Not a job. The page states no cost or fee, so check each program page. The Dance, Theatre and Arts and Design intensives list no exact dates on the main page. Scholarships are not mentioned.
duration: One week for the intensives. Music camps run 3 to 6 days.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the main page. Check each program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. You must be going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in 2026-2027.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain the steps. Call 301-609-4095.
notes: The page footer lists 5 Garrett Avenue, La Plata, MD 20646. Program is for the 2026-2027 school year cycle; no 2027 dates are posted.
duration: 4 to 12 hours per week in summer
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 16 and 17 through the Minor Program. A parent must attend orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. The Volunteer Manager will email you a background check. Finish it. Then wait for an interview and orientation. Call Volunteer Coordinator Daniela Rakes at 859-230-5026.
notes: The page says volunteers must be 18, or 16 for the Minor Program. Ask the coordinator which jobs minors can do and whether the barns are open to them.
duration: No minimum hours. Barn shifts run 8:30 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:30. Park representative shifts run 9:00 to 1:00 and 1:00 to 5:00.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school youth. The council is always accepting new members.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Register for the Neighborhood Youth Council form and list your school so you get its meeting schedule. Council Ambassadors also meet outside school hours.
notes: The page lists 2 phone numbers, 859-280-8004 and 859-280-8006. Confirm which one to call. There are 4 elected roles. They are Council Ambassador, Secretary, Treasurer and Parliamentarian.
duration: Meetings at each high school during school hours
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Anyone age 14 or older. Volunteers ages 14 to 17 need permission from a parent or guardian. The parent or guardian also signs the application online.
how_to_apply: Use the online volunteer form. Have a parent or guardian sign it. Then do a screening with the Volunteer Coordinator, an orientation and any training for your role.
notes: Background checks apply to volunteers 18 and older. The page has no separate teen program.
duration: Agreed when you are accepted. Teen roles may need less time.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Lexington youth who will be in grade 10, 11 or 12. The page gives no age range and no more residency rules.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the online form. To get first pick for a summer job, finish the online Skills Sessions. Also go to the Career Fair, Verification Clinic, Parent Orientation and Youth Worker Orientation.
