notes: Partners for Youth is at 162 E. Main St., Suite 210, Lexington, KY 40507. Phone 859-280-8006. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. Ask the office.
duration: 6 weeks, June 14 to July 24, 2027
pay_detail: $15 per hour, up to 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: High school students at schools in districts that take part. Talk to your guidance counselor in grade 9 or 10.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor if your district takes part. Districts that want to join can email jumpstart@uky.edu.
notes: The page does not list which districts take part. The program page says students who continue at BCTC can finish a healthcare associate degree in two years or less. A UK HealthCare scholarship has a work-back agreement, but students can choose another path with no commitment.
duration: Grades 11 and 12 coursework
pay_detail: Dual-credit courses can reduce or remove the cost of college. A UK HealthCare tuition scholarship after graduation comes with a work-back commitment. Pay while in school is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who apply to the yearly summer program. Selected teens are told by mid-April.
how_to_apply: Watch the UK HealthCare volunteer page for the next form. The steps are a packet, an interview in person and health checks. Health checks are a TB risk check and blood test, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap, and a flu shot in flu season. Call Volunteer Services at 859-323-6023.
notes: The page says adults over 18 need a background check and drug screen. Teens do not. It also says volunteering here does not lead to a job in the University of Kentucky system. The office cannot offer internships or job shadowing. The page was updated Aug 3, 2026.
duration: Summer. Adult volunteers commit to at least 2 hours a week. The teen schedule is not posted.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 and up. Anyone under 18 must have a parent or a named adult with them at all times during orientation training. Youth cannot handle animals.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer account with the Become a Volunteer link on the page. Then go to orientation at a shelter with your parent or guardian.
notes: A parent or designated adult must be with you at all times through orientation. The page does not list the shelter addresses in the text read. A COVID-era section mentions remote projects for younger kids, but it may be outdated, so it is not listed here.
duration: Ongoing. Orientation first, at one of three shelter locations.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Look for teen openings in the Loudoun volunteer portal. Then send the PRCS volunteer application.
notes: Questions: 703-777-0343. Also see PRCS Connect (bit.ly/PRCSteens) for current teen programs.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens who live in Loudoun County. The page lists recruiting high schools but gives no age or grade range.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Ask through the contact form on the page or call 703-777-0343.
notes: The page does not say when applications open next year.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not listed

who_can_apply: Loudoun County high school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Send the Youth in Government Day application online. The page has a JotForm link.
notes: Held at Douglass Community Center and the Loudoun County Government Center, both in Leesburg. The page does not mention a later date.
duration: One day, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers must be at least 14 years old. You must be in school now or have graduated recently.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online junior volunteer form. If you qualify, you get an interview. You also get onboarding details. Then you meet the coordinator before you start.
notes: Call the Volunteer Office at 502.896.7388 for session start dates. The program page does not say what the oldest age is. You can join more than one session.
duration: Each session is about 7 to 8 weeks. You must serve at least 6 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older can join any shift on their own. Younger teens need a guardian. Mobile Pantry: 8 and older with a guardian. Main Distribution Center: 14 and older with a guardian, or 12 and older in a group. Community Kitchen: 15 and older with a guardian. Senior Outreach Warehouse: 12 and older with a guardian.
how_to_apply: Make an account on the Dare to Care volunteer site. Pick a shift from the calendar. Groups send a group volunteer form instead.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and a shirt that covers your shoulders. You need an account on the volunteer site if you want school service hours verified. Ask for at least 3 business days. Some shifts have a ratio of 5 volunteers under 16 to 1 adult.
duration: Shift by shift. Shift lengths are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. A teen who turns 13 during the calendar year can apply. Each teen fills out their own form. The museum cannot accept a form filled out for someone else.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Interest Form yourself. Returning volunteers sign up for weeks by email. Write to education@fraziermuseum.org.
notes: Camp dates, hours and the number of weeks are not on the program page. You only fill out the form once, even if you return in later years.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 13. The form asks for a parent name, an emergency number and a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application and choose a branch. Finish a Workers' Compensation form in person at the branch before you start. Call 574-1611 and ask for the volunteer coordinator at your branch.
notes: The page says volunteer hours may be tracked and shared with the Library Foundation. The branch phone number is listed on the page as 574-1611.
duration: Not stated. Availability choices on the form are after school and Saturdays.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 23. You must be enrolled in school full time.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link in the Chorus Volunteer Program section of the program page. You will be told about the next orientation.
notes: Call the volunteer office at 502-566-5141 with questions.
duration: Chorus volunteers give 40 hours of service per year.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the event page. A Zoom link is sent before the event.
notes: One-time online event. The event page links to a recording of the October 21, 2025 summit.
duration: One session, Oct 20, 2026, 9 to 11 a.m. Eastern, on Zoom
pay_detail: Free with registration

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must audition and be accepted before you can register.
how_to_apply: Email kyle@kyshakespeare.com to set up an audition. After you are accepted, you can register.
notes: Rehearsals are at 616 Myrtle St. Ask about scholarships on the camp page. The company also offers a camp called The Mechanicals for ages 15 to 18, which costs $195 for 1 week or $295 for 2 weeks.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday.
pay_detail: $495 for the five-week program. The camp page links to scholarship information.

who_can_apply: High school students who care about fair treatment of all people and can lead. You need good attendance, grades and conduct. You must be able to meet 2 evenings a month at the Ali Center in downtown Louisville.
how_to_apply: Students must apply, but the page does not describe the steps. Use the Contact us link on the Youth Leadership page.
notes: Past spring break trips listed on the page include Chicago, St. Louis and Washington, D.C. The fall retreat is at Camp Piomingo in Brandenburg, KY. The page says the program is free.
duration: School year, two meetings a month plus three group trips
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Forest Restoration is open to ages 18 and older, or 16 and older with adult supervision. The page lists no age rule for groundskeeping, so ask.
how_to_apply: Click the Volunteer Today button on the volunteer page. Fill out the form and sign the volunteer waiver. For teen roles, send an email to info@louisvillenaturecenter.org or call 502-458-1328.
notes: The page gives no separate hours or rules for youth. The rule for ages 16 and up with adult help applies to Forest Restoration.
duration: Forest Restoration work days: Wednesdays and Fridays (10 a.m. to 1 p.m. in warm months, 1 to 3 p.m. in cold months). Groundskeeping: Monday to Friday and most Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Pick a hospital and use its summer teen application.
how_to_apply: Choose a Norton hospital. Fill out its Summer Teen form on the Norton volunteer page. Then contact that hospital's volunteer manager.
notes: Norton Audubon, Brownsboro, Hospital, West Louisville, Women's and Children's, and Norton Children's Hospital each list a teen form for ages 14 to 17. Norton Women's and Children's also has a school year teen form. Norton Scott lists no teen program. The page says only some hospitals take teen volunteers all year. Openings are limited. The page says hospital volunteers must pass a background check and health screen. It does not say if that applies to teens.
duration: Not stated. The student program takes less time than the adult program, which asks for 6 months at 2 to 4 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Young people who live in Jefferson County. The program page says ages 16 to 19. A 2025 news post from the same group said ages 16 to 21, counted on June 1.
how_to_apply: Register at summerworks.org, finish the Job Readiness training, then apply for jobs. Create or upload a resume on the site.
notes: The two pages give different top ages (19 and 21), so check the age rule when registration opens. Pay rate, hours and work permit rules are not stated on either page. Ask the program.
duration: Summer. Length is not posted.
pay_detail: You earn a paycheck. No hourly rate is posted. Private employers pay the youth they hire directly.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16 by June 1 of the program year and have taken at least one advanced science course. You need your own bank account for pay and a way to get to the Health Science Campus each day. Students related to Brown Cancer Center faculty cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Email the form to the program coordinator. Add an unofficial transcript. Add two letters of recommendation. One is from a science teacher. Finalists are interviewed online.
notes: A faculty committee picks who is interviewed. The program page does not say where you must live. Ask the coordinator at ashley.kareken@louisville.edu. The program page lists the 2026 pay and dates. They may change.
duration: 9 weeks, at least 30 hours a week (2026: June 1 to July 31)
pay_detail: $3,500 stipend for the 2026 program. The Brown Cancer Center pays other costs.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. You need consent from a parent. You need a recommendation letter and an essay. You need shot records (2 MMR, 1 varicella) and a QuantiFERON TB blood test.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. By the deadline, send an essay (at least 1 paragraph), a letter of recommendation, consent from a parent and shot and TB records.
notes: The main volunteer page says volunteers must be 16 or older. They need a flu shot from October to April. Questions: VolunteerServices@UofLHealth.org (the program page lists no phone number).
duration: Two-week sessions. In 2026: UofL Hospital June 15 to 26 (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.), Shelbyville Hospital June 9 to 20 or July 7 to 18 (8 a.m. to 3 p.m.), Mary & Elizabeth June 16 to 27 (8 a.m. to 1 p.m.).
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Leaders-In-Training is for ages 15 to 16. Counselors-In-Training is for ages 16 to 17.
how_to_apply: Leaders-In-Training: the program page lists the sessions and price tiers. Counselors-In-Training: enrollment is by application and then an interview. A monthly payment plan and financial help are offered.
notes: This is a paid program for the teen, not a job. The program page does not name the camp town. Check the session dates before you plan, because the year is not shown.
duration: Leaders-In-Training is 2 weeks. Counselors-In-Training is 3 weeks.
pay_detail: Leaders-In-Training costs $1,515 to $1,850 and Counselors-In-Training costs $1,435 to $1,750, depending on the price tier. Kentucky sales tax of 6 percent is added. Financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old by the last day of the course.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for Lifeguard Training button to see open courses. If none are listed, call your local YMCA branch.
notes: Course sites include Norton Commons and Oldham County, plus Clark County, Floyd County and Southeast branches. The program page does not say if work papers are needed for the job. Prices can differ by location.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: The course starts at $175 for Y facility members and $225 for program members. The fee is refunded if the Y hires you as a lifeguard (hiring length rules may apply). The job pay rate is not posted.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. All volunteers need a current TB (tuberculin) skin test.
how_to_apply: The page points to the zoo's volunteer form. To ask about the teen program, send an email to the Coordinator of Volunteers at mary.taylor@louisvilleky.gov. Or call 502-459-2181.
notes: The zoo page lists no season or hours for the youth program, so the season shown is a placeholder. It also describes a separate 50-member Zoo Youth Board for students ages 13 to 18. It does not say how to join, so ask the volunteer coordinator.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: At least 14, in high school, and not yet 21. A 2.0 GPA or higher if still in high school. Must be a U.S. citizen, pass a background check, physical test and written exam, and have written parent approval if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email bmarshall@mariettaga.gov to RSVP for a meeting. Attend 4 monthly meetings in a row and fill out the welcome packet. Then you get a background check, interview and a 3-month trial.
notes: The web page says ages 14 to 21; the requirements sheet says applicants must be under 21. The web page says meetings run Thursdays 6 to 8 pm, while the requirements sheet says 6 to 9 pm, so confirm the hours.Meets at 240 Lemon Street, Marietta, GA 30060. Phone 770-794-5355 or 770-794-5300 (ask for the Community Response Unit). The sheet says the fee goes to Learning for Life, Scouts BSA. Not a paid job.
duration: Meets about 3 Thursdays a month, 6 to 9 pm. Attend at least 2 a month, plus 5 volunteer hours a month.
pay_detail: Not a paid job. You pay a yearly membership fee and buy part of the uniform. Competition travel costs up to $250 per trip.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors in Maryland public high schools. The state page does not give an age or hour rule (local school systems may add rules).
how_to_apply: Join through your high school, then apply for open positions with participating employers.
notes: More than 2,000 high school students have taken part since 2016. State office phone 410-767-2246.
duration: Part-time during high school. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Paid part-time apprentice positions. The wage is set by the employer and is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students living in the Chesapeake Bay watershed (Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Washington DC). Summer Expeditions are for rising 9th to 12th graders. No past experience needed.
how_to_apply: Use the contact form on the CBF page or call 410-268-8816. Registration for Summer Expeditions opens in early January.
notes: Earns service-learning hours at restoration events. Ask CBF about cost and scholarships for expeditions.
duration: Year-round program. Summer Expeditions last several days.
pay_detail: Not stated. Costs for Summer Expeditions are not on this page.

who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school or college, or graduated within one year of the start date. Needs a 2.5 GPA on an unofficial transcript. Postings have a high school minimum requirements section.
how_to_apply: Apply on the state jobs site (jobapscloud.com/MD). Send a state application, a resume, two letters of support from people who are not relatives and an unofficial transcript. If none are open, fill out the Internship Interest Form to get news. Contact: julie.kline@maryland.gov.
notes: Internships are posted by park, office or program. The places vary around the state.
duration: About 10 to 12 weeks (summer June to August, fall October to December)
pay_detail: Some are paid, some are volunteer. Check the Salary section of each posting.

who_can_apply: Anyone 11 or older (11-year-olds must be in sixth grade). The form has a teen option. The library has no court-ordered community service spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the library page and pick a preferred branch (Brunswick, C. Burr Artz, Emmitsburg, Middletown, Myersville, Point of Rocks, Thurmont, Urbana or Walkersville).
notes: Opportunities vary by branch. Hours and length are not posted.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from the Mid-Atlantic region. The program page gives no ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Maryland Forestry Foundation. Use the camp link on the Maryland DNR page.
notes: The only page checked was a 2025 notice. Ask the Maryland Forestry Foundation for the current dates, ages and cost.
duration: 1 week (July 20 to 26 in 2025)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees are listed on the camp website (not read). The page says Maryland students may get some costs covered.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older. Swim instructors 15 or older with teaching experience (14 or older to volunteer with no experience). Front desk aides 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply online at rockvillemd.gov/careers, then come to a hiring event or interview for a skills test (200 yard swim, 2 minute tread). Call 240-314-8750.
notes: Pay and ages are from the 2026 flyer and may change. Going to the event does not guarantee a job. Course fee discounts may be available for people who want to work for the city. Under-18 workers may need a Maryland work permit; the flyer does not say.
duration: Summer season
pay_detail: 2026 flyer: lifeguard $18.25 to $19.25, swim instructor $18.75 to $20, front desk aide $17.65 to $19.00. Uncertified lifeguards start at $18.25 after they get certified.

who_can_apply: Maryland 4-H youth who are at least 14 years old by July 1 of the fair year. You need your own ride to the fair.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 4-H Youth Worker Application. It is an online form linked on the Extension page. It asks for a letter from your county 4-H Extension Educator. Youth who are picked go to training.
notes: The job description says picked youth must apply for a minor work permit. They must also fill out federal and state job forms. Contacts: Chris Anderson, 301-314-7187, and Kevin Huang, 301-405-8105.
duration: At least four 4-hour shifts during the fair (Aug 20 to Sept 14 in 2026)
pay_detail: Hourly pay at current Maryland wage standards. Fair admission and parking passes on days worked.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 or older by Teen Boot Camp.
how_to_apply: Turn in the full application when it opens. Incomplete ones are not considered. Then go to a group interview. Questions: volunteers@marylandzoo.org or 443-552-5266.
notes: 2026 timeline from the page: selections May 28, parent orientation June 10, Boot Camp sessions June 22 to 26 and June 29 to July 3. The page text is partly inconsistent about dates, so check it when it updates. The Teens menu also lists a Keeper-in-Training Camp that was not read.
duration: At least one year: 4 shifts a month, one shift at a zoo event, and a one-week Boot Camp (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. The page mentions no fees.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application. They can be up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.

who_can_apply: The Maryland 4-H pages do not list an age range. Programs vary by county. Contact your local Extension office to learn which clubs and programs fit your age.
how_to_apply: Contact your local University of Maryland Extension office. Ask about clubs, camps and programs in your county. Then use the Enroll in Maryland 4-H link on the Join a Club page.
notes: Maryland 4-H Center: 8020 Greenmead Drive, College Park, MD 20740, 301-314-9070. The leadership page lists a 2026 Volunteer and Teen Forum in Ocean City in November 2026. It has workshops for adults and teens aged 13 and older.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: The page says costs are kept to a minimum. No amounts are given.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Boys State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. Phones, smartphones and smartwatches are not allowed. The site recommends against driving yourself because the week is tiring. Staff are mostly veterans. The page says that in most cases a sponsor pays the expenses, and students who are not sponsored should ask the program about costs.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.

who_can_apply: Students in a high school agricultural education program. The site says Maryland FFA has almost 3,000 student members in 50 chapters. Age and grade rules are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has an agricultural education program and FFA chapter. The Maryland FFA home page has a Join FFA button and a chapters page.
notes: The 2026 National FFA Convention and Expo is listed on the site for Oct 20 to 24, 2026 in Indianapolis. If your school has no FFA chapter, contact the Maryland FFA office through the Contact page.
duration: School year, ongoing
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the program pages. Ask your chapter advisor.

who_can_apply: Maryland residents who are seniors at a Maryland public or nonpublic high school and are at least 16 years old. You apply through the school you attend, not where you live.
how_to_apply: Contact your county page coordinator. The page has a list. Get the county's application and find its deadline. The Maryland page says the coordinator works with your high school.
notes: Each year 105 pages and 36 alternates are chosen from across the state. Program contact on the page: Tawana Offer, Tawana.Offer@mga.maryland.gov, 410-946-5120 (Student Programs). Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Two weeks that are not back to back during the 13-week session (second week of January to early April)
pay_detail: A meal allowance of about $50 per day worked. The Page Office arranges lodging for pages from outside Anne Arundel County who ask for it. Pages pay their own travel to Annapolis.

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Girls State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. The Girls State page lists a Samsung American Legion Scholarship event on the last day. The page says that in most cases a sponsor pays the expenses, and students who are not sponsored should ask the program about costs.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 25, 2027
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: This center is not taking students while it is paused. To ask about other Job Corps centers, make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-5627.
notes: Paused: on Oct 16, 2026 the Job Corps center list (jobcorps.gov/explore/center-locations) showed Woodstock as "Operations Paused". The Department of Labor said on Dec 19, 2024 that it would pause operations here. The center's own site still loads with no notice, so trust the national list. Call 800-733-5627 to ask about other centers. Center address: 10900 Old Court Rd, Woodstock, MD 21163. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 17. Ages 10 to 13 must come with a parent or guardian. Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. A signed parent permission form is required for all youth.
how_to_apply: Click Register on the volunteer page to pick a session. Everyone must register before arriving. Groups of 5 or fewer register one by one. Larger groups fill out the group request form.
notes: The volunteer page does not name its work site. The only address on the contact page is the Decatur headquarters at 3240 Clifton Springs Road. Confirm the site when you register. MedShare does not host court-ordered or required community service.
duration: One session at a time: Wed and Fri 9 am to noon; Thu and Sat 9 am to noon and 1 to 4 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: High school students (grades 9 to 12) with a GPA of 3.0 or above.
how_to_apply: The pages do not explain how to apply. Use the Contact Us page at cityofmemphisyouth.org or call 901-636-6264.
notes: The same office runs B.O.S.S., a mentoring program for grades 9 to 12 with no GPA rule. Students meet a mentor 2 times a week after school at community centers. The Memphis city page gives the grade range and says participants get a stipend but gives no amount. The program page gives neither.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: A monthly stipend. The amount is not posted.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older, including students. A student under 18 needs consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online request form for applicants under 18. Ask 6 to 8 weeks ahead. Email CFCD@BMHCC.ORG with questions.
notes: The page says requests for the Baptist Memorial Hospital for Women are paused until further notice. Baptist's regular volunteer program is for ages 18 and up. The page does not list which hospitals take part, so ask when you apply.
duration: At least 2 hours and no more than two full working days (24 hours)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens. The hospital's page does not list ages or grades. Regular weekly volunteers must be 18, so VolunTEEN is the teen route.
how_to_apply: Watch the Volunteer Programs page in February. Email lbvolunteers@lebonheur.org or call 901-287-5225 with questions.
notes: Ages, fee and shot requirements are not on the hospital's own pages. Ask Volunteer Services before you plan around this. Under 18 and not in VolunTEEN: the hospital points teens to one-time group volunteer events.
duration: Four sessions with eight teens in each. Session dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 of the program year.
how_to_apply: Use the program's own form, not the general volunteer form. Send 2 references from teachers or counselors. Send a consent form from a parent. Send a photo and media release. Send a copy of a birth certificate, permit or passport. Send shot records (MMR and chickenpox) and a 200 word essay. Late entries are not accepted.
notes: Send materials by email to sandra.moore@mlh.org or mail them to Volunteer Services, 1265 Union Ave., Ste. E-161, Memphis, TN 38104. Call 901-516-7481. You must complete all four weeks.
duration: 4 weeks. In 2026 orientation was June 1 and volunteering ran June 2 to 25, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: City of Memphis youth ages 14 to 22. The page does not define what counts as a Memphis resident.
how_to_apply: The program pages do not explain how teens apply. Contact the Office of Youth Services. You must show a photo ID to pick up your paycheck.
notes: Office is at 315 S Hollywood St., Memphis, TN 38104. A separate Shelby County Commissioners summer youth program exists. The county page could not be read.
duration: 6 weeks, up to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid by paper check, up to 20 hours a week. The hourly rate is not posted on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by the first day of the session.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application. Send 2 reference letters from teachers or counselors. Send your last report card. Send a 500 word essay on why you like health services. Also send a Confidentiality Agreement and the Commitment Standards. Everything must be in or you will not be considered.
notes: Mail the papers to Teenteer Volunteer Program, Regional One Health, 877 Jefferson Ave., Memphis, TN 38103. Or scan and email them. Call Volunteer Services at 901-545-7247.
duration: One session, the week of June 2 to 4 in 2026 (June 3 was a half day)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students who will be sophomores, juniors or seniors.
how_to_apply: Applications are not open yet. If you want to know more, send an email to summeracademy@rhodes.edu.
notes: Students pick 1 class and go to 2 sessions a day. The program page lists a cost of $2900 with room and board. It says aid is available. Signing up by April 15 gives a $200 discount. The page prints a 2026 session (June 21 to July 2, 2026) next to the 2027 dates. Confirm the year with summeracademy@rhodes.edu.
duration: 2 weeks in June 2027 (residential)
pay_detail: Cost is not posted on the page. Ask summeracademy@rhodes.edu.

who_can_apply: For grades 5 to 12. Performance and production students must audition. Stax 101 students do not have to audition.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online sign up form. Performance students give a 2 song audition, a music theory test and an interview. Production students send an MP3 of their own music plus the theory test and interview. To get a discount, send proof of income after you sign up.
notes: It costs money. The academy says it serves area youth, even if they can not pay. For questions, send an email to smaprogramming@staxmusicacademy.org or call 901-942-7627.
duration: August to May (after-school), or June (summer)
pay_detail: Tuition: $1,250 per year for the after-school program (August to May) and $750 for the Summer Music Experience (June). Need-based discounts and merit scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Other rules are not posted.
how_to_apply: The pages do not explain how to apply. Use the Contact Us page at cityofmemphisyouth.org or call 901-636-6264.
notes: The city's youth services page says the program gives youth in grades 9 to 12 a chance to take part. The MYCC page says it aims to lift up young voices. Meeting times, stipend and timing are not posted.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Teens must be 11 or older. Volunteering is during the school year, with extra hours in summer for the Summer Reading Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Missouri youth ages 14 to 18 (age range from the Get Involved page; the program page itself does not state age).
how_to_apply: Answer short essay questions. Have two reference forms sent in. One is from 4-H staff or faculty. One is from a teacher, coach, boss or mentor.
notes: Cost is not stated. Contact 4hyouth@missouri.edu or 573-882-9359.
duration: One calendar year starting at State Congress
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current Missouri 4-H members in grades 9 to 12. You need a recommendation from 4-H staff. Time on State Council or a national trip is a plus, not a must.
how_to_apply: Online application with three 250 to 300 word essays and one reference form from 4-H staff (not a family member). Finalists do a Zoom interview.
notes: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot. The page says it is held in even-numbered years, so the next one would be March 2028.
duration: 3 days (March 4 to 6, 2026)
pay_detail: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot.

who_can_apply: Missouri youth, per the 4-H program page. SPIN clubs take ages 5 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use Join 4-H and Enroll now on the program page, or contact your county 4-H office. Statewide questions: 4hyouth@missouri.edu, 573-882-9359.
notes: Costs are not listed on the page.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who live in Missouri. Your household must meet the income limit (for example, gross monthly income of $2,413 or less for a household of 1, $4,109 for 3, $4,957 for 4).
how_to_apply: Call and ask for a Youth Specialist at your regional workforce board. Examples listed: Full Employment Council in Kansas City 816-471-2330 ext. 1256, St. Louis City 314-657-3557, Workforce Development Board of St. Louis County 314-615-6010.
notes: Income limits come from the page and may change. The page lists regional boards across the state for other areas.
duration: Up to 320 hours
pay_detail: Paid training. Up to 320 hours. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: The page does not say who can join or state grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag teacher about your school's chapter. State application forms are on missouriffa.org.
notes: 26,830 members (per the page). Camp page says Missouri FFA hires college-age students for camp staff, so that job is not for most teens. Dues are not stated.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page checked for this card does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'apply here' link on the Recreation employment page to see the seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.

who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.
how_to_apply: Open the SSL Opportunities list on the Montgomery Parks site. Pick an event approved for SSL hours. Then register. You log in or create a volunteer account. Email parksvolunteers@montgomeryparks.org with questions.
notes: If you need many SSL hours in a short time, the page says that is only sometimes possible. Contacts on the page: Montgomery Parks Customer Service (301) 495-2595, and Volunteer Services 301-495-2504 on the main volunteer page. Office: 2425 Reedie Drive, 12th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students with interest in STEAM, health or biomedical research and a 3.0 GPA or higher. The research option also needs your latest report card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. For the research option, also send your report card, an essay about lab research and two recommendation forms. One must be from a science teacher. Some applicants are interviewed.
notes: Costs money. A session can be cancelled if too few students sign up. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. Ryan Clark, 404-752-1843. Dates shown are from summer 2026.
duration: 3 weeks (June 1 to 19, 2026) or 6 weeks (June 2 to July 10, 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: 3-week option $1,000. 6-week research option $1,500. No stipend listed.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a grade, age or GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application form linked on the summer programs page. A flyer is also posted there.
notes: The same page lists three other programs (FIRE UP, CADET, SCREP) that are for college or graduate students, not high schoolers. The symposium is in person for all summer students. The application form link is the 2026 one.
duration: 2026: presentations June 1 to 19 (Mon to Thu, 10 am to 3 pm), fieldwork July 7 to 18, symposium July 21 to 22
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask the program about cost or stipend.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors from the Metro Atlanta area with a 2.85 GPA or higher and an interest in a health career. An interview is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Apply Now form. Teacher recommendations, grades and an interview help pick who is chosen.
notes: Costs money. The same page lists a separate college track, which is not for high schoolers. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. J. Wesley Lockhart, 404-752-1197.
duration: 4 weeks (2026 program dates not stated on the page)
pay_detail: $1,000 program cost

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who are still in high school.
how_to_apply: The online application is closed because the program is full. The program page has a junior volunteer form you can download. For job shadowing, email aststudentservices@ascension.org. For Rutherford volunteer questions, email bryan.lowe@ascension.org.
notes: Adult volunteers must be 18 or older, but this junior program is for ages 15 to 18. Applications open January 1 and close when the program is full.
duration: 3 weeks, 9:00 am to 11:00 am
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe how to register. Email fire@mtsu.edu to ask about dates and sign-up.
notes: This is a day camp, so it does not include housing. The page also says a pre-law camp is being explored but is not confirmed.
duration: 4 days (day camp)
pay_detail: $300 per student. This covers activities, labs, lunch and snacks each day, and a t-shirt.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 can apply to volunteer at the Smyrna Public Library. Linebaugh Library in Murfreesboro also takes teen volunteers by semester. The page lists no age range for Linebaugh.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for the branch you want. At Smyrna, teens should fill out the form themselves, not a parent. Smyrna questions go to smyrnays@rclstn.org. Linebaugh questions go to kturner@rclstn.org or tdavis@rclstn.org.
notes: Other library branches are not taking volunteers right now, per the page. Volunteers age 18 and up use a different form.
duration: One semester. The Smyrna fall season runs Aug 17 to Nov 21. The page does not state a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply through the museum's volunteer portal (MyImpactPage) via the Learn more link on the Volunteer page. General museum volunteer steps listed: application, background check, new volunteer orientation. Questions: volunteer@lifeandscience.org.
notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).
duration: Camp weeks; schedule not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Residents of Albemarle, Charlottesville, Greene, Louisa or Nelson who are at least 17 or entering 12th grade. High school applicants need a college admittance letter or a counselor letter showing they plan to attend college.
how_to_apply: Submit an application form, an essay of at least 300 words, transcripts with GPA, a resume, a college letter, and two reference letters from non-family members, to director@jmrl.org or to the Library Director, 201 East Market St, Charlottesville.
notes: The official source read is the 2026 program flyer (PDF) on jmrl.org; the library's other pages did not list this internship. An applicant cannot receive the award more than twice. Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).
duration: 200 hours of library work
pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)

who_can_apply: Any high school student in Durham County in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Watch the Nasher Teen Council page for the next application. The page does not say when it opens. Meetings are every Thursday evening during the school year.
notes: Durham County students only. Watch the page for the next application.
duration: Thursdays 5:30 to 7:30 PM, October to April
pay_detail: Free. Snacks, dinner and parking are provided at every meeting.

who_can_apply: People over age 14 can take the Open Opportunities shifts. The 21+ events are not open to teens.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the museum's volunteer portal. Then sign up for a volunteer orientation. If you have questions, send an email to volunteer@adventuresci.org.
notes: The museum also runs Youth CR3W, a youth program with its own form. The CR3W page does not state ages, pay or schedule. Ask volunteer@adventuresci.org before you assume it fits you.
duration: No minimum hours stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free membership after 100 hours.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who are still in high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the West junior volunteer application between January and March. The hospital also asks for an interview. You must wear a uniform.
notes: Call 615-222-2127 for Midtown and West. Ascension Saint Thomas Rutherford has its own junior program. That program runs three weeks in July.
duration: 6 weeks. The program begins in June.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and older for the 2026 camps. The RISE research camps also need a 3.0 overall GPA and a 3.0 math and science GPA.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the newsletter on the camp page to hear when registration opens. Then register for the camp you want.
notes: Camps for 2027 may differ from the 2026 list. The page asks you to email Beth Bowman at beth.bowman@belmont.edu with questions.
duration: One-week camps. RISE ran about four weeks.
pay_detail: Most 2026 camps cost $425. The RISE research camps cost $1,700. One camp, VISIBL, was $0 for Metro Nashville students nominated by a science teacher. Email Beth Bowman if cost is a problem.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 or older. Younger teens (10 to 17) can volunteer through the Family Team program with a parent or other adult family member.
how_to_apply: Download and fill out the Teen Volunteer Application. Then do the orientation training you must take. Call the Volunteer Manager at 615-353-6966 with questions.
notes: The page says the teen program is for age 16 or older and does not give an upper age. The application PDF on the page is dated June 2025, so ask the Volunteer Manager if it is the current form.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Songwriters ages 12 to 18. July applicants also send a recording of 1 original song. People who have never come before get first pick.
how_to_apply: Email camp@countrymusichalloffame.org for 2027 sign up info. If you want aid, apply for it before you sign up. For the July camp, send up to 5 minutes of audio or video of 1 original song with lyrics.
notes: Costs real money. Campers who have been to two or more camps may be waitlisted.
duration: 1 week: June 14 to 19, 2027 (beginner to intermediate) or July 12 to 17, 2027 (intermediate to advanced)
pay_detail: 2026 fees on the page: $505 for museum members and $595 for non-members. 2027 fees are not posted. Need-based aid can lower the fee to $297 or $30.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 or high school freshmen to seniors. You must pass a background check, which the museum pays for. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Today on the Teen Team page. Or sign up for an info session. Email volunteer@countrymusichalloffame.org with questions.
notes: The museum also runs a Songwriting Camp for ages 12 to 18 (June 14 to 19 and July 12 to 17, 2027). In 2026 fees were $505 for members and $595 for non-members, with need based aid.
duration: About one assignment per month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Litter pick-up is open to all ages. Trail work, invasive plant removal and stream clean-up are for ages 18 and up, or ages 13 and up with an adult. School groups in grades K to 12 can volunteer with two or more chaperones.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile in the Friends of Warner Parks volunteer database. Fill out the information form and sign the waiver.
notes: Under 18 means you need an adult for most work. The Ambassador program is 18 and up. The page does not give an age rule for the seasonal SWEAT trail crew. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 18 who want to work with peers and professional artists.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe the application. Email teens@fristartmuseum.org with questions.
notes: The Frist also runs free Teen ARTlabs (art sessions with professional artists). Ages and dates for those are not listed on the Teens page; see the museum's teen events calendar.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The museum says TAAG time may count toward required service hours.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. Genesys Works partners with specific schools. Nashville is working with Metro Nashville Public Schools for its first class.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application, then interview, then confirm you accept. Click Apply Now on the Genesys Works application page and pick the Nashville location. Email nashville@genesysworks.org with questions.
notes: This program is new in Nashville. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a year-long internship
pay_detail: Paid internship. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: People 13 and older can have a Hands On account. Each project has its own age rule, so check the listing. Kids under 13 volunteer through the family page.
how_to_apply: Make a Hands On account and sign up for a project. A parent or guardian must sign the Hands On waiver. Bring the waiver to the project and check in with the Volunteer Leader.
notes: For school credit, bring your school's form. Ask the volunteer coordinator to check your hours.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 16.
how_to_apply: Send the finished application to Erin Adams. Staff review the forms. Then they invite students to an interview.
notes: The page still says 2026 applications are open, but that camp has passed. Ask about 2027 through the contact link. The camp is an initiative of the Benjamin Harrison Presidential Site.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day.
pay_detail: $350 per student, or $300 for Hermitage members. Lunch is not included. Limited financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: The program page does not state an age range. Read the STriVe online guide for details.
how_to_apply: Watch the hospital volunteering page for the application in Spring 2027. Read the STriVe online guide first.
notes: Applications may close early if the hospital gets many. The Caring Hands Crew is for anyone 16 and up who wants to help the hospital's mission.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Youth who live in Davidson County. Ages 14 to 15 apply for Experience Work. Ages 16 to 18 apply for High School Internships.
how_to_apply: Pick Experience Work or High School Internships on the POWER Youth job portal, search the job list for your age group, apply and check your email for a confirmation. Call 615-862-8860 for help.
notes: The program page says it serves ages 14 to 22 overall and lists High School Internships for ages 16 to 19. The job seekers page says 16 to 18, so this card uses 18. Confirm with Metro Action. This card covers the teen tracks only. Neither page says whether a work permit or ID is needed, so ask Metro Action. Office is at 1281 Murfreesboro Pike, Nashville.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 1 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $12 per hour (Experience Work, ages 14 to 15). $15 per hour (High School Internship).

who_can_apply: Anyone age 13 or older. Volunteers under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form for 1 person. Then watch your email for next steps.
notes: The library says it does not take every applicant. It places volunteers by what each site needs. It also asks you to keep a set weekly schedule, so check you can. The page says shorter jobs can be found through Hands On Nashville.
duration: Weekly shifts for at least 6 months and 50 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Standard food sorting is for ages 12 and older. Cold food sorting is for ages 16 and older at the Martin site. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign a waiver. Volunteers under 16 must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Book a shift ahead of time on the online volunteer calendar. Bring a signed Youth Volunteer Waiver if you are under 18. Groups of 5 or more need a leader who is 18 or older.
notes: The food bank asks for 1 adult for every 7 volunteers under 18. Walk-ins may not be accepted. The sites named on the page are Martin, Nacarato and Camden, and shift days differ by site.
duration: Shift length is not stated on the program page. Stay for the full shift.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Hiring starts at age 15 for most jobs. Many jobs need you to be 16 or older. Only a limited number of jobs are open to 15-year-olds.
how_to_apply: Use the online careers portal. Send one application only, for the department you want most. A hiring manager will contact you if your application fits, so check your contact info.
notes: Do not apply to more than one department. Do not call to ask about status. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18, so ask the employer.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Pay rate not stated on the program page. The page says you get daily pay.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Say if you want residential or day. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, a one-page essay and one recommendation letter. Incomplete packets are not considered.
notes: Run with Cummins as a partner. Contact Dre Davenport at ddaventp@tnstate.edu or 615-963-5389.
duration: Dates are June 7 to July 3, 2026. The length in weeks is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $400 per student. It is not refundable. Meals are provided.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, and a one-page essay. Your teacher or counselor emails one recommendation letter to Professor Kang Du.
notes: The Tennessee Department of Transportation runs and funds this program. Contact Professor Kang Du at kdu@tnstate.edu. Or call the College of Engineering at 615-963-5401.
duration: 4 weeks: 3 weeks on campus, then 1 week online.
pay_detail: Free to students. Pay or a stipend is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Open to grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $50 fee. If you are placed in a course you pay a 20% deposit one week after the admission notice. Check the box for aid if you want to apply for it.
notes: It costs money. The page offers aid for families with adjusted gross income of $105,000 or less or severe hardship. It offers a payment plan for everyone. The page mixes 2026 deadlines with 2027 session dates. Confirm both with precollege@vanderbilt.edu.
duration: One week. The tuition page lists several 2027 session dates in June and July.
pay_detail: One-week tuition on the PTY page: $2,150 (grades 7 to 8), $2,850 (grades 9 to 10), $2,950 (grades 11 to 12). Tuition covers course, materials, housing and meals. $50 application fee ($100 international).

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16. Your school must have an affiliation agreement with VUMC. Homeschool students need an agreement with their homeschool group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application in one sitting. It does not save. Upload your health insurance card, a health form, a safety quiz certificate and signed forms.
notes: Minors cannot observe in some places. These are operating rooms, emergency departments, pediatric intensive care units and the Vanderbilt Psychiatric Hospital. If your school has no agreement with VUMC, you are not eligible. Email VOE@VUMC.org with questions.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is no application fee.

who_can_apply: Teens from age 13 to high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send 1 recommendation form from someone who is not a relative or family friend. Then go to a 60 minute group interview and all training sessions.
notes: The zoo's page and its info sheet differ on small things (how many recommendations, the fee). Send an email to volunteer@nashvillezoo.org before you apply. The dates on the info sheet are from the last cycle posted. They are interviews Mar 28 and 29 and Apr 11 and 12, and a summer start on May 26.
duration: Summer: one shift a week for at least 7 weeks plus one week of Zoo Camp. School year: at least 4 hours each semester plus one special event.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo's page mentions a one-time fee that includes a uniform, but no amount is posted.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 can join the teen programs. Age is counted as of January 1 of the program year. You join through your local county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H program. Then enroll through 4-H Online. That is the system for joining, renewing and signing up for events.
notes: The teen page was updated April 30, 2026. Clover Crew is listed as new in 2026. Programs differ from county to county. The pages do not give a fee or the dates for the teen events.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.

who_can_apply: Teams of 3 to 5 students from a school, non-traditional school or youth group such as 4-H or FFA. High school teams need five members to place at state. Each team needs an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Sign up with your county Soil and Water Conservation District. In Wake County, fill out the Wake Envirothon sign-up form. The official form is emailed to advisors later in fall 2026.
notes: The dates above come from Wake County's page. Other areas of the state have their own area dates and deadlines, so call your county district. Wake contact: Leah Purvis, 919-250-1065.
duration: Area contest plus 2 day state event
pay_detail: Wake County's district pays registration for Wake teams. Fees for other counties are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who belong to a school FFA chapter, which runs through a school agricultural education program. Homeschool students can join if they take an agriculture course and have an SAE project (for example through the NCSU Agriscience Academy chapter).
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher if your school has an FFA chapter. Take an agriculture class. The chapter advisor sends in the roster and dues. Homeschool families use the Homeschool FFA Membership Application on the page.
notes: The state office is at 4111 Beryl Road, Raleigh, NC 27606, 919-515-4206. The site says North Carolina has over 47,000 FFA members. If your school has no ag program, the page explains how a school can start one.
duration: Membership year runs Aug 1 to July 31
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $12 for high school students ($7 national plus $5 state) and $8 for middle school students ($7 national plus $1 state). Many chapters collect these through the school.

who_can_apply: High school students or recent high school graduates in good academic standing. Seniors may apply to take part the summer before college. College students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Governor's Page application and send the online recommendation form to two people: a non-relative school staff or faculty member (unless homeschooled) and a non-relative adult who can speak to your fit. Applications without both recommendations are not processed.
notes: Founded in 1973. The work location is the Albemarle building, 325 N Salisbury St, Raleigh. Business clothes are required. Pages and their guardians arrange where to stay and eat in Raleigh. Office of the Governor phone: (919) 814-2000. The page does not list dates for page weeks. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One page week of four days (Monday afternoon, then Tuesday to Thursday)
pay_detail: $200 stipend per week to help with travel and lodging costs. A limited number of host families provide meals and rides for a $100 fee paid by the page.

who_can_apply: North Carolina residents in public or non-public schools. You must meet one of the GPA or course rules in the family overview, for example a 3.25 unweighted GPA. You cannot apply on your own. Your school or district must nominate you first.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or local Governor's School coordinator. Turn in the student application at your school, not to the state office. It has one essay or audition and a personal readiness form. Turn in two recommendation forms too.
notes: Competitive. The family overview says about 1,800 students are nominated and about 800 are picked in a typical year. Students must stay the whole session and may attend only once. The overview says you may not use AI on the application.
duration: Four weeks (June 20 to July 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $600 tuition per student, collected through the school or district. Need-based scholarships are offered by the NC Governor's School Foundation. Families pay for travel.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors in good school standing. A North Carolina House member must sponsor you. You must not have been a House Page before. School principal approval is needed if you serve during the school year.
how_to_apply: Ask your own House member to sponsor you (find yours with the Find Your Legislators tool). Then fill out the online application, which goes to that member. You can ask the House Page office, Room 1329, 16 W. Jones Street, Raleigh, for a paper copy.
notes: Very competitive and you can apply with only one member. The Speaker of the House makes the final appointments. Housing in Raleigh is up to your parent or guardian. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One week, Monday to Thursday, while the legislature is in session
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Centers: Schenck, 98 Schenck Dr, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768. Kittrell, 1096 U.S. Highway 1 South, Kittrell, NC 27544. Oconaluftee, 502 Oconaluftee Job Corps Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719. No closure notice showed on the pages on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school girls in grades 9 to 12 who are enrolled in a North Carolina public, private, charter or home school. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to girls from across the state, but all placements are in the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application portal opens in early January 2027. The FAQ says to check the program website for current deadlines. Email your resume, cover letter and transcript to doa.youth.involvement@doa.nc.gov. Students who skip these documents are dropped from the process.
notes: Only 15 to 20 spots. You must get yourself to your job site every day; the program only gives rides to Wednesday and Thursday events. Contact named on the page: Jean McBride. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 4 weeks, 40-hour weeks Monday to Friday (July 2027, exact dates not posted yet)
pay_detail: $1,700 stipend, paid on the second to last day of the program. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You are chosen by an application, a teacher's note and a group interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student form and a teacher recommendation form. Both are due by the deadline.
notes: Volunteer role, and it costs a yearly fee. Contact Lynn Cross (listed on the page) about scholarships.
duration: September to May: two planning meetings a month (Wednesdays 4 to 6pm), every cafe on first Fridays Sept to April, August retreat
pay_detail: $75 per year for snacks, T-shirt and supplies. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 during the 2026-27 school year. Selected by application.
how_to_apply: Applications reopen in January 2027 and are due Friday, April 9, 2027 at 5pm. Students bring their own lunch. The museum supplies program materials, snacks and transport to field sites.
notes: The page also still shows last year's dates (deadline April 8, 2026). The 2027 dates above are the ones listed for the 2027 program. Location is the Nature Research Center, 121 West Jones St., Raleigh.
duration: 1 week, 9am to 4:30pm daily (June 14-18, 2027)
pay_detail: $50 for the week. Scholarships available on request.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. The page states no residency requirement. The program follows Wake County's school calendar.
how_to_apply: The page gives no step-by-step process. Staff contact is Lynn Cross (listed on the page).
notes: The page did not describe how students are picked.
duration: September to April. One monthly meeting with Living Collections staff plus two monthly group meetings with scientists (3:30-5 pm).
pay_detail: $75 per year (snacks, T-shirt, boots and protective eyewear); optional trips may cost extra for travel

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders. The museum's general volunteer rule is 18 and older; under-18s join through the teen programs.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in mid-January 2027, then attend a group interview if invited. The page does not describe the application steps; contact the listed staff member.
notes: Teens may reschedule up to 3 of the 10 shifts. Other teen programs on the museum's Teens page (Climate Resilience Institute, Cafe Coordinators, Teen Science Cafes) were listed without dates or fees.
duration: 10 weeks, June 15 to August 19. One shift a week (Tue, Wed or Thu, 10-1 or 1-4). Required orientation Saturday May 15.
pay_detail: $75 per summer (covers orientation, food, T-shirt, nametag and props)

who_can_apply: Recommended for ages 11 to 17. Free, no application stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Show up at the Daily Planet Cafe at the museum or watch live on YouTube. No sign up is listed on the page.
notes: A good first step before applying to Cafe Coordinators.
duration: 1 hour, 6pm to 7pm, first Friday of each month
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10, 11 or 12 who are in good school standing. A North Carolina senator must sponsor you. If you serve during the school year, your principal must approve it first.
how_to_apply: Contact your senator and ask for an application. It is not online and not available from the Page office. Return the finished form to your senator.
notes: Competitive. Each senator can sponsor only a set number of students. The Senate President Pro Tempore makes the appointments. Business clothes are required. Bring money for lunch each day.
duration: One week during the legislative session: report Monday afternoon, work Tuesday to Thursday
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: High school (secondary) and college (postsecondary) students in career and technical education pathways.
how_to_apply: Ask your career and technical education (CTE) teacher about your school's chapter. Your advisor signs you up on the national SkillsUSA registration site. It is linked from the NC join page.
notes: Contacts on the site: information line 919-675-1241, info@SkillsUSAnc.org, P.O. Box 88, Oxford, NC 27565. The March 1 date is described as an annual national deadline, not tied to a named year.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $14, per the NC SkillsUSA join page.

who_can_apply: Academically talented North Carolina students in their second or third year of high school who want STEM careers. Applicants must complete the Residency Determination Service process. Students are picked by Congressional District.
how_to_apply: Apply through NCSSM Admissions. The application is on cfnc.org, so you need a CFNC account. Finish the Residency Determination Service step. Write the Summer Ventures essays. Have your school send your transcript and teacher and counselor evaluations.
notes: 2027 campuses and dates listed: Appalachian State (June 20 to July 31, to be decided), East Carolina (virtual week June 27 to July 3, then on campus July 4 to 24), UNC Charlotte (June 20 to July 31, to be decided), UNC Wilmington (June 20 to July 17). Accepted students do an online Research Prep course in June. Contact: summerventures@ncssm.edu or 919-416-2747.
duration: About four weeks between mid-June and end of July 2027, depending on the campus
pay_detail: No cost to accepted students. Meals and housing on campus are included. It does not pay a wage.

who_can_apply: Junior Division: ages 13 to 18 and not yet graduated from high school. There is also a Young Artist Division for ages 18 to 23. Instrumentalists.
how_to_apply: Watch the competition page for 2027 details. If you have a question, you can send it by email to education@ncsymphony.org.
notes: Niche: for serious young players. Entry fee and rounds' dates are not stated on the page.
duration: Preliminary and final rounds (the page does not say where)
pay_detail: No pay. First and second prize winners in each division receive cash awards.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in North Carolina, chosen by American Legion posts. The About page describes the program as for young men in North Carolina. No age or residency rule beyond that is listed.
how_to_apply: Applications open Nov 1, 2026. Local American Legion posts pick delegates. Find a post near you. The FAQ page links a post finder. Or email info@tarheelboysstate.org.
notes: Delegates must attend the full week. The FAQ page says graduates get an automatic $20,000 scholarship to Chowan University, spread over 4 years. The girls' program is a separate American Legion Auxiliary program (Tar Heel Girls State) and is not covered here.
duration: One week (the 87th session is June 20 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: $500 per delegate for lodging, meals and two uniform shirts. A local American Legion post, business or community group often pays it. Families with money worries are told to contact the program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. Cadets join a local cadet or composite squadron, and you may join any one in the wing.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the NC Wing page. Then contact a squadron and visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application and pay dues.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. NC Wing office: 3520 Alamance Road, Burlington, NC 27215, 336-290-7473, info@ncwgcap.org. The NC Wing site lists a 2027 summer encampment page.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $60 for North Carolina in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Start as early as age 16. You must be enrolled in high school or be a high school graduate, interested in a high-demand career field, and ready to do both on-the-job learning and classroom instruction.
how_to_apply: Find a Registered Apprenticeship opportunity on the ApprenticeshipNC site and contact the program sponsor or employer to apply. Questions: apprenticeshipnc@nccommunitycolleges.edu or 919-807-6988. The page also mentions youth apprenticeship consortia that serve high school students.
notes: The NC Department of Labor says youth under 18 who work in North Carolina must have a Youth Employment Certificate, started by the employer once you have a job offer. Some jobs are off limits to people under 18 unless a supervised practice agreement is approved. Specific openings and employers change, so use the Find Apprenticeship Opportunities tool.
duration: Varies by apprenticeship
pay_detail: Apprentices are paid employees from day one, with raises as you gain skills. The wage depends on the employer and is not stated.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in good standing at a public, private, charter or home school in North Carolina. You do not need a legislator to sponsor you.
how_to_apply: The page says to complete the student application, but it shows no link. Contact the program coordinator, Erica Gallion, at (919) 301-1372. Ask for the application.
notes: The page does not say where the application is, what it costs or when it is due. Check the page again or call the coordinator before you plan.
duration: A conference of about three days (the 2025-26 session was March 13 to 15, 2026)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Open to rising sixth graders through recent high school graduates. For the Junior Wildlife Assistant role you must be in 10th or 11th grade when you apply, live within 90 miles of the zoo, and be able to lift 50 lbs and stand for 30 minutes. Other roles have their own rules on their pages.
how_to_apply: When recruitment opens, choose a teen role on the zoo's Teen Volunteers page. Send in that role's application. Junior Wildlife Assistants also do a 20 minute phone interview. They go to at least two Zoo Pathways events.
notes: Roles listed: Play Pals (middle school), Junior Wildlife Assistant (high school), Camp Crew (middle and high school), Zoo Futures (middle school). Zoo address: 4401 Zoo Parkway, Asheboro, NC 27205, 336-879-7001.
duration: Summer only, May through August. Junior Wildlife Assistant: 6 weeks, 13 to 15 hours a week (last season June 17 to July 31)
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time $20 onboarding fee for new volunteers, which can be waived for families with financial hardship.

who_can_apply: Age or grade requirements are not stated on the page. Ask the program manager.
how_to_apply: The page does not say when the next council opens. Questions: Erin Hanehan, manager of teen and college programming (erin.hanehan@dncr.nc.gov).
notes: The museum also runs teen workshops for ages 13 to 18 (separate, listed on the same page).
duration: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 pm, Sept 17, 2026 to June 3, 2027
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: North Carolina residents. The page does not list grade levels. It wants students with strong school skills from many walks of life.
how_to_apply: Online application through the INSPIRE page. Contact inspire@ncssm.edu or 919-416-2784.
notes: Held at NCSSM-Morganton in western NC, not in the Triangle. Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week residential (June 21-26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free (room and meals included)

who_can_apply: Current North Carolina 8th graders. You must live in the counties listed for each campus. The Durham campus counties include Wake, Durham, Orange and many more.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. There is a workshop on how to apply on Dec 3, 2026. There is an info session in Durham on Jan 14, 2027.
notes: Only for students who are in 8th grade when they apply. Cohort 1 is for current 8th graders; Cohort 2 is for the returning rising 10th graders.
duration: 1 week residential each summer, two summers, plus school year workshops
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Rising 7th through 12th graders from anywhere. You apply for a course whose requirements you meet. A parent fills out part of the application.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian with custody fills out part 1 of the application. The student writes the short answers. Admission is rolling. Students can ask for money help after they are accepted.
notes: There is also a free sponsored option for 60 students in 18 western NC counties (Dogwood Health Trust). Dates and fees are from the last cycle's pages.
duration: Varies by course
pay_detail: $495 to $1,495 for rising 7th to 9th graders; $695 to $1,925 for rising 10th to 12th graders. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: The page links to an interest form and to a program website. It does not list application steps.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: High school students with disabilities in grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th to 12th graders). You can be in regular classes. You can also be on the Occupational Course of Study (a high school diploma track). Students in public, charter, private and home school can apply.
how_to_apply: Student and at least one parent must attend an open house first, then apply. Contact program director Joann Blumenfeld, (919) 633-3120.
notes: The first open house date (Jan 14, 2027) is the one that starts the process. Pay amount for internships is not stated.
duration: June to June (summer week plus Saturdays in the school year)
pay_detail: The program is free. Paid STEM internships are also offered. The pay amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Must be a high school student. The page does not say whether out-of-state students can apply.
how_to_apply: Visit the program website to learn more and apply (growforit.ces.ncsu.edu/growforit-programs/hssi). The page does not list application steps.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: $650. Some financial help may be available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors who like farming and farm careers (NC Farm Bureau page).
how_to_apply: Download the application from the NC Farm Bureau IFAL page. Or get one at your county Farm Bureau office.
notes: Dates are last year's. The NC Farm Bureau page does not state a cost, so the no cost entry is not confirmed. In 2026 the program ran at three campuses (NC State, NC A&T and University of Mount Olive). The site you attend may differ.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: Any current high school student.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program website. The address is cals.ncsu.edu/animal-science/extension/livestock-science-camp.
