notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 through 12. NC State chapter works with schools in northeastern and central North Carolina.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MSEN office. See the program website (fi.ncsu.edu/teams/msen).
notes: Dates are last year's pattern. Contact the MSEN office about scholarships.
duration: Yearlong, September to July
pay_detail: $110. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Must be a high school student. The page does not list grade rules or a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Visit the program website to learn more and sign up (growforit.ces.ncsu.edu/growforit-programs/nc-youth-institute). The page does not tell how to sign up.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: One-day conference at NC State (the 2026 listing gives April 16 and 17, 2026)
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors with an interest in poultry.
how_to_apply: Apply at go.ncsu.edu/applypssi
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders from North Carolina.
how_to_apply: Apply through your local NC Soil and Water Conservation District. Deadlines differ by district. They are usually in late March. Contact the co-coordinators listed on the page (Liz Driscoll, liz_driscoll@ncsu.edu, 919.886.3424).
notes: Dates are last year's. Awards and scholarships are given to students at the workshop.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade (2026 page). Homeschooled, out-of-state and international students are encouraged to apply. Admission is based on academics (typically A's and B's in math and science) and interest.
how_to_apply: Online application: GPA, school and counselor info, and two short written answers (camp goals and a problem you would like to solve). Each applicant is placed in one workshop.
notes: All dates and the fee on the page are for 2026; 2027 terms were not posted. The Engineering Place also runs day camps for younger students.
duration: 1 week (2026 weeks: June 14-19, June 21-26, July 5-10, July 12-17)
pay_detail: $1,550 camp fee in 2026, no refunds. A limited amount of financial aid is available for demonstrated need.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Contact the program (Kent Lupino, named on the page) to ask about joining a team.
notes: The page does not give a season or the fee. Tournaments can go to the state, regional and national level if a team qualifies.
duration: Team practice Mondays and Thursdays 6 to 9 pm, plus Saturdays as needed
pay_detail: Team registration fee (amount not stated). Donations also help fund teams.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders (program precollege page). Scholarships based on need are offered. The Shelton page says 1 in 3 participants gets one.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Apply link on the Shelton Challenge site for the Red Hat Shelton Challenge at NC State. Other partner sites run the same program in other places.
notes: Dates are last year's. Check sheltonleadership.ncsu.edu/shelton-challenge-programs for 2027 dates.
duration: 6 days, residential

who_can_apply: High school students. Preference goes to rising juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Visit the TexTEC program website to learn more (textiles.ncsu.edu/academics/k-12/textec-camp). The page does not list the steps to apply.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 2 days, day camp

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. Up to 40 students per week are chosen. The choice is based on grades, activities and interest in the Wilson College of Textiles.
how_to_apply: Apply on the STEP website (step.textiles.ncsu.edu).
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: $450. Partial and full scholarships for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: U.S. or U.S. territory residents who are rising high school sophomores, juniors or seniors (rising college freshmen also accepted) and are 15 by June 7, 2027. Past in-person campers cannot apply for in-person VetCAMP again.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline. Pay the $30 application fee for each week you apply for. Virtual VetCAMP is offered to all who are not picked for the in-person camp.
notes: Applicants must upload an unofficial high school transcript. Maximum of about 5 wait-listed per week.
duration: 5 days. 2027 weeks: June 28 to July 2 and July 5 to July 9. A virtual VetCAMP is also offered.
pay_detail: $800 for the week as a day camper, or $1,050 as an overnight camper ($800 plus $250 for dorm and meals). $30 application fee. Pricing may change.

who_can_apply: Students ages 9 to 19. The eligibility section of the page says 9 to 19, but its header says ages 9 to 14. Check the page to be sure.
how_to_apply: Apply on the workshop website. The address is english.chass.ncsu.edu/youngwriters.
notes: Dates are last year's. Several sessions, check which one fits your age. Page is inconsistent on age range (header says 9 to 14, body says 9 to 19).
duration: 2 weeks, afternoons (day program)

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who go to a high school in the NRCC service region. You must meet college placement rules. You need a note of support from a high school official and a signed form from a parent. Strong freshmen and sophomores may be able to join. They need the OK of the high school principal and the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor and use the dual enrollment forms on the NRCC page. The parent signature form is required.
notes: The NRCC page still showed an old campus closure banner, so confirm the details with the college. Cost to students is not stated on the page.
duration: Semester by semester
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Newport News residents ages 16 to 17 and young adults ages 18 to 24. Under 18 needs a signed parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth - Apply for the Youth Career Program link on the city page. Finish the application steps.
notes: Not open to 14 and 15 year olds. The city page does not state the wage.
duration: About 25 hours a week, June to August (from the employer page)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page, so check it again in late October.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 13 to 17. This includes teens going into 9th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Conservation Youth Team page. Info sessions were held in February and March. Teens who are picked have an interview.
notes: Dates are from the 2026 cycle. Applications open December 1, and the year is not stated. The page lists interest sessions in February and March.
duration: About 150 hours in summer plus fall or spring sessions for first-year members
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $100 registration fee for shirts, name tag and materials. A scholarship covers this fee for a few first-year applicants.

who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents, at least 16 by the start date, with a 3.00 GPA or higher. You must be in good standing at a school or approved home school in Anderson, Blount, Campbell, Knox, Loudon, McMinn, Monroe, Morgan, Roane or Sevier County, Tennessee. Proof of health insurance is required.
how_to_apply: Apply on Zintellect by Oct 21, 2026. A full form needs recommendations from a STEM teacher and a principal. Home school students can use a curriculum coordinator. Forms that are missing a recommendation are not read.
notes: Closes very soon. You can miss up to five days without losing stipend. Appointments may be extended depending on funding. Only students from the ten listed Tennessee counties can apply.
duration: 16 to 17 weeks, Jan 26 to May 15 or May 22, 2027, part time each week
pay_detail: $125 per week for part-time participation

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 17 who will be in grade 10, 11 or 12 and are under 18. You must be able to attend the full camp.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps yet. Email the ORNL K-12 Education team (address on the SAGE page) or call 865-576-7658.
notes: The camp is at 1 Bethel Valley Road, Oak Ridge, TN 37830. Residency rules are not stated. Ask the K-12 team about cost and who can apply.
duration: About 1.5 weeks (July 12 to 22, 2027)
pay_detail: Pay and cost are not stated

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors interested in skilled trades and technical careers. No age range is given.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply yet. Contact the ORNL K-12 Education team (865-576-7658) or the contact listed on the Trades Camp page.
notes: The camp is at 1 Bethel Valley Road, Oak Ridge, TN 37830. Residency rules are not stated.
duration: 4 days
pay_detail: Pay and cost are not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. You need a set schedule and must complete an application. Adults also complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out a volunteer application. Sign in with the Volunteer Coordinator for each shift. Training is given.
notes: The county document is titled 2024, so confirm shifts and openings with the library before you go. Main branch only: 137 W. Margaret Lane, Hillsborough. Re-check 2026-10-10: the county PDF matches the age, schedule, application and background check terms. It says nothing about ongoing intake or a 2026 date, so the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: 1 or 2 hour shifts, Monday to Friday 10am to 5pm, as spaces are available
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 in Prince George's County. Placements are by random lottery. The county's main SYEP pages were blocked for my reader, so residency and work-eligibility rules are not confirmed here.
how_to_apply: Apply online at syep.mypgc.us during the spring window. Eligible applicants are entered in a random lottery for a placement. Questions: syep@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6200 (from the county release).
notes: Facts come from the County Executive's official March 1, 2026 bulletin; the county SYEP web pages returned Access Denied to my reader, so confirm at syep.mypgc.us. Highly in demand, so apply the day the window opens. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.
duration: 6 weeks (Jul 6 to Aug 14 in 2026)
pay_detail: Hourly and stipend opportunities are available (rate not stated in the county release).

who_can_apply: Youth must reach the required age on or before May 31. It is 14 for Summer Playtime and 15 for Summer Day Camps. Youth cannot volunteer at a site where a younger sibling or child is a registered participant. Ages 15 and older need a criminal background history check.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Volunteer Opportunities page of pgparks.com. Each youth may volunteer at only one Summer Playtime or Summer Day Camp site. Transportation is not provided.
notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: 12 to 15 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Approved for Prince George's County Public Schools Student Service Learning hours.

who_can_apply: About 20 high school-age youth who live in Prince George's County. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Email your name, resume, school information and a list of extracurricular activities to Stephen.Makle@pgparks.com. The page names him as the contact.
notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: School year; meetings in person at community centers and online
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn student service learning credits or community service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 (library system rule). VolunTEEN is for grades 6 to 12. The Kids Achieve Club welcomes teens over 15. Volunteers cannot staff the Circulation or Information desks.
how_to_apply: Get a volunteer application from your local branch. Ask for the volunteer coordinator. For VolunTEEN, sign up through the Beanstack app.
notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Temporary (limited) or regular (at least 6 months) schedules
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student service learning hours are available.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 (must be 16 by June 1). A recent graduate can still apply if they are still 17 on June 1. Recent graduates who are 18 go to the college or adult programs. You need a 3.0 GPA or higher and interest in a health career.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Two or more recommendation forms (teacher, counselor, coach or boss, not family). Show you are immune to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox, and have a TB test. Send a headshot and parent signatures.
notes: You must go to the required orientation, or you can apply next summer.
duration: June 8 to July 30, 2027: at least one shift a week for at least six of the eight weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $25 program fee. Uniform shirts are provided.

who_can_apply: Students age 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student volunteer application in person at the branch you choose, or contact the branch. Volunteer Office: 703-792-6100.
notes: Adult volunteer roles on the same page need age 18. Branch list is at pwcva.gov/department/library/branch-locations-hours/.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Add a one-page cover letter. Add one letter from a teacher, boss or volunteer leader. Email volunteer@maymont.org or call 804-525-9000.
notes: Ask the volunteer lead for the 2027 dates.
duration: One 4-hour training and at least 10 morning shifts (8:45 am to 12:15 pm) in the summer camp season (2026: June 1 to Aug 14)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: City of Richmond residents who are in school. Counselors in Training: ages 14 to 16 (14 by July 1). Summer Work Experience: ages 16 to 19 (16 by July 1, not 19 before the program ends).
how_to_apply: Apply online starting March 1 with your latest report card and one proof of residency. Work experience also needs a signed Social Security card and a photo ID. Questions: 804-646-7000 or 3-1-1.
notes: Page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Work experience about 6 weeks, early July to mid-August; mandatory training in May
pay_detail: Paid by the employer or by the Academy. The youth pay rate is not stated on the FAQ page.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page (ages and residency are not listed).
how_to_apply: Download the YCC application (Word document) and email it to the park contact, or mail it to 3215 E. Broad Street, Richmond, VA 23223. Questions: 804-795-5019 ext. 1.
notes: Only five spots. The page was last updated April 2024, so confirm the year, pay and ages with the park.
duration: 8 weeks in July and August, Monday to Friday, 8 hours a day. Five youth are hired.
pay_detail: $7.25 per hour (as posted; page last updated April 2024)

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, or at least a rising sophomore. Must attend the initial training and commit to 8 shifts over 16 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the museum's volunteer page. It is hard to get in. They look at writing, drive, growth and teamwork.
notes: The page labels these as 2027 spring applications, but its weekday and date pairs (Sunday, Nov 8 and Saturday, Jan 10) match 2026. Confirm the dates with the museum.
duration: 8 shifts over 16 weeks, every other weekend (Saturday or Sunday)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who are interested in pharmacy. About 30 are selected. No GPA rule listed.
how_to_apply: Register through the link on the VCU School of Pharmacy summer programs page. Questions: pharmacy@vcu.edu.
notes: Students are responsible for their own housing and transportation. The page is for 2026, so confirm the 2027 dates.
duration: 1 week, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm (2026: July 20 to 24). Not residential.
pay_detail: $50. Fee waivers can be requested when accepted.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older (some roles need 18). Must sign a liability waiver and complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Call 540-342-5718 or email hsell@smwv.org. The contact is Hunter Sell, Director of Operations.
notes: The page is not teen specific. Ask how the background check works for minors.
duration: No required hours stated
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. Membership perks after 10, 50 and 100 hours.

who_can_apply: Female high school students who are ready to start exploring college. Parent or guardian permission is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form now for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. Applying is not an application to Spelman and does not promise admission. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the CPI page itself says only that late submissions are not accepted.
duration: 2 weeks, residential. Session 1: June 5 to 18, 2027. Session 2: July 2 to 17, 2027.
pay_detail: $3,150 per session (the page says cost is subject to change)

who_can_apply: Female high school students in 11th grade with a 3.0 GPA and at least a 3.0 in English and science. Parent permission is required. One page also says juniors and seniors, so confirm your grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the ECP page itself does not give a due date.
duration: 4 weeks, residential, June 19 to July 16, 2027
pay_detail: Biology $4,500, English $4,500, Dance $4,400 (subject to change)

who_can_apply: The Volunteer Center takes volunteers ages 6 and up. F.A.R.M. distribution events need volunteers who are 16 or older. Food on the Move events need volunteers who are 18 or older. Volunteers under 16 need one adult for every five of them.
how_to_apply: Pick a shift on the volunteer sign-up page and register. Do not wear open-heel or open-toe shoes. Minors use the minor waiver form.
notes: The Foodbank requires one adult volunteer for every five volunteers under 16, in groups or not. Plan 3 to 4 months ahead for groups. Court-ordered service is not accepted.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens from the St. Louis area. Age range not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn more and apply link on the museum's teen assistants page. A contact email is listed there.
notes: The page did not list ages. Ask the museum before you apply. The page title reads Museum Assistants.
duration: Up to 24 hours a week in summer. At least 5 hours a month in the school year.
pay_detail: $15 per hour

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16. Teens volunteer through their high school and get community service credit hours.
how_to_apply: Call 314-362-5324 and ask for the student application packet. Send in all of the information at one time. If the spots are full, you can go on a waiting list.
notes: Students should not use the adult application. No more than three absences are allowed in Summer Teens. School-year community service hours are possible when there is room. Call the Volunteer Office to ask.
duration: At least 7 weeks and 60 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get community service credit hours.

who_can_apply: High school students in the St. Louis metro area. CAM aims for a mix of new and returning teens and a mix of art backgrounds.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Applications for 2026 are closed. Learning and Engagement staff review applications.
notes: You must attend all sessions to get the stipend.
duration: 2026: May 27 to July 16 (Wed, Thu, Fri 2 to 4 p.m.) plus three sessions Aug to Nov
pay_detail: $500 stipend if you finish the whole program. Public transit costs can be reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18 who live in the St. Louis County Library District.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in March. In 2026 the page had an Apply Now button for the teen internship application.
notes: The 2026 internship ran June 1 to August 7. The intern must be flexible with the schedule and with branches. The intern also writes a final reflection about the summer.
duration: 10 weeks, 12 hours per week
pay_detail: $15.00 per hour, about 12 hours per week

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Send the form on the program page. A participating branch will contact you.
notes: Only participating branches run TAG. Meeting times are not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and in the 6th grade. Teens fill out the teen volunteer application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen volunteer application on the program page. You can also call 314-994-3300 or email volunteer@slcl.org.
notes: Each community service request is looked at on its own.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library says volunteering can count toward a community service requirement.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors at a public or private high school in the St. Louis area, in good academic standing. Children of St. Louis Fed employees cannot apply. Only one student per school is picked.
how_to_apply: A teacher nominates you. You send the application form. Your teacher then sends a Teacher Recommendation form.
notes: After the program, members may apply for a limited number of summer internships at the St. Louis Fed. Questions: STLSSBoD@stls.frb.org.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth starting at age 13. The museum wants people who are outgoing, flexible and patient, and who like working with children.
how_to_apply: Send an application on the program page. If chosen, you have a personal interview and then an orientation.
notes: Volunteer sites are the Magic House in Kirkwood and MADE for Kids at 5127 Delmar Blvd. in St. Louis. The page does not give an upper age limit.
duration: You are asked to serve at least 30 hours within a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says volunteering can help with community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students. Most programs are for rising juniors and seniors. The Health Professions Summer Institute also takes rising sophomores. The design and art program takes students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in spring. Each program has its own registration. Fees vary by program.
notes: Pick the program that fits your grade. Fees are from 2026 and may change.
duration: 1 day to 1 week
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $65 portfolio workshop, $75 Cybersecurity, $85 Biz Camp, $100 Saints Science Academy, $150 Health Professions, $700 Rawlings Sport Business (lodging and meals included).

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18 who like a career in medicine. Students fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Send in the TLC form, a questionnaire, a letter of recommendation from a teacher or school mentor and a minor consent form. Accepted students do a background check and a health screen (shot history, TB test, urine drug screen). Questions: 314-251-6180.
notes: The Tuesday and Thursday program has room for 40 students. Mercy has a Monday, Wednesday and Friday program too.
duration: 2026: June 9 to July 30, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (three required orientation days)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers must be at least 16. You fill out an application and have an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the program page. Placement depends on an interview and on what the hospital needs.
notes: The hospital is in west St. Louis County. The page does not say how many hours a week you must give.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: You are a rising junior or senior. You go to a partner high school. The 2026-27 partners were Metro Classical and Academic and University City High. The rest were Rosati-Kain Academy, Crossroads College Prep and Nerinx Hall.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the form opens. You apply from a partner high school.
notes: Your school must be a partner school. Coordinator: 314-577-9466, eco-act@mobot.org. Transportation help is offered for activities outside school.
duration: One week of summer training, then the school year
pay_detail: Free. Taken as a for-credit class. Meals and gear for outings are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who like bugs, nature and working with kids and families. Must attend in-person orientation and training. Interviews are required.
how_to_apply: Apply online in spring, then go to a group interview. Questions: butterflyhouse@mobot.org.
notes: Spots are limited. Lead MANTIS needs 2 or more years of MANTIS experience.
duration: June to August, at least 30 hours (Lead MANTIS 40 hours)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is provided. Lead MANTIS volunteers get a Friends and Family membership.

who_can_apply: St. Louis region youth ages 16 to 20.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the program page for future seasons.
notes: The page says it is mainly an education program and stipend details come at orientation. It serves St. Louis regional youth.
duration: Three programs a year (spring break, summer, fall)
pay_detail: Paid $15.00 per hour as a stipend. Bus passes, snacks and lunch provided.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 14 to 18. You must send a letter of recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the spring window. Upload a letter of recommendation. Spots are few. If you have a question, send an email to SageServiceProgram@mobot.org.
notes: Shifts run seven days a week, 10 a.m. to noon and 12:30 to 2:30 p.m. Not everyone who applies gets a spot.
duration: June to October. First year: at least 50 hours including training.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in the 16 county St. Louis area and like plant science, gardening, botany or nature studies. You must come to monthly meetings.
how_to_apply: See the program page for the application.
notes: The page lists acceptance notices by September 16, 2024, so its dates are old. Confirm details before you apply.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Stipend paid at the end of the program. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12 who live or go to school in St. Louis City.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the council page.
notes: Accepted teens serve at least one year. Meetings are virtual.
duration: At least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: High school and college students who are at least 16 when they submit the application. A student who turns 16 during the summer must wait for the next summer.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page early next year. The link was open for only 48 hours in 2026. You must attend the mandatory orientation and finish the screening.
notes: In 2026 the program ran June 8 to August 14, Monday through Friday. Screening has a urine drug screen, a background check (Social Security number needed), and blood tests for TB, measles, mumps and rubella. You also need proof of a flu shot or agree to get one. Call 314-542-4768 with questions.
duration: 10 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week (34 hours or more)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Current 9th and 10th graders from the St. Louis region (they join as rising 10th and 11th graders). A cohort of 20. Needs two teacher recommendations.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form from December to February. Send 2 teacher recommendations. Give clear answers to every question.
notes: The week of training has an overnight stay at the Dana Brown Overnight Center. Only full applications are looked at.
duration: 11 months (training week in early June, then field programs through April)
pay_detail: Stipend based on the number of hours you work at SIFT events. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Live in the City of St. Louis, age 16 to 24, and household income under $69,090 and/or live in a Qualified Census Tract. Under 17 needs a parent or guardian signature on the Eligibility Form.
how_to_apply: The program is closed because it reached capacity. Watch the SLATE program page and its Facebook page for updates. When it opens, you need proof of age, St. Louis residency and household income.
notes: SLATE is seeking more funding. Missouri work permit rules not checked.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering grade 11 or 12 with a 3.0 GPA, parent and high school permission, the course prerequisites and an open seat. Up to 11 credit hours a semester.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Visiting Young Scholar application online. Questions: vys@slu.edu or 314-977-3534.
notes: Your high school decides if the credit counts toward graduation. SLU is a Catholic Jesuit college.
duration: Fall, spring or summer semesters
pay_detail: $350 per credit hour. Lab fees extra. No scholarships or tuition help.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 17 when they apply and in the spring of their junior year. Students must go to a one-hour information meeting and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Check the program page this fall for the new timeline. You need an application, an interview, health requirements, a background check and two references.
notes: Spots are limited. The hospital takes one student per school and at most four students at a time during the school day.
duration: One year, at least one weekday evening shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Anyone who is at least 12 years old can volunteer with the library district.
how_to_apply: Call 636-441-2300, extension 1579, to ask how to start. The program page links only an adult application. Teen Leadership Committee meetings are on the library events calendar.
notes: You can volunteer at your local branch. You can also volunteer with the Library Foundation or the Friends of the Library.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens who attend committee meetings can get an hour of volunteer credit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and 15 who live in St. Louis City or North St. Louis County.
how_to_apply: Apply online at stlyouthjobs.org/apply. A Job Coach then contacts you.
notes: Not a job placement.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Stipend paid after you finish the program. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at a St. Louis area school with a 2.5 or higher GPA. You must be in or past Algebra. You need a transcript, a behavior report and a teacher or counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the UMSL Bridge page when it opens. Send a transcript, behavior report and recommendation form.
notes: Check the UMSL Bridge page for the next application date.
duration: First two Saturdays of each month, October to February, 7:45 a.m. to 12 p.m.
pay_detail: UMSL's landing page calls its Bridge services free. No pay.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 10 at a St. Louis area school with a 2.5 or higher GPA. You must be in or past Algebra. You need a transcript, a behavior report and a teacher or counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the UMSL Bridge page when it is taking students. Send a transcript, behavior report and recommendation form.
notes: The landing page says grades 6 to 10 across middle and high school sessions; the high school page says grades 9 to 10.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July, Monday to Friday 7:45 a.m. to 12 p.m. (2026 high school session began June 22)
pay_detail: UMSL's landing page calls its Bridge services free. No pay.

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now. You can be a freshman, sophomore or junior.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the program page. Questions: precollege@wustl.edu.
notes: Costs and dates were not on the program page. Check the Fees and Scholarships and Dates and Deadlines pages.
duration: Summer program (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $985 commuter or $1,485 residential, plus a $50 nonrefundable application fee. Need-based scholarships offered.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the program page. Questions: precollege@wustl.edu.
notes: Costs and dates were not on the program page. Check the Fees and Scholarships and Dates and Deadlines pages.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $4,075 for 3 credits online or commuter, $7,825 for 6 credits commuter, $8,385 to $12,135 residential, plus a $50 application fee. Need-based scholarships offered.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors (finished 11th grade) from any high school in Missouri or Illinois in the Greater St. Louis area. You do not need research experience. Missouri and Illinois residents only.
how_to_apply: Online application with five short answers and two essays. Two recommendation letters, one from a math or science teacher.
notes: Takes only 10 to 12 students a year. Students from St. Louis Public Schools and under-resourced schools are strongly encouraged to apply. Work is in person in the lab.
duration: 8 weeks (May 31 to July 23, 2027)
pay_detail: $4,800 stipend (before taxes) for the summer

who_can_apply: High school age students who are 15 by May 1 of the application year. Limited spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Ask a teacher or youth leader to send a recommendation form. Go to 1 group interview. If accepted, do a background check and online training.
notes: Next cycle dates follow last year's pattern. Email zooalive@stlzoo.org with questions.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. Must be 15 by the volunteer orientation date (May 9 in 2026). Orientation and training are required.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in February 2027 for the form and interviews.
notes: 2026 orientation was May 9 and training May 16.
duration: Late May to early August, at least 30 hours, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts as service hours.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 for 2026-27 who attend a high school inside the City of Stonecrest. A parent or guardian must register you and send one proof of school enrollment. You must commit to regular attendance.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian fills out the Stonecrest NextGen Program Application Form on the page and sends proof of enrollment. Spots are first-come, first-served.
notes: Only 30 spots. City Hall: 3120 Stonecrest Boulevard, Suite 190, Stonecrest, GA 30038, 770-224-0200. Write to Nicholas Ivey at nivey@stonecrestga.gov. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: 6 Saturday sessions, 10 am to 1 pm, Oct 2026 to Mar 2027
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Durham County students who attend Durham Public Schools. Priority goes to students who would be the first in their family to graduate college (parents have not earned a Bachelor's degree) and/or qualify for free or reduced lunch. Students should be at or slightly below grade level and have strong family support. Rising 6th through 11th graders can apply. A lottery picks 60 to 65 students.
how_to_apply: Print the form for your grade, add the latest report card, End of Grade scores, a teacher recommendation and family questions, and drop it at the W.G. Pearson Center, 1200 Spaulding Street, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 6 PM. Chosen by lottery.
notes: Only 60 to 65 students are picked. A lottery picks them. The page does not state the cost to families. You can contact Karla Fernandez, Director of Operations. Her email is karla.fernandez@studentudurham.org.
duration: Multi-year
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at a participating Georgia high school or approved home study program. 11th and 12th graders and returning 10th graders can take any approved course. New 10th graders take career courses, or core courses with the required SAT or ACT score. 9th graders can join but get no state funding.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school and parent or guardian, apply to the college, and apply for dual enrollment funding at GAfutures.org. Atlanta Tech asks for PSAT, SAT, ACT or Accuplacer scores (a 2.6 HOPE GPA can be used for 11th and 12th graders).
notes: Atlanta Tech funding rules on its page: 15 funded hours per semester, a 30 hour total, and funding ends after two course withdrawals. Atlanta Tech high school contact: hsadmissions@atlantatech.edu or 404-225-4511. This is a course program, not a job, so no work permit applies. The TCSG page sends students to GAfutures.org. The GAfutures Dual Enrollment Application Procedure page says students must apply to the college first, then complete the online Dual Enrollment Funding application; its Apply Now button opens secure.gafutures.org, which shows a GAfutures sign-in page first.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
pay_detail: No tuition, fees or books for the first 30 hours for eligible students. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: High school 4-H members who are project finalists, state winners or All Stars. You sign up through a county Extension office.
how_to_apply: Register through your county Extension office. Students and a parent or guardian must sign Form 600A before attending.
notes: Level I is 9th and 10th grade. Level II is 11th and 12th grade. Council officer candidates must already be in the Tennessee 4-H Honor Club.
duration: About 4 days
pay_detail: $75 for state finalists. $325 for All Stars attending as non-finalists. State Council members and volunteer leaders attend on scholarship.

who_can_apply: Any Tennessee youth. The state site does not list ages or grades for joining. Ask your county Extension office. Some camps and events are set by grade.
how_to_apply: Call or visit your county Extension office. State office phone: 865-974-2128.
notes: The state site names these ways to lead: State 4-H Council, Honor Club, All Stars and the Southern Region Teen Leadership Conference. Camps for older teens are set by grade, so ask the county office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the state site. Camps and events list their own fees or say to ask the county office.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12, and college students, who are in a farm and food class at their school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or your ag teacher. Sign up for a farm and food class.
notes: If your school has no agricultural education program, the state office says to contact them. Camp Clements is the state FFA leadership camp. Association phone: 615-762-4930.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues not stated on the state site.

who_can_apply: High school students tied to FFA who are nominated by their teachers. Up to 4 students per FFA chapter. You can attend only one year.
how_to_apply: Your ag teacher gathers the 2-page application and the fee check. The teacher mails them to the camp director. Her name is Caley Peyton. The address is Tennessee Forestry Association, 2605 Elm Hill Pike, Suite G, Nashville, TN 37214.
notes: Camp has run since 1950 at Piney Creek Camp. Contact cpeyton@tnforestry.com or 615-281-0714.
duration: 6 days (May 31 to June 5 in 2026)
pay_detail: $95 for early registration, $120 after May 8 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Student leaders in Tennessee. The 2027 page does not list grades. Ask your county Farm Bureau office about sponsorship and grade rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the Tennessee Farm Bureau summit page for the application. Call 931-388-7872 with questions.
notes: Check with your county Farm Bureau, since the application is still marked coming soon.
duration: 5 days (May 31 to June 4, 2027)
pay_detail: $200. Covers class materials, meals Monday through the Friday banquet, dorm housing, transport to activities and trained counselors.

who_can_apply: Youth who face barriers to work or school. In-school youth are ages 14 to 21, attending school and low-income. Out-of-school youth are ages 16 to 24, not in school, and must meet at least one barrier such as being homeless, in foster care, or having a disability.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Essentials office in your county. Davidson is 615-253-8920. Rutherford is 615-898-8081. Williamson is 615-370-6004.
notes: Other Tennessee regions have different provider offices, listed on the same page. Teens must qualify under the rules above. Call first to ask if you are eligible.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Exact grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: The page says to contact Senior Program Director Stella London at slondon@ymcamidtn.org to start a team at your school. It does not say how single students sign up.
notes: Over 80 students serve as elected officers. Ask the YMCA about cost and if a student without a school team can join.
duration: High school: 3-day conferences. Middle school: 1-day conferences.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed on the page

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Delegations are started at a school. Exact grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: The page says to contact Senior Program Director Stella London to start or join a team at your school. Her email is slondon@ymcamidtn.org.
notes: The YMCA also runs Model United Nations through the same center. Ask about cost and sign-up before you plan.
duration: High school conferences are 4 days. Middle school conferences are 1 day.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed on the page

who_can_apply: Teens who are in high school or about to start, and at least 14 as of May 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link is posted. You must finish every step. These are a required Challenge Day, a required volunteer tree planting and an interview.
notes: Competitive. Not everyone who applies gets a job. Returning members can apply for outside study spots with partner groups. 2026 dates are shown. Watch the page for the 2027 schedule. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit (employment certificate) is required for minors under 16, so 14 and 15 year olds need one. A school issuing officer or the county school superintendent gives it.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 12:30 pm
pay_detail: Starting at $12 per hour

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors who live in the City of Tucker.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the city's Youth Council page. Members may reapply at the end of their term.
notes: The page lists no direct phone or email; it links to the city's Contacting the City page. The page does not post the next application date. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: One-year term. Meetings on the third Wednesday, September to April.
pay_detail: Unpaid civic role

who_can_apply: Students who finished 9th or 10th grade. You should be truly curious about farming, food, nature science, math and tech.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add your unofficial transcript and two short essays. Add a recommendation form from one or two teachers or counselors.
notes: Questions: agriquest@uga.edu. Cancel 6 or more weeks ahead for a refund minus $50.
duration: 7 days
pay_detail: $300 covers housing, meals, instruction, field trip transport and activities. Full scholarships for accepted students with financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished sophomore year and are 16 by the program start date. You must have taken one high school lab science course and one semester of algebra. You should be interested in ag, food and environmental science. First time participants only.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with short essays. Pick a campus (Athens, Griffin or Tifton). Add two recommendation letters from science or math teachers. Upload an official transcript.
notes: Not residential. You must arrange your own housing and transport, and travel to the campus daily. Contacts on the page: Athens 706-542-2713, Griffin 770-228-7264, Tifton 229-326-4663. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This program requires age 16.
duration: Five weeks (June 1 to July 7 on the page, plus a three day conference July 8 to 10). The page does not show the year.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship, 30 hours a week. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students from across Georgia who are going into their senior year. No other rules are listed on the pages. In 2026 exactly 50 students were chosen from 664 applications.
how_to_apply: Apply through the UGA Admissions application portal when it opens. Ask the Office of Academic and Community Engagement (oace@uga.edu) about future cycles. Admissions phone on the application page: 762-400-8800.
notes: Very competitive: a UGA news story dated Sep 3, 2026 says the program got a record 664 applications for 50 spots. Exact 2026 dates and application requirements were not on the pages the reader could open. The ACE page says there is no cost to attend and describes residence hall living and dining, but does not explicitly say housing and meals are covered.
duration: One week, residential
pay_detail: Free to attend. The pages say there is no cost and that housing and meals are included.

who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 4 weeks (Jul 7 to Jul 31 in 2026), commuters only
pay_detail: No cost to students selected (stated on the page). No stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th grade through graduating 12th grade. The page does not state a minimum age or a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and choose a campus or online. Then apply online. You need a transcript, a health insurance card and a card to pay the application fee and deposit. There are no essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 3 weeks (Jul 13 to Jul 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 package fee: $1,791 campus option or $1,420 online option (3 credits, tuition and fees). Also a $75 application fee and a $275 program deposit that is credited to the bill. Partial scholarships, none above 30% of the package fee.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.
duration: 1 week. 2027 weeks: June 14-18, June 21-25, June 28-July 2, July 12-16. Commuter only, no residential option.
pay_detail: $625 per student per week (includes a $50 non-refundable registration and placement fee); some tracks may add a $25 activity fee; lunch and snacks included. Need-based aid for permanent NC residents who are rising seniors.

who_can_apply: Honor roll students who have finished their junior year. International high school students cannot be considered. If you are under 17, you must say you will live with a parent or legal guardian during Summer School.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the Summer Visitor application. Send a transcript. Send a personal statement that names the course. Also send a letter of support from a teacher, principal or counselor.
notes: You can only take courses in Summer Session 2. High school seniors cannot audit courses. The 2027 application is not open yet, so no dates exist to confirm.
duration: Summer Session 2
pay_detail: Summer School tuition applies. Amount is not on this page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 11 to August 7), residential
pay_detail: The FAQ says the maximum aid package covers full tuition and fees for Virginia residents, which is $7,097 for 2026. The cost for other students and the full breakdown were not read. Small number of need-based aid packages.

who_can_apply: High school youth ages 14 to 18. Students must attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian and an all-day orientation on the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Submit the online interest form, attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian, then interview if selected. Two references must complete the online reference form before the interview.
notes: The page mentions a lottery. Cost and immunization rules for juniors were not stated on that page; UVA Health's general volunteer page lists a health assessment, vaccination requirements, background check and training for volunteers. Questions: 434-924-5251.
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 8 to July 31); at least 50 hours, or one full weekday, with at least 6 weeks of service

who_can_apply: 4-H participants are youth ages 5 to 19. Community 4-H clubs are for ages 9 through 18. You join by contacting your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office and ask about the 4-H program.
notes: The page also lists a 4-H State Congress, camps, maker education, shooting education and youth leadership opportunities. Details such as dates and fees for those were not on the page.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You and your parents must live in Virginia. Home-schooled boys can apply if they meet the home school rules on the site. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Your high school counselor suggests candidates. Local American Legion post members interview them. Find your district chairperson on the Apply page. Ask about how your district does it.
notes: Delegates stay in university dorms. A delegate who turns 18 before the last day must pass a background check. It costs about $16, and the program refunds it. Two delegates go to Boys Nation in Washington, DC. The site lists a 2027 page, but no 2027 dates were found on the pages. The apply page lists the fee as a $600.00 application fee per delegate. It says individual or parental sponsorships are not permitted. Registrar: registrar@vaboysstate.org.
duration: One week (the 2026 session ran June 21 to 27, 2026)
pay_detail: Free to the delegate. The $600 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as an American Legion post, business or school group. Parents and students may not pay it.

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. Public, private and home school students can apply. Must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident of the United States (proof is needed).
how_to_apply: Delegates are selected by local American Legion Auxiliary units by interview, whenever possible. If your school has not been contacted, find your district on the map and email your district registrar for help. Online registration opens in spring 2027 for chosen delegates.
notes: The 2027 director listed is Cheryl Shine, director@vagirlsstate.org. Delegates must stay until 3:00 PM Friday to get program credit. The pages do not say the cost, so ask your district registrar.
duration: One week: Sunday June 20 to Friday June 25, 2027
pay_detail: There is a delegate fee, but the amount is not stated on the program page. Fees are paid to the district registrar (the site lists April 15, 2027 for fees to reach registrars). Ask your district registrar about the cost and who may sponsor you.

who_can_apply: Virginia youth who will be 13 or 14 years old on January 13, 2027. You must be in good school standing. Your school must agree to the long absence.
how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the Capitol Classroom Page Programs page. Verify your date of birth. Create an account. Finish every part of the application. Ask your principal, teachers and counselor first, since you will miss school. Questions: HousePageInfo@house.virginia.gov or (804) 698-1502.
notes: The Speaker of the House picks the pages. Pages live in a residential setting with other pages. They have a mandatory evening study hall. Incomplete applications are not considered, so check that your application shows as complete. This is a separate program from the Senate Page Program. The 2028 dates are not posted yet, so the dates shown are from the 2027 session.
duration: The 2027 session. The page says 7 weeks in odd-numbered years
pay_detail: A paid position of about 40 hours a week. The program FAQ says pages get a weekly session expense payment (no taxes withheld) and a regular wage paid every two weeks (taxes withheld). Dollar amounts are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents who are 13 or 14 on the first day of session (the second Wednesday in January), with no exceptions. You live with a parent or guardian. You go to an accredited school or a qualifying home school. You should have an A or B average.
how_to_apply: Use the Application for Admission page of the Prospective Senate Page Portal during the open window. Questions: pageinfo@senate.virginia.gov or (804) 698-7410.
notes: Pages stay at a designated hotel Sunday night to Friday noon each week, and the hotel room is billed to the Senate Clerk's Office. Admission counts as an excused school absence. Cell phones are turned in during work hours. Rates are listed as subject to change. The overview page lists a $50 activity fee in recent years and does not list uniform or binder costs.
duration: The whole legislative session: 46 calendar days in odd-numbered years and 60 calendar days (nine total weeks) in even-numbered years
pay_detail: $340 a week before taxes plus a $225 a week non-taxed expense deposit (per diem). Rates can change. Families pay about $50 for an activity fee, uniform clothes and a binder, and get the student to Richmond.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 through 17. You must be at least 14 by June 1, 2027, must not turn 18 before the session ends, and must still be in high school the fall after the program. You need your own email, bank account and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Crew Member application on the page. Two professional or academic references must turn in their forms by the deadline. Chosen applicants join a group interview. They also go through a background check.
notes: Competitive. The page says it gets many more applications than spots. About ten crew members live at each host park with three to four adult crew leaders. Crews are split into male and female groups. Cell phones, laptops and other devices are not allowed during the program. Contact: vspycc@dcr.virginia.gov. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before working. Its page does not mention this program. Ask the program if one is needed.
duration: Two weeks. 2027 sessions: June 20 to July 3, or July 11 to 24
pay_detail: $750 stipend after you finish the two-week program. You may also get community service hours.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens).
how_to_apply: Use the unit locator to find a cadet or composite squadron. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Or apply online if your squadron says you can.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Virginia Wing HQ: 7401 Airfield Drive, Richmond, VA 23237, 804-454-7356. The wing site lists squadrons in Blacksburg, Charlottesville, Herndon, Springfield, Richmond and other towns.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students. Applicants must apply by the posted deadline, attend a short interview and orientation, and commit to at least 25 service hours.
how_to_apply: Apply by the posted deadline, then interview and attend orientation. Contact Anna Deater-Deckard, anna@vadm.org, 434-977-1025 x104.
notes: The museum is a small children's museum for infants to age 8, so the work is with young kids. Weekday and Saturday shifts are available.
duration: June to August; at least 25 service hours. Gallery shifts of 2-4 hours, 1-3 times a week; camp assistants commit to a full camp week (Mon-Fri, 8:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m.)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Interns get high school service credit, a letter of recommendation, training, free parking and museum passes to share.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents ages 13 to 16 on the first day of camp. You like nature, have good grades and have not been before. An adult who is not family must nominate you.
how_to_apply: Student fills in the first three sections of the application and nomination form. The nominating adult (teacher, forester, youth leader) fills in the fourth. Submit both together by mail, email or fax.
notes: Camp has run for more than 70 years. It was formerly called Holiday Lake Forestry Camp. Scholarships come from forest industry and conservation sponsors.
duration: 5 days (June 15 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: Selected students get a $300 scholarship and pay a $95 registration fee.

who_can_apply: High school students on a team of five with one adult coach or chaperone. The page says high school students but gives no grade range.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Soil and Water Conservation District. If you do not know it, email byron.minson@vaswcd.org.
notes: Exact 2027 dates were not posted on the program page. Check the Current Competition page on the same site.
duration: Spring contests
pay_detail: No fee is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors from Virginia public, private and home schools. Selection is by your school or county, not by Virginia Tech.
how_to_apply: Start with your school counselor. Or ask the gifted and talented lead. The Virginia Department of Education handles applications. They go through your school or county.
notes: Contact Dr. Brett Milliken, agschool@vt.edu, 540-231-6836 for cost and deadlines. Classes run 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with evening and weekend activities.
duration: 3 weeks (June 20 to July 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders) enrolled in Virginia high schools who are interested in health careers. 20 students took part in 2026.
how_to_apply: The application starts at the local school district level. Forms are on the Virginia Department of Education Summer Residential Governor's School page. You can also email MHSgovschool@radford.edu.
notes: Held in Roanoke, not in Blacksburg. Email MHSgovschool@radford.edu. The Virginia Department of Education page blocked our reader, so check it for current dates.
duration: About 3 weeks, late June to early July in 2026
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders) enrolled in Virginia high schools. Starts at your local school district.
how_to_apply: The application starts at the local school district level. Application forms and guides are on the Virginia Department of Education Summer Residential Governor's School page. Admitted students register on SchoolDoc.
notes: Email rugovschool@radford.edu. The Virginia Department of Education page blocked our reader, so check it for current dates and forms.
duration: Summer residential session (dates not stated on the program pages)
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 18 who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. You must be able to commute to and from the work site daily. Transportation to the site is not available.
how_to_apply: Download the YCC application form (DI-4014) from the park page and send it in. Questions go to nathaniel_phelps@nps.gov.
notes: The park is a drive from Charlottesville. Teens must arrange their own ride every day. Work permit rules for Virginia were not checked.
duration: About 8 weeks (2026 season June 15 to August 6)
pay_detail: $15.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Open to rising high school juniors and seniors. The pages do not state a Virginia residency rule for this program (WEE VT has one).
how_to_apply: Send the joint application with WEE VT and UPWARDS. Rank your choices. Write short essays of 120 words each. Add a grade transcript and a parent financial statement for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jun 28 to Jul 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students in the grade band for each camp. No GPA or residency rule appears on the pages.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp application link on the College of Science camps page; apply for a scholarship inside the form. Cancellation refund minus a $30 fee until 4 weeks before camp.
notes: Explore Science rising 9-10 camp was listed as full in 2026. Questions: explorescicamp@vt.edu. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 5 days (Sunday to Thursday)
pay_detail: 2026 price $1,150 per residential camp ($700 for the day camp for rising 7th-8th). Camp fees cover instruction, supplies, room and board; need-based scholarships are available in the application.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at the listed high schools. They are Floyd, Franklin County, Giles, Narrows, Bassett, Magna Vista, E.C. Glass, Heritage, Martinsville, Pulaski, Salem, William Fleming and Patrick Henry. When first picked, you must be 13 to 19. You must have low income, be first in your family to go to college, or be at risk in school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form that matches your school (Roanoke City, Salem, or Southwest Virginia list). A Spanish PDF application is also posted.
notes: Only for the listed schools, so Blacksburg and Christiansburg students are not on the list. Ask the TRIO office if your school can be added. Federal income and first-generation rules apply.
duration: School year (weekly tutoring, monthly events) plus up to six weeks in summer
pay_detail: Free. The page says students get paid for participating but does not give an amount.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are Virginia residents.
how_to_apply: Joint application with the C-Tech2 and UPWARDS summer programs: rank your choices, add short essays (120 words each) and a grade transcript, and a parent completes a financial statement used for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: The program page as fetched on 2026-10-10 does not state the $2,500 cost or any amount; confirm the cost on the apply page before quoting it. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jul 12 to Jul 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Virginia high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16, Virginia residents, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents. A 2.7 GPA is required. You also need a teacher recommendation and a school counselor letter. NASA security rules usually allow only citizens and permanent residents at the summer academy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then ask a teacher and a school counselor to send their letters through the online system. They get an email from notices@spacegrant.net. Letters sent any other way are not accepted. Contact: Regina Delzer, rdelzer@odu.edu.
notes: Closing soon. Statewide for Virginia, so it may also appear on another Virginia list. The page says 180 top scholars who finish the course attend the summer academy. The application link is on the page.
duration: Six online modules from late November, then a 6 day summer academy for selected scholars
pay_detail: Free. Scholars picked for the summer academy get transportation, housing and meals.

who_can_apply: Virginia students now in grades 9 to 12. Your local district sends the application on. The state group makes the final picks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the camper application and give it to your local Soil and Water Conservation District. Ask them about scholarships.
notes: Questions: byron.minson@vaswcd.org. If you are 13 to 16, see Camp Woods and Wildlife from the Virginia Department of Forestry.
duration: 1 week (July 12 to 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Camp fee not listed on the state page. Local districts may give scholarships, so ask yours.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors with a 2.8 or higher unweighted GPA, or test scores showing college readiness. The career path also accepts a principal recommendation in place of the GPA. You must keep a 2.0 college GPA after two courses.
how_to_apply: Use the New CCP Students page and the Advising and Registration page on the Wake Tech CCP site. Or email CCP staff with questions.
notes: Only one application per student. Use a personal email address. Wake County Public School students name their principal or a stand-in on the application.
duration: Semester by semester
pay_detail: Tuition-free

who_can_apply: Wake County high school juniors or seniors who are allowed to work in the U.S. You must have applied for Career and College Promise at Wake Tech. The path is Electrical Systems Technology.
how_to_apply: Talk with the career coordinator at your school. Or talk with Career and Technical Education staff. You can also email Todd Campbell. He runs the Wake Tech Electrification Training Project.
notes: You need your own transportation to Wake Tech and to the employer, though help may be available. Attend at least 90% of sessions. The 2026 page listed juniors and seniors expected to graduate in 2026 or 2027.
duration: 6 weeks, 8am to 5pm Monday to Wednesday, employer days Thursday and Friday
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend and 6 hours of college credit. Tools and materials provided.

who_can_apply: Juniors in Wake County Public School System high schools. Talk to your career development coordinator or CTE teacher.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Wake Tech page for the apprenticeship academy. You can also ask for help from the career coordinator at your school.
notes: Paths are building trades (carpentry, electrical, HVAC, plumbing, welding), car and truck tech, and mechanical engineering and advanced making. The page gives no year with the October 16 date. It follows the Spring 2027 wording. The page says Career and College Promise helps cover tuition. It does not say tuition is fully paid. The page says the academy will serve 250 students over three years, but no next round is posted, so the date shown is from the Spring 2027 round.
duration: Starts Spring 2027; about two years including paid apprenticeship
pay_detail: First year: monthly stipend, plus help with books, supplies and transportation. Second year: paid apprentice. Career and College Promise helps cover tuition.

who_can_apply: High school students age 16 or older (the page covers ages 16 through the summer after graduation). Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN and Occupational Health clearance. Apply to only one location: Raleigh Campus or Cary Hospital.
how_to_apply: Review the current junior-eligible openings, then submit the online application for one campus during an open window. Selected students interview, give two references, finish medical screenings and attend orientation.
notes: Not first come, first served. Processing takes about 3 to 5 weeks. Required Occupational Health clearance includes flu, MMR, Varicella, Tdap and TB. Not for court-ordered community service. The page describes volunteer service, not an internship or job shadowing. The check dates are a schedule the page gives, not a promise that applications will open on those days.
duration: Minimum 6 months, one day a week on a regular set day and time

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 who are interested in a health care career. Spots are limited and competitive.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send shot records (MMR, DPT, Varicella). Have your school counselor fill out and sign the School Records Release. You can email, fax or mail documents to Volunteer Services. If you are picked, there is a short 15-minute interview.
notes: Volunteer Services: 3950 Austell Rd, Austell, GA 30106, (470) 732-3767. Picks use a finished application and the required documents. They also look at time commitment, past volunteering, GPA and leadership. They look at speaking skills and interest in health care too. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: June 4 to July 29 in 2026, one 4-hour shift a week plus a 2-hour orientation
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role (16 service hours validated)

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Picks are based on the full application. They also look at whether you can keep the time commitment. They look at past volunteering, GPA, leadership, speaking skills and interest in health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window. Email your shot record as a PDF. It needs 2 MMR, 2 Varicella or proof of the illness, and 1 Tdap. Your school counselor fills out and signs the recommendation form and emails it. The interview is in March and the orientation is in April. After you are accepted, you get TB test steps.
notes: Accepted students may keep volunteering in the school year if Volunteer Services says yes. It is competitive. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit.
duration: 8-week summer session in June and July, one 2-hour shift a week for 6 of the 8 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page mentions no fees.

who_can_apply: High school students aged 16 to 18. You need shot records, a school counselor form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen application. Email your shot record (2 MMR, 2 chickenpox or proof you had it, 1 Tdap) as a PDF. Have your school counselor sign the recommendation form and email it. Then you are called for an interview.
notes: Spots are limited. Not everyone is accepted. Picks look at past service, GPA, leadership and interest in health careers. Students accepted for summer may keep volunteering in the school year with approval.
duration: Summer session in June and July: one two-hour shift per week for six of the eight weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: City of Atlanta residents ages 16 to 24 who are WIOA eligible. In-school youth are generally 16 to 21, must meet income and other criteria, and may have a barrier such as disability, English learner, foster care, homeless, justice-involved or parenting. A WorkSource Atlanta Eligibility Specialist makes the final decision.
how_to_apply: 1) Finish the online youth orientation. 2) Create a profile in the WorkSource Georgia portal and save your SID number. 3) Upload your documents. 4) Book an eligibility appointment, or email WSAYouth@AtlantaGa.Gov with subject Ready to RISE. 5) Take the My Next Move career assessment. 6) Eligibility review.
notes: Eligibility is income and barrier based, so not every teen qualifies. The document list includes a Social Security card and proof of address; this is the official city workforce board, but upload documents only through the portal named on the page. Under 18 using parent documents: proof of relationship and shared address is needed. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: Year-round, no set end date
pay_detail: Paid work experience and internships are one service. Wage not posted on the page. Services are no cost.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 24 who face barriers to work. The page does not define barriers.
how_to_apply: Apply online at ATLworks.org. Send everything it asks for. An eligibility specialist reviews it and replies within 7 business days. Then you meet the specialist and make a career plan.
notes: The page does not mention work permits. Contact 404-371-2000 (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm) or 311CCC@dekalbcountyga.gov.
duration: Paid work experience up to 14 weeks
pay_detail: $13 per hour for paid work experience, up to 14 weeks. Up to $250 more in milestone rewards. Free to join.

who_can_apply: Fulton County residents ages 16 to 24 who are interested in employment or training and meet low-income guidelines and/or have significant barriers to education or employment.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Visit the youth center at 4405 Mall Blvd., Suite 400, Union City, GA 30291, or call a career center: South Fulton 404-613-6800 (5710 Stonewall Tell Rd., Suite 160, College Park) or North Fulton 404-613-4480 (7741 Roswell Rd., Suite 205, Sandy Springs).
notes: A March 2026 county news release says WorkSource Fulton also offers the Career Compass Academy, a five-week paid virtual work readiness program for ages 14 to 24 that is income based. Teens signed up at the county's Summer Teen Hiring Fair on April 11, 2026; next year's dates are not posted. If you live inside the City of Atlanta, also look at Youth R.I.S.E. and ask which office serves your address. The county's older Summer Youth Job Training and Summer Youth Internship pages return errors now.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Leaders Club requires being a Y program member or facility member; the page states no membership rule for Changemakers. A Jr. Leaders Club exists for grades 6 to 8.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the teen community page. Changemakers uses the Teen Clubs sign-up. Or ask at a local YMCA branch.
notes: Leaders Club can include travel to conferences and leadership events. The page does not say how many community service hours a club gives. Which branch runs a club and when is not stated, so ask your local Y. The Y's teens page lists a Legacy Leaders college scholarship for active teen members, with a last day to apply of Sunday, September 13 (year not stated).
duration: Leaders Club meets weekly. Changemakers meeting schedule and season length not stated.
pay_detail: Clubs are free for teens who are Y members. Financial help is available. The page does not give membership prices.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. The Chapel Hill-Carrboro YMCA page links a nomination form, an application and a handbook. The page does not say which listed branches are in Raleigh or Durham.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the page, attend an interest meeting, or contact your branch's Teen Director.
notes: Branches listed: A.E. Finley, Alexander Family, Chapel Hill-Carrboro, East Triangle, Kerr Family, Kraft Family, Northwest Cary, Poole Family and Taylor Family YMCAs. The page does not explain the difference between Member and Participant dues.
duration: Early fall to the end of the school year
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $240 per year (Member) or $301 per year (Participant); club dues only, not annual events

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Locations are shared directly with participants.
how_to_apply: Register through the program's online registration page. Questions: yo.sobha@ymcatriangle.org.
notes: Achievers may earn certified community service hours and may receive partial scholarships as seniors. The page does not say which cities host groups.
duration: Biweekly summits, mostly Saturdays 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. (some on other weekdays), September 2026 to May 2027
pay_detail: $217 per year (Members) or $228 per year (Participants). Financial assistance is available through a separate form.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 17 years old by June 1, 2027 who are enrolled in high school (or equivalent) for the coming school year.
how_to_apply: Online application plus an essay of 2 pages or less written by the teen alone (AI-looking essays are rejected), and one recommendation from a non-family adult. Selected teens interview in person in March and attend orientation with a parent in April.
notes: Staff review in February, notification of next steps by March 1. A current TB test is needed each year by June 1. Shifts are A.M., P.M. or full day. The page does not print a year beside Jan 1 and Jan 31; the year is read from the 2027 program-year details.
duration: June 1 to May 31. At least 160 hours total: 100 in summer, 30 in fall, 30 in spring. Required training week June 7 to 11, 2027.
pay_detail: Unpaid. $30 orientation fee covers name badge, uniform shirt and access card. Scholarships available for qualified applicants.
